2. AI Studio creates a new project within the same sub-account.
3. The system opens the newly created project.
4. AI Studio starts the conversion through the project's chat.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083386018/original/86FIjx6TY9jiUfocguDTeTXvkOhYwK-tvQ.png?1792056199)

**Step 6: Monitor the Migration**

1. Follow progress in the migrated project's chat.
2. Check the dashboard for the **Migrating to SSR** status.
3. Use Preview when available to inspect the project.
4. Allow the AI-assisted conversion to finish before attempting to publish or make restricted changes.

The status clears when the project is ready as a TanStack Start application. If the process stops before completion, enter `continue the migration` in the migrated project's chat. Do not restart migration from the original project unless you intentionally want to create another copy.

**Step 7: Review the Completed Project**

After the migration status clears:

1. Open the converted project.
2. Preview its pages and navigation.
3. Review the generated application for missing functionality or unexpected changes.
4. Test the features that required SSR or server-side functionality.
5. Use AI Studio chat or supported editing tools to fix any remaining issues.

```
Important: A completed migration does not guarantee that every part of the application works exactly as before. Review and test the converted project before publishing it.
```

---

## **Review Forms, Calendars, and Workflow Connections**

Migrating a project does not automatically redirect workflow triggers from the original project to the new project. Review existing integrations before switching to the migrated website.

1. Identify the forms and calendars used by the original application.
2. Confirm that the migrated project's forms and calendars work correctly.
3. Review any CRM connections used by those components.
4. Navigate to **Automation > Workflows**.
5. Open workflows associated with the original AI Studio project.
6. Review the trigger filters for project, form, page path, and domain.
7. Update the relevant filters or connections when transitioning to the migrated project.
8. After publishing, submit test entries and verify the expected workflow executions.

Existing project-specific workflow triggers remain associated with the original project until their configurations are updated.

For more information, see [AI Studio Form Submitted Workflow Trigger](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008298).

### **Review Publishing and Domain Connections**

Publishing the migrated project is a separate decision from completing the framework conversion.

Before publishing:

- Confirm that the migrated project is functioning correctly.
- Identify which domain or published URL you want to use.
- Verify all relevant workflows and integrations.
- Review important page titles, metadata, and SEO settings.
- Plan any domain transition separately to avoid disrupting your existing live website.

Your original website and connected domains remain unchanged until you make separate publishing or domain configuration changes.

For additional guidance, see [AI Studio in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007587).

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Should I migrate my React project just because TanStack Start is available?**

No. Migration is optional. If your existing React project meets your requirements and does not need server-side rendering or full-stack functionality, you can continue using it without migrating.

**Q: Can I migrate the same original React project more than once?**

Yes. Starting migration again from the original project creates another separate copy. If you are trying to finish an incomplete conversion, resume the existing migrated project instead of creating another copy.

**Q: What if the migrated application looks different from my original website?**

Review the differences in Preview and use AI Studio chat or available editing tools after migration to correct them. The AI-assisted conversion may require additional changes before the new application is ready to publish.

**Q: How can I tell whether my migration is complete?**

The project's **Migrating to SSR** status clears once the converted application becomes a normal TanStack Start project. You should still test the application's behavior before publishing.

**Q: Can I use my existing workflow automations with the migrated project?**

Yes, but project-specific workflow configurations may need to be updated. Review the original project's triggers and filters, configure them for the migrated project where appropriate, and test submissions after publishing.

**Q: Do I need to recreate my API keys and integrations after migration?**

The release does not guarantee that every integration or credential configuration transfers automatically. Review the migrated application's integration requirements and configure any necessary secrets or connections before publishing.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [AI Studio: SSR, Server Functions, REST APIs, and Secrets](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008701-ai-studio-ssr-server-functions-rest-apis-and-secrets)
- [AI Studio in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007587)
- [AI Studio Form Submitted Workflow Trigger](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008298)
- [AI Studio – Pricing](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008322-ai-studio-pricing)
- [Code Editor in AI Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007652-code-editor-in-the-ai-studio)
- [Advanced SEO Support in AI Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007691)

title_en: New MCP connectors
source_md:
AI • Managed Agents • Ask AI

New MCP Connectors

Connect Clay, Lemlist, Airtable, Composio, and Reap to HighLevel AI experiences so agents can securely use third-party tools to enrich data, automate outreach, manage records, access connected apps, and repurpose video.

What You'll Learn

HighLevel's MCP connector catalog now includes five additional apps: **Clay**, **Lemlist**, **Airtable**, **Composio**, and **Reap**. These connectors extend Managed Agents and Ask AI beyond native CRM actions by giving them controlled access to tools available in connected third-party accounts.

This guide explains what each new connector is designed for, how MCP apps work with Managed Agents and Ask AI, how to select the tools an agent can use, and how to test a connector before using it in live automation.

Available Now

Clay, Lemlist, Airtable, Composio, and Reap are now available in the MCP connector catalog. They join the existing and growing collection of third-party integrations available to supported HighLevel AI experiences.

# **What are the New MCP Connectors?**

MCP, or **Model Context Protocol**, provides a standardized way for AI agents to connect to external applications and use the tools those applications expose. In HighLevel, MCP app connectors allow Managed Agents and Ask AI to work with authenticated third-party services without requiring you to manually build every integration.

Once an MCP app is connected, you control which available tools the AI can use. A Managed Agent can then call those tools when its trigger and instructions require them, while Ask AI can use enabled connector tools while responding to your requests.

The latest catalog expansion adds **Clay**, **Lemlist**, **Airtable**, **Composio**, and **Reap**.

## **Key Benefits of MCP Connectors**

MCP connectors extend AI automation beyond HighLevel by letting agents securely access selected capabilities from third-party applications. This makes it possible to build richer automations without creating a separate custom integration for every use case.

- **More External Actions:** Let AI agents work with supported tools in connected third-party apps.
- **Controlled Tool Access:** Choose which tools each connected app makes available to the agent.
- **Secure Connections:** Authenticate through the connector's supported OAuth or secure sign-in flow instead of placing credentials in agent instructions.
- **Multi-App Agents:** Connect multiple MCP apps to a Managed Agent when one workflow needs to work across several systems.
- **Faster Automation:** Add prebuilt app capabilities without manually configuring individual API calls for every operation.
- **Broader AI Workflows:** Combine CRM events, AI reasoning, and external applications in one agent workflow.

## **Five New MCP Connectors**

Each connector expands the types of work an AI agent can perform. Choose the app that matches the external data, outreach, record management, multi-app automation, or content-production task you want the agent to handle.

| Connector | What It Enables | Example Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Clay** | Build and enrich lead lists using company and contact data from 100+ sources, enrichment waterfalls, and outbound preparation tools. | Enrich a newly created lead before routing it to sales. |
| **Lemlist** | Work with cold-outreach activities such as lead discovery, multichannel email and LinkedIn sequences, and campaign management. | Add qualified prospects to the appropriate outbound campaign. |
| **Airtable** | Read, create, and update records across connected Airtable tables and views using the tools made available by the connector. | Create a project record after a customer completes onboarding. |
| **Composio** | Reach 1,000+ tools through one managed gateway that handles supported authentication and gives agents access to connected application actions. | Build an agent that needs to take actions across several external systems. |
| **Reap** | Repurpose long-form video into shorter clips with supported captioning, dubbing, and translation capabilities. | Turn a long recording into short-form assets ready for a content workflow. |

**Important:** Available tools can vary by connector, connected account, third-party permissions, and future connector updates. Review the tool list shown during setup before publishing an agent.

## **How MCP Connectors Work with Managed Agents**

A connector gives the agent access to external tools, but it does not decide when the agent should run or what the agent should do. Managed Agents combine triggers, instructions, apps, capabilities, and optional Knowledge Bases so each part of the configuration has a clear role.

### **Triggers Determine When the Agent Runs**

Triggers start a Managed Agent when the configured event occurs. For example, an agent might run when a contact is created, an opportunity is created, or a lead-generation form is submitted.

### **Apps Define Which External Systems the Agent Can Use**

The **Apps** area contains the MCP connectors assigned to the Managed Agent. A single agent can use more than one connector when its instructions require actions across different external applications.

### **Instructions Tell the Agent What to Do**

Clear instructions define when an external tool should be used, what information should be passed to it, and what outcome the agent should produce. Giving an agent access to a connector does not mean every available tool will be called on every run.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080665834/original/cHjstd7zZKESrYYXP1AKrsCTnOj7w9Ftow.png?1789107309)

**Note:** Screenshots may show existing connectors such as Notion or HubSpot as examples. The same Apps workflow is used to add supported connectors from the current catalog. Tool counts can change as connectors are updated.

## **Using MCP Connectors in Managed Agents vs. Ask AI**

Managed Agents and Ask AI can both use MCP connectors, but they serve different automation patterns. Managed Agents are designed for triggered, autonomous work, while Ask AI uses connected tools in response to a user's request.

| Area | Managed Agents | Ask AI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **How work starts** | Configured trigger or supported agent event | User asks Ask AI to perform a task |
| **Where connectors are configured** | Apps area inside the Managed Agent | Customize → Connectors → Manage Connectors |
| **Typical use** | Repeatable or event-driven automation | Interactive, user-initiated work |
| **Tool control** | Select connector tools available to the agent | Enable the connector and control available tools |

## **How To Setup and Use New MCP Connectors**

Proper setup ensures the AI has access only to the external account and tools required for its task. Connect the app, review its permissions, select the appropriate tools, and test the behavior before relying on the connector in production.

### **Option 1: Connect an MCP App to a Managed Agent**

Managed Agents use MCP apps as part of event-driven automation. The app should be attached to the specific agent that needs its tools so access remains aligned with the agent's purpose.

### **Step 1: Open Managed Agents**

Managed Agents are configured from Agent Studio, where you can define the agent's instructions, triggers, apps, capabilities, Knowledge Bases, testing, and publishing state.

1. Go to **AI Agents → Agent Studio**.
2. Open **Managed Agents**.
3. Create a new Managed Agent or open an existing agent.

### **Step 2: Add an MCP App**

The Apps area determines which external connectors are available to the agent. Only add connectors that are relevant to the automation the agent is expected to perform.

1. Locate the **Apps** area.
2. Click **Add app**.
3. Browse or search the MCP catalog.
4. Select **Clay**, **Lemlist**, **Airtable**, **Composio**, **Reap**, or another supported connector.

### **Step 3: Connect the External Account**

Authentication allows the connector to act within the permissions granted by the external service. Use the supported OAuth or secure sign-in flow presented by the connector.

1. Select the MCP app.
2. Click the option to connect or add an account.
3. Sign in to the applicable third-party account.
4. Review and authorize the requested access.

### **Step 4: Choose the Tools the Agent Can Use**

Tool selection controls the specific actions exposed to the agent. Limiting access to the tools required for the use case makes the agent's capabilities easier to understand, test, and govern.

1. Review the available tools for the connector.
2. Select the tools the agent needs.
3. Leave unrelated tools disabled when they are not required.
4. Click **Save**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080665931/original/9wjn7Ig_Odkx_N-vCllS9FJeNsCO2sNPqg.png?1789107339)

### **Step 5: Update the Agent Instructions**

The agent needs clear guidance about when and why to use the connector. Good instructions reduce unnecessary tool calls and make the expected outcome easier to test.

Include details such as:

- Which situations require the external app.
- What data the agent should read or send.
- Which actions it is allowed to perform.
- When the agent should ask for clarification.
- What the agent should do when the connector returns an error or no result.

### **Step 6: Configure the Trigger**

Triggers determine when a Managed Agent begins its work. Choose an event that provides the right context for the connected app action.

For example, a lead-enrichment agent could run when a contact is created, while a follow-up agent could run after a form submission or another supported CRM event.

### **Step 7: Test the Agent**

Testing confirms that the correct connector and tool are selected, the external account returns the expected information, and the agent follows the restrictions in its instructions.

1. Click **Test Agent**.
2. Use representative test data.
3. Confirm the correct MCP tool is invoked.
4. Verify the expected result appears in the external app.
5. Refine the instructions or tool permissions if the result is not correct.

### **Step 8: Publish the Managed Agent**

Publishing makes the tested configuration available for live execution. Publish only after confirming the trigger, external account, tool permissions, and agent instructions behave as intended.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080665965/original/qRmPY3BS7TJ83n0fVMVrngKs2qHdqTmW1Q.png?1789107359)

### **Option 2: Connect an MCP App in Ask AI**

Ask AI connectors are designed for user-initiated tasks. Connect the app once, control which tools are enabled, and then ask Ask AI to perform supported work using that connected account.

1. Open **Ask AI**.
2. Go to **Customize → Connectors**.
3. Select **Manage Connectors**.
4. Find the MCP app you want to use.
5. Connect and authenticate the applicable third-party account.
6. Review and enable the tools Ask AI should be allowed to use.
7. Enable the connector.
8. Start a chat and give Ask AI a clear request that requires the connected app.

## **Security and Access Best Practices**

MCP connectors can allow AI to take real actions in external systems, so connector access should match the agent's exact responsibility. Limiting accounts, tools, and instructions reduces unnecessary access and makes production behavior easier to audit.

- **Grant only required access:** Authorize the minimum third-party permissions necessary for the agent's job.
- **Select only required tools:** Avoid enabling every available tool when the agent needs only a small subset.
- **Keep credentials out of prompts:** Use the connector authentication experience rather than placing passwords, API keys, or login details in agent instructions.
- **Write explicit guardrails:** Tell the agent which actions it may perform and which situations require confirmation or escalation.
- **Test with realistic inputs:** Verify read and write actions before exposing the agent to live triggers.
- **Review third-party requirements:** Some apps may require their own account, plan, permissions, or feature access.
- **Recheck tools after connector updates:** Available tool lists can evolve as MCP integrations add or change capabilities.

## **Troubleshooting MCP Connectors**

Most MCP connector issues come from authentication, third-party permissions, tool selection, or unclear agent instructions. Check each layer separately to identify whether the connection, tool, or agent behavior needs to be adjusted.

| Issue | What to Check |
| --- | --- |
| **The app is connected but the agent cannot use it** | Confirm the connector is attached to the correct agent and the required individual tools are enabled. |
| **Authentication fails** | Reconnect the app, verify the third-party account credentials, and confirm the account is allowed to authorize the requested access. |
| **A required tool does not appear** | Review the connector's current tool list and the permissions or plan available in the connected third-party account. |
| **The agent uses the wrong external action** | Reduce unnecessary tool access and make the agent instructions more explicit about when each tool should be used. |
| **The Managed Agent does not run** | Verify that the intended trigger is configured, the agent is published, and your test event matches the trigger conditions. |
| **The connector previously worked but now fails** | Check whether authorization was revoked or expired, then reconnect the third-party account and retest the tool. |
| **Ask AI does not use the connector** | Confirm the connector is enabled, the required tool is allowed, and your request clearly asks for an action that requires the connected app. |

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

Q: Are Clay, Lemlist, Airtable, Composio, and Reap replacing existing MCP connectors?

No. These apps expand the existing MCP connector catalog rather than replacing current connectors.

Q: Can one Managed Agent use more than one MCP connector?

Yes. Multiple MCP apps can be attached when the agent needs to work across several external systems. Keep its instructions clear about when each connector should be used.

Q: Does adding an MCP connector automatically cause the Managed Agent to run?

No. The connector provides external tools. The Managed Agent still needs the appropriate trigger and instructions to determine when it runs and what action it should perform.

Q: Can I control which tools an MCP app exposes to an agent?

Yes. Review the available tool list after connecting the app and enable only the tools required for the agent's use case.

Q: Do I need an account with the third-party app?

Generally, you must authenticate an eligible account with the third-party service. Required plans, permissions, or features can vary by app.

Q: Can Ask AI use these MCP connectors too?

Yes. This release applies to Managed Agents and Ask AI. Ask AI connectors are managed from Customize → Connectors → Manage Connectors.

Q: Are catalog MCP connectors the same as custom MCP connectors?

No. Catalog connectors are prebuilt integrations available from the MCP app catalog. Custom MCP connections are a separate configuration path for connecting other compatible MCP servers.

Q: Why does my connector show a different number of tools than a screenshot?

Tool counts can change as connectors evolve. Use the current tool list displayed in your account as the source of truth for the actions available to your agent.

### **Related Articles**

[MCP Connectors for Managed Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008304-mcp-connectors) [Setup and Use Managed Agents in Agent Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007931-important-update-agent-studio-is-evolving) [Ask AI Skills and Connectors](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008434-ask-ai-skills-and-connectors) [Custom MCP Connectors for Managed Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008353-custom-mcp-connectors-for-superagents-agent-studio) [Managed Agents, Conversation AI & Ask AI: What's the Difference?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008362-super-agents-conversation-ai-ask-ai-what-s-the-difference-) [Skills Platform for AI Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008315)

title_en: Importing Opportunities using a CSV file
source_md:
Opportunity CSV import lets you create new Opportunities or update existing Opportunities in bulk using a CSV file. This is useful when migrating deal data from another system, adding Opportunities to existing contacts, or updating Opportunity information such as Pipeline, Stage, Status, Value, and custom fields.

Every Opportunity must be associated with a contact. If the contacts already exist in HighLevel, you can perform an **Opportunities-only import** using their Contact IDs. If you also need to create or import the contacts, use a **Contacts + Opportunities** import instead.

> **Important:** For an Opportunities-only import, each row must contain a valid **Contact ID**, **Opportunity Name**, and **Pipeline**.

---

## **Key Benefits of Importing Opportunities with a CSV File**

CSV import provides a faster way to create or update multiple Opportunities without editing each record individually. Preparing the data correctly before importing also helps preserve the relationship between contacts, pipelines, stages, and Opportunity information.

- **Bulk Opportunity Creation:** Create multiple Opportunities from one CSV file.
- **Existing Opportunity Updates:** Use Opportunity IDs to update existing records in bulk.
- **Contact Association:** Connect imported Opportunities to the appropriate existing contacts.
- **Pipeline Organization:** Import Opportunities into existing HighLevel pipelines and applicable stages.
- **Custom Data Migration:** Map supported Opportunity custom fields from another CRM or data source.
- **Import Troubleshooting:** Review import results and failed rows through Bulk Actions.

---

## **Before You Import Opportunities**

Preparing your CSV and HighLevel account before starting the import reduces mapping errors and unintended duplicate Opportunities. Confirm that the required CRM records and fields exist before uploading the file.

Before importing:

- Save the file in **CSV format**.
- Keep the CSV file under the currently documented **30 MB** limit.
- Create the HighLevel pipelines you intend to use before importing.
- Create the applicable pipeline stages before importing stage information.
- Create any **Opportunity custom fields** you want to map.
- Confirm that every Opportunity-only row contains a valid **Contact ID**.
- Include **Opportunity ID** when updating an existing Opportunity.
- Review your data for blank or incorrect values.
- Test the process with a small sample file before importing a large dataset.

> **Important:** Completed imports do not have a one-click undo option. Review your mappings and test with a small group of records before running a large import.

### **Prepare Pipeline and Stage Values**

Pipeline information determines where imported Opportunities are organized. Preparing these values in HighLevel before the import helps ensure the Opportunities are assigned to the intended sales process.

The **Pipeline** value in the CSV should correspond to an existing HighLevel pipeline.

If you include Pipeline Stage, make sure the intended stage already exists in the applicable pipeline.

---

## **Opportunity-Only vs Contacts + Opportunities Import**

HighLevel supports importing only Opportunities or importing Contacts and Opportunities together. Choose the method based on whether the contacts associated with the Opportunities already exist in HighLevel.

| Import Type | Use When |
| --- | --- |
| **Opportunities Only** | The contacts already exist in HighLevel and you have their valid Contact IDs. |
| **Contacts + Opportunities** | You need to import or create contacts and associate their Opportunities from the same CSV rows. |

For an **Opportunities-only import**, do not add unnecessary Contact-import requirements such as Name, Email, or Phone formatting when the contact already exists and is being associated through Contact ID.

For a **Contacts + Opportunities** import, the applicable Contact-import requirements also apply because HighLevel is creating or importing the Contact records.

---

## **Required and Optional Opportunity Fields**

The fields included in your CSV determine what information HighLevel can create or update on each Opportunity. Required fields establish the contact relationship and pipeline placement, while optional fields let you migrate additional deal information.

| Field | Requirement | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Contact ID** | Required for Opportunities-only import | Associates the Opportunity with an existing HighLevel contact. |
| **Opportunity Name** | Required | Defines the Opportunity name. |
| **Pipeline** | Required | Assigns the Opportunity to an existing pipeline. |
| **Pipeline Stage** | Recommended when stage placement is needed | Places the Opportunity in the applicable stage of the selected pipeline. |
| **Opportunity ID** | Required when updating an existing Opportunity | Identifies the specific existing Opportunity HighLevel should update. |
| **Opportunity Value** | Optional | Stores the monetary value associated with the Opportunity. |
| **Status** | Optional | Sets the applicable Opportunity status. |
| **Custom Opportunity Fields** | Optional | Imports additional Opportunity-specific information. |

### **Opportunity Status**

HighLevel supports the following Opportunity statuses:

- **Open**
- **Won**
- **Lost**
- **Abandoned**

If your source CRM uses different status names, normalize those values to the applicable HighLevel statuses before importing.

### **Opportunity Custom Fields**

Opportunity custom fields are separate from Contact custom fields. Create the required custom fields for the **Opportunity** object before starting the import.

During field mapping, map each CSV column to the corresponding Opportunity custom field.

---

## **How to Import Opportunities Using a CSV File**

The import workflow lets you choose the record type, upload the CSV, map each column to a HighLevel field, and review import settings before processing the records. Carefully review the mappings before starting because incorrect identifiers or pipeline values can create unintended records.

### **Step 1: Start the Import**

1. Go to **Opportunities** in your HighLevel sub-account.
2. Click the available **Import** option.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081214710/original/zO2v3ZZzdPsIJHRDDmjQmCinbSGnsRov_w.png?1789661464)
3. Choose the applicable import type:

   - **Opportunities**, or
   - **Contacts + Opportunities**, when both record types need to be imported.  
       
      ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081214763/original/iUFMcMb7dXfYR_9sbjZA-zLRCuLzFQl8_w.png?1789661494)

### **Step 2: Upload the CSV File**

1. Select or drag and drop your CSV file into the importer.
2. Confirm that the file uploads successfully.
3. Review any initial file warnings before continuing.

### **Step 3: Choose the Import Behavior**

Select the applicable import behavior based on whether you are creating new records or updating existing records.

When updating existing Opportunities, make sure the CSV includes the correct **Opportunity ID** values.

> **Important:** If you intend to update an existing Opportunity but do not provide the correct Opportunity ID, HighLevel may create another Opportunity instead of updating the intended record.

### **Step 4: Map CSV Columns to HighLevel Fields**

Field mapping tells HighLevel where each CSV column belongs. Verify identifiers and Opportunity fields carefully before proceeding.

Map the required fields:

- **Contact ID**
- **Opportunity Name**
- **Pipeline**

Then map applicable optional fields such as:

- Pipeline Stage
- Opportunity ID
- Opportunity Value
- Status
- Opportunity custom fields

If a CSV column should not be imported, leave it unmapped and confirm **Don't import data for unmapped columns** when prompted.

### 

### **Step 5: Configure Empty-Value Behavior**

When updating existing Opportunities, decide how blank cells in the CSV should affect existing HighLevel data.

Enable **Don't update Empty Values** when blank CSV cells should leave existing Opportunity values unchanged.

For example:

If an existing Opportunity has a value in a custom field but the corresponding CSV cell is blank, enabling this option preserves the existing HighLevel value instead of replacing it with an empty value.

### **Step 6: Review and Start the Import**

### 

Before submitting:

1. Review the mapped fields.
2. Confirm that required fields are mapped.
3. Review any warnings.
4. Confirm your empty-value settings.
5. Verify that unwanted columns are excluded.
6. Start the import.

---

## **How Opportunity Updates Work**

Updating Opportunities requires a reliable way to identify the existing record. Opportunity ID provides that identifier so HighLevel can apply imported values to the intended Opportunity rather than treating the row as a new deal.

### **Creating New Opportunities**

When creating a new Opportunity:

- Include a valid Contact ID.
- Include Opportunity Name.
- Include Pipeline.
- Add Stage, Status, Value, and custom fields when needed.
- Opportunity ID is not required for a new Opportunity.

### **Updating Existing Opportunities**

When updating an Opportunity:

1. Include the existing **Opportunity ID** in the CSV.
2. Map that column to Opportunity ID.
3. Map the fields you want to update.
4. Decide whether blank cells should overwrite existing values.
5. Start with a small test import before updating a large number of Opportunities.

> **Important:** A missing or incorrect Opportunity ID can result in the importer creating another Opportunity instead of updating the intended one.

If you need the IDs before preparing your CSV, see the related HighLevel documentation for locating Pipeline, Stage, and Opportunity IDs.

---

## **Import Contacts and Opportunities Together**

A combined import is useful when the contacts associated with the Opportunities do not already exist in HighLevel. Contact and Opportunity information can be placed on the same CSV row so the records can be created/imported and associated during the import.

Use this method when migrating data such as:

| Contact Data | Opportunity Data |
| --- | --- |
| First Name | Opportunity Name |
| Last Name | Pipeline |
| Email | Pipeline Stage |
| Phone | Opportunity Value |
| Contact custom fields | Opportunity Status |
|  | Opportunity custom fields |

During the import:

1. Select **Contacts + Opportunities**.
2. Upload the combined CSV.
3. Map Contact columns to Contact fields.
4. Map Opportunity columns to Opportunity fields.
5. Review both sets of mappings.
6. Complete the import.

Contact-specific requirements such as valid identifying information and phone formatting apply when Contact records are being imported.

For complete Contact-import preparation requirements, see the dedicated Contact CSV import documentation rather than duplicating those rules here.

---

## **Review Import Results and Fix Errors**

Bulk Actions provides visibility into the status and outcome of your CSV import. Reviewing the results is especially important after large migrations because some rows can succeed while others fail due to missing IDs, invalid values, or mapping problems.

After starting the import:

1. Go to **Bulk Actions**.
2. Locate the applicable import.
3. Review its status.
4. Click **Show Stats** to view the import results.
5. Review successful and failed records.
6. Open the **Error** tab when failures are present.
7. Download the available error log.
8. Review the reason each affected row failed.
9. Correct the failed rows in your CSV.
10. Re-import only the corrected records as appropriate.

Avoid immediately re-importing the entire original file when only some rows failed, especially if the successful rows already created Opportunities.

---

## **Troubleshooting Common Opportunity Import Issues**

Most Opportunity import errors are caused by missing identifiers, pipeline mismatches, incorrect update behavior, or field-mapping problems. Checking these areas first can help resolve failed rows without rebuilding the entire import.

### 

### **Opportunity Is Not Linked to the Correct Contact**

Confirm that the CSV contains the correct **Contact ID** and that the column is mapped to Contact ID.

For an Opportunities-only import, each Opportunity must be associated with an existing contact.

### 

### **A New Opportunity Was Created Instead of Updating the Existing One**

Check the **Opportunity ID**. If the update row does not contain the correct Opportunity ID, HighLevel may treat it as a new Opportunity.

### **Pipeline Is Not Accepted**

Confirm that the Pipeline value corresponds to an existing HighLevel pipeline. Create the required pipeline before importing rather than expecting the CSV import to create the pipeline automatically.

### **Opportunity Appears in the Wrong Stage**

Review the Pipeline Stage value and confirm that the intended stage exists within the selected pipeline.

### **Existing Data Was Replaced by Blank Values**

Review whether **Don't update Empty Values** was enabled during an update import. Enable it when blank CSV cells should preserve the existing HighLevel values.

### **A Custom Field Is Missing During Mapping**

Confirm that:

- The custom field was created before starting the import.
- It was created for the **Opportunity** object rather than the Contact object.
- You are mapping the CSV column to the correct Opportunity field.

### **Some Rows Failed While Others Imported Successfully**

Open the import under **Bulk Actions > Show Stats > Error**, download the error log, correct the failed rows, and re-import the corrected data.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I import Opportunities without importing Contacts?**

Yes, if the contacts already exist in HighLevel. For an Opportunities-only import, each Opportunity must include a valid **Contact ID** so HighLevel can associate it with the correct contact.

**Q: Is Contact ID required for an Opportunities-only import?**

Yes. Current HighLevel documentation requires Contact ID, Opportunity Name, and Pipeline for an Opportunities-only CSV import.

**Q: How do I update an existing Opportunity instead of creating a new one?**

Include the existing **Opportunity ID** in your CSV and map it during the import. Without the correct Opportunity ID, HighLevel may create another Opportunity instead of updating the intended record.

**Q: Do my Pipelines and Stages need to exist before importing?**

Create the required pipelines and applicable stages before importing. Pipeline values should correspond to existing HighLevel pipelines, and any imported stage should belong to the intended pipeline.

**Q: What happens to existing values when my update CSV contains blank cells?**

Enable **Don't update Empty Values** when blank CSV cells should leave existing HighLevel Opportunity data unchanged.

**Q: Can I import Opportunity custom fields?**

Yes. Create the custom fields for the Opportunity object before starting the import, then map the applicable CSV columns during field mapping.

**Q: Can I undo an Opportunity import?**

No. HighLevel does not provide a one-click rollback for a completed import. Test with a small sample file and review your mappings carefully before processing a large dataset.

**Q: Where can I find failed Opportunity import rows?**

Open **Bulk Actions**, locate the import, select **Show Stats**, and review the **Error** tab. Download the error log to identify and correct failed rows.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Importing Contacts Using a CSV File](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004432)
- [CSV File Format for Importing Objects](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003905)
- [Importing Contacts and Opportunities via CSV](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004432)
- [Troubleshooting Bulk Imports Via CSV](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001223155)
- [How to Use Custom Fields for Opportunities](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000521)
- [How to Find Pipeline, Stage, and Opportunity IDs in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001160284)

title_en: Rentals — Partial Payments
source_md:
# **What Are Partial Payments for Rentals?**

Partial Payments helps rental businesses accept a smaller payment at checkout and collect the remainder closer to the rental date. This is especially useful for high-value rentals such as vehicles, vacation homes, and equipment.

Partial Payments lets customers split their rental cost into two scheduled payments: a deposit collected at booking and the remaining balance due before the rental starts, with optional automatic collection. This reduces the amount due at booking and helps convert higher-value rentals that customers might otherwise abandon at checkout.

When enabled, a HighLevel invoice is created with a two-installment payment schedule for each booking. The deposit row is charged immediately. When auto-collection is enabled, HighLevel attempts to charge the balance on the configured due date using the card saved at booking.

```
Note: Partial Payments requires Require Payment at Booking to be turned on. When Require Payment is off, installment schedules cannot be created — the booking is confirmed without charge and payment is collected manually.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Partial Payments for Rentals?](#What-Are-Partial-Payments-for-Rentals?)
- [Key Benefits of Partial Payments for Rentals](#Key-Benefits-of-Partial-Payments-for-Rentals)
- [How It Works](#How-It-Works)
- [Prerequisites](#Prerequisites)
- [How to Configure](#How-to-Configure)
- [Security Deposit and Partial Payments](#Security-Deposit-and-Partial-Payments)
- [What Customers See at Checkout](#What-Customers-See-at-Checkout)
- [Viewing and Managing Payments](#Viewing-and-Managing-Payments)
- [Payment Failure](#Payment-Failure)
- [Booking Changes and Additional Charges](#Booking-Changes-and-Additional-Charges)
- [Non-Card Payments](#Non-Card-Payments)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **Key Benefits of Partial Payments for Rentals**

Flexible payment schedules make higher-value bookings easier to reserve while helping businesses keep payment timing and outstanding balances clear.

- **Lower upfront cost:** Customers secure a rental by paying a configured deposit rather than the entire rental price.
- **Clear checkout amounts:** Customers see what is due today and when the remaining payment is due.
- **Optional automatic collection:** Businesses can enable balance charging on the scheduled due date.
- **Payment visibility:** Booking details show each scheduled payment's amount, due date, and status.
- **Flexible security deposit timing:** Eligible security deposits can be collected with the booking deposit or final balance.

---

## **How It Works**

The payment schedule separates the booking deposit from the remaining rental balance. Understanding when each installment is created and due helps you predict what customers will pay.

**Payment schedule**

When a customer books with Partial Payments enabled, a HighLevel invoice is created with two payment schedules:

- **Schedule 1 — Deposit:** Payable immediately at checkout. Amount = the deposit percentage × rental total.
- **Schedule 2 — Balance:** Payable on the configured due date. Amount = remaining rental total

```
Security deposit can be due along with the deposit or with the balance, depending upon how it is configured.
```

**Collapse rule — late bookings**

If a booking is made within the configured threshold, both installments are collapsed into a single full payment payable immediately at checkout.

If the balance due date has already passed at the time of booking, the same collapse applies.

**Example :**

Balance is set to be collected 7 days before the rental start date, however the booking is being made 2 days before the rental start date, in this case, the payment not be split into two installments.

**Payment methods**

Auto-charge on the balance due date requires a card saved at booking. Cash and offline payments cannot be auto-charged — see [Non-Card Payments](#non-card-payments) below.

```
ACH bank transfer support will be extended soon.
```

---

## **Prerequisites**

Payment collection must be configured before installment schedules can be created. Confirm the booking payment setting and available payment methods before switching on Partial Payments.

Before enabling Partial Payments, confirm the following:

- **Require Payment at Booking is on.** Partial Payments is not available when Require Payment is off. The toggle will not appear.
- **Card or ACH payment methods are available.** Auto-charge on the balance due date only works when the customer saves a card at checkout. If your location accepts cash only, Partial Payments will not auto-charge the balance.

```
When partial payments is enabled, other payment methods are not allowed at checkout as they can't be auto-charged.
```

---

## **How to Configure**

Global payment settings determine the deposit percentage and how far ahead of the rental the balance becomes due. Review these values carefully because they apply to new bookings across your listings.

All Partial Payments settings live in **Calendars → Calendar Settings → Rentals → Global Settings → Payment settings**.

**Step 1 — Enable Partial Payments**

1. Go to Global Settings → Payment settings.
2. Confirm **Require payment at booking** is turned on.
3. Toggle**Partial payments***ON*.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084318881/original/dXJchNu_y7mSxlTSgIGOkH75QKToFuQAOg.png?1793109603)

Show Rentals → Global Settings → Payment Settings, with Require Payment at Booking, Enable Partial Payments, the deposit field, balance due setting, auto-collect toggle, and Save Changes highlighted.

**Step 2 — Configure the payment schedule**

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
 | Deposit amount | 1–99% of booking total (including applicable taxes and fees, but excluding the refundable security deposit) charged at booking |
| Balance due | When is the remaining balance due |
| Auto-collect balance on due date | Automatically charges the saved card on the balance due date. When on, only card-based payment methods appear at checkout. |

```
Auto-charge timing: Scheduled installments are charged at 11:00 AM ET / 10:00 AM CT / 9:00 AM MT / 8:00 AM PT on the due date.
```

**Step 3 — Security deposit timing (if applicable)**

This option appears only when **Require payment at booking is ON**, **Security deposit is ON**, **Collect upfront is selected**, and **Partial Payments is ON**.

- **With the booking deposit** —The security deposit is collected with the deposit at booking. Choose this for maximum early protection on high-value assets.
- **With the balance payment**  — The security deposit is collected alongside the balance. This minimises the amount due at booking.

**Applies to new bookings only:** Saving or changing the global payment plan does not recalculate existing bookings. Existing bookings keep the schedule established when they were created.

---

## **Security Deposit and Partial Payments**

Refundable security deposits are separate from the rental deposit percentage. Choosing when they are collected affects the amounts customers see due today and later.

When Security deposit is set to **Collect upfront** and Partial Payments is on, the security deposit is always collected as a single full amount — it is never split proportionally across installments.

**Security deposit timing options**

| Option | When SD is charged | Due today (example: $1,200 rental, $300 SD, 25% deposit) |
| --- | --- | --- |
  | With the balance payment | Alongside the balance, before rental start | $300 *(deposit only)* |
| With the booking deposit | With the first installment at booking | $600 *(deposit + SD)* |

**Card on File mode**

When Security Deposits is set to **Card on File**, the deposit is not included until charged explicitly later. Partial payments works normally on the rental total only. The card saved at booking is used for both the balance auto-charge and as the card on file for the security deposit.

---

## **What Customers See at Checkout**

The order summary makes future charges visible before a customer confirms a rental. The displayed amounts reflect the selected booking deposit, balance due date, and security deposit timing.

The booking page payment summary updates automatically based on your configuration. Customers always see:

- **Due today** — the deposit amount payable while booking
- **Upcoming payment** — the balance amount and due date

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084319012/original/qOm32yPg1dRJ0SFM49ceDpLox64iM8nBzg.png?1793109652)

Highlight the customer order summary showing “Due today,” the future payment amount and due date, and the automatic charge explanation where applicable.

**If the booking is within the collapse window**

The installment schedule is replaced with a single full payment.

**If Require Payment at Booking is off**

No charge is collected.

---

## **Viewing and Managing Payments**

The booking payment summary separates installments so you can see which amounts are already paid and which still need attention. Use the booking view to confirm the due date and status before collecting a payment manually.

1. Open **Calendars → Appointment List View**, select **Rentals**, and open the booking.
2. Review the payment summary for each installment's **amount**, **due date**, and **status** (for example, **Payment 1 of 2 · Paid** and **Payment 2 of 2 · Pending**).
3. To collect an outstanding installment early or when no card is available for auto-collection, use **Actions → Collect Payment** from the booking sidebar.
4. Select one scheduled payment or multiple outstanding payments to collect together. Scheduled payments are collected for their full scheduled amounts.
5. Return to the payment summary to verify the updated status.

## 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084319122/original/o6Vzzp807osz_fC236qjGY7gYAE99QaujQ.png?1793109710)

---

## **Payment Failure**

A failed scheduled payment can leave a balance outstanding even after a rental was booked successfully. Review the payment status and invoice notification settings to follow up appropriately.

Payment failure handling for scheduled installments is managed natively by our invoices. No additional setup is needed.

**What happens when a balance charge fails**

1. It attempts to charge the saved card on the due date.
2. We retry the charge automatically — up to 3 attempts, 24 hours apart.
3. After all retries fail, the payment needs to collected manually.

```
Configure reminder and failure email templates in HighLevel Invoice Settings (Payments → Invoices & Estimates → Settings → Notifications). These templates control the reminder sent before each installment and the failure email sent after a failed charge. These templates are not overridden by the booking system.
```

```
Note: Bookings are not auto-cancelled after a payment failure. Cancellation is always an operator action.
```

---

## **Booking Changes and Additional Charges**

Editing dates or prices can change what remains payable. Review the updated payment schedule after every modification so charges and due dates stay aligned with the rental.

**When a booking is updated, the payment schedule is recalculated based on when the update happens.**

**Rental date changes:** If the rental start date changes, the outstanding balance due date moves with the new start date according to the configured number of days before the rental.

```
If auto-collect was on, it is turned off for the booking if it is updated.
```

**Before the deposit is paid**

The invoice is updated with the new total and a fresh payment schedule is calculated using the same configured percentages.

**After the deposit is paid, before the balance is due**

- If the total increases, the balance due in the 2nd installment is increased.
- If the total decreases, the balance due is decreased. [Note : Balance due can never fall below what has been already paid].

**After all installments are paid**

- **Total increases** — An **Additional charges** row is added to the booking. This creates another payment schedule row in the backend on the invoice.
- If you keep adding more listings/updates after complete payment, the Additional charges row updates to reflect the new totals, while on the invoice, a new schedule row gets added everytime.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084319276/original/S6pd0SOBoBc9GW27dCLaOBwdbLz-HP0gLQ.png?1793109771)

Show the separate Additional Charge row and Pending status created after the booking amount increases following full payment.

```
Note: Changes to a booking total after the invoice is fully paid do not trigger automatic refunds. The operator must initiate any refund manually from the booking detail.
```

---

## **Non-Card Payments**

Future automatic collection depends on a payment method that supports charging the customer later. Check the checkout payment options before relying on scheduled auto-collection.

Auto-charge on the balance due date requires a card saved for the contact. Cash and other offline payment methods cannot be stored for future auto-charge.

When partial payments are enabled, all other payment methods are disabled.

```
Note: When Require Payment at Booking is off, all payment is collected manually regardless of payment method. Partial Payments is not available in this mode.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Can I set different payment plans for different listings?**

No. Global Settings defines the default for all listings.

**What happens if a customer cancels after paying the deposit but before the balance is due?**

The unpaid balance row is voided immediately — it is never charged. The deposit refund follows your cancellation policy. The security deposit (if collected upfront) is always refunded in full on pre-rental cancellations, regardless of the cancellation policy.

**Can a customer pay the balance early?**

Yes. The customer can click Pay Now on the invoice at any time to pay the balance before the due date. Alternatively, the user/admin can also collect the payment via the booking view early on.

**What if I change the deposit % after bookings have already been made?**

Changes to Global Settings apply to new bookings only. Existing bookings retain the schedule that was created at the time of booking.

**What if I add an extra charge after the customer has fully paid?**

An additional row is created on the booking and the invoice for the extra amount. The original payment schedule is not modified. Send a payment request from the booking detail to collect the additional charge.

**At what time does auto-charge fire on the due date?**

Auto-charge runs at 11:00 AM ET / 10:00 AM CT / 9:00 AM MT / 8:00 AM PT on the configured due date.

**Can I charge custom amounts when partial payments are enabled?**

No. When partial payments are enabled, you can only collect the configured schedule amounts in full. [Ex : 25%, 75% or both schedules together].

**Does changing the rental start date change the balance due date?**

Yes. The balance due date adjusts with the new rental start date using the configured lead time.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Rentals — Global Settings](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006640-rentals-global-settings)
- [Rentals — Creating a Booking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006624-rentals-creating-a-booking)
- [Rentals — Editing a Booking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006626-rentals-editing-a-booking)
- [Rentals — Overview of Bookings](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006622-rentals-overview-of-bookings)
- [Rentals — Configuring Pricing & Discounts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006611-rentals-configuring-pricing-discounts)
- [How to Set Up Self-Service Cancellations for Rentals](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008750-how-to-set-up-self-service-cancellations-for-rentals)

title_en: Hair Salon Snapshot
source_md:
Snapshots • Beauty & Fashion • Account Setup

Hair Salon Snapshot: Setup and Installation Guide

The Hair Salon Snapshot provides a reusable starting point for agencies creating sub-accounts for hair salons. It includes calendars, custom fields, forms, funnels, pipelines, templates, review settings, and workflows that can be customized before launch.

The Hair Salon Snapshot helps agencies reduce repetitive setup by importing a prebuilt collection of salon-focused account assets. The snapshot can be used when creating a new sub-account or loaded into an existing sub-account.

A snapshot is a configuration template, not a finished live account. Business details, staff, calendars, domains, communications, integrations, workflows, and customer-facing pages must be reviewed and tested before they are activated.

What You'll Learn

Learn what the Hair Salon Snapshot contains, how to import and install it, what is not transferred, which settings require customization, and how to test the account before launch.

Important

Do not publish pages, activate workflows, send messages, or assign live phone traffic immediately after installation. Review and test every imported asset first. Loading a snapshot is not an account backup or one-click undo process.

# What Is the Hair Salon Snapshot?

The Hair Salon Snapshot is a reusable account template designed to accelerate the setup of sub-accounts for hair salons. It packages selected configuration assets so agencies can begin with a consistent salon-focused structure instead of building every calendar, field, page, template, pipeline, and workflow from scratch.

The current snapshot appears in the agency snapshot library as **V2 Industry - Beauty & Fashion - Hair Salon**. After installation, each imported asset should be customized to match the salon's services, staff, branding, booking rules, communications, and operating processes.

## Key Benefits of the Hair Salon Snapshot

The snapshot reduces repetitive configuration while giving agencies a consistent foundation that can be adapted to each salon's services and customer journey.

- **Faster Account Setup:** Begin with prebuilt salon-focused assets instead of creating the complete sub-account manually.
- **Consistent Client Onboarding:** Use the same structure across multiple salon clients while customizing business-specific details.
- **Prebuilt Scheduling Foundation:** Start with service calendars and a calendar group that can be assigned to staff and updated for salon services.
- **Lead Capture and Follow-Up:** Use the included form, funnels, pipelines, templates, and workflows as a starting point for salon lead generation.
- **Reusable Marketing Assets:** Customize imported email templates, message templates, offer pages, and nurture automation.
- **Flexible Deployment:** Create a new sub-account from the snapshot or load selected assets into an existing account.

## What Is Included in the Hair Salon Snapshot

Reviewing the asset inventory before installation helps you understand what will be added and which areas require customization. The current V2 Industry Beauty & Fashion snapshot contains 60 assets across 11 categories.

  

| Asset Category | Quantity | Primary Area |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Calendar Groups | 1 | Calendars |
| Calendars | 6 | Calendars |
| Custom Fields | 29 | Custom Fields |
| Custom Values | 3 | Custom Values |
| Email Builder Templates | 5 | Marketing |
| Forms | 1 | Sites |
| Funnels & Websites | 3 | Funnels & Websites |
| Pipelines | 2 | Opportunities |
| Review Settings | 1 | Reputation Management |
| Text & Email Templates | 2 | Marketing |
| Workflows | 7 | Automations |
| **Total** | **60** | **11 asset categories** |

## Supporting Resources in the Setup Guide

The Hair Salon Setup Guide provides implementation guidance that goes beyond the assets shown in the snapshot inventory. These resources help configure the imported account but should not be treated as automatically deployed snapshot assets.

- **Account Setup Guidance:** Business Profile, users, phone, email, domains, social connections, payments, and reputation settings.
- **Salon Advertising Example:** An advertising mockup and campaign guidance for promoting a salon offer.
- **Voice AI Guidance:** Prompt suggestions for common salon questions, lead qualification, and appointment booking.
- **Quick-Win Recommendations:** Mobile app, chat widget, missed-call text-back, payment requests, snippets, and review requests.
- **Launch Checklist:** Guidance for updating the form, funnel, website, calendars, pipelines, workflows, email templates, and Link-in-Bio page.

[Open the Hair Salon Setup Guide](https://playbooks.gohighlevel.com/hair-salon)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081027732/original/Wr-ZGJn8KkyuhFiahDu7J-1CeSjdx3-Dxg.png?1789532561)

**Resource clarification:** The current snapshot inventory does not list an imported Ad Campaign, Social Planner post, or Voice AI Agent category. Treat the advertising mockup, social guidance, and Voice AI prompts as supporting setup resources unless those assets are verified inside the destination account.

## What Is Not Included

Snapshots transfer reusable configuration assets, not the salon's live customer history or authenticated third-party services. Understanding these exclusions prevents the imported account from being mistaken for a fully connected production account.

- Contacts and imported customer databases
- Conversations, messages, emails, and conversation history
- Appointments and historical calendar activity
- Live reputation data or existing customer reviews
- Stripe connections or other payment-provider authentication
- Phone-number ownership, routing, or carrier registration
- Email-domain authentication and DNS records
- Facebook, Instagram, Google Business Profile, or other external integrations
- Staff login credentials or connected external calendars
- Published website domains or live funnel deployment

## Before You Install the Hair Salon Snapshot

Preparing the agency and destination account before installation reduces import errors, duplicate assets, and accidental replacement of existing configuration.

- Confirm you have Agency Admin access or the required Snapshot permissions.
- Decide whether the snapshot will create a new sub-account or be loaded into an existing one.
- Review the snapshot's 60-asset inventory before choosing what to install.
- Review existing assets in the destination sub-account if it is already active.
- Export or document important existing configuration before overriding conflicts.
- Collect the salon's business name, logo, contact details, address, website, time zone, currency, services, staff, pricing, and availability.
- Collect access to required domains, email DNS, phone services, social accounts, Google Business Profile, and payment provider.
- Plan a testing period before imported assets are activated for live customers.

## How To Install and Set Up the Hair Salon Snapshot

Choose the installation path that matches the destination. Importing a shared snapshot adds it to the agency library, while creating or loading applies its assets to a specific sub-account.

### Step 1: Import the Shared Snapshot

Use the Snapshot Share Link to add the Hair Salon Snapshot to the agency-level snapshot library.

1. Sign in to the agency account that should receive the snapshot.
2. Open the Snapshot Share Link below.
3. Review the snapshot information and rename it if needed.
4. Import the snapshot.
5. Go to **Agency View → Account Snapshots → Imported Snapshots**.
6. Wait until the import completes before loading the snapshot.

[Import the Hair Salon Snapshot](https://affiliates.gohighlevel.com/?fp_ref=ghl-main&share=5L9fPJXULvqiibJnGBje)

**Sign-in behavior:** If the share link opens a sign-in or account-selection page first, sign in to the intended agency and reopen the link.

### Option A: Create a New Sub-Account from the Snapshot

Creating a new account from the snapshot is the cleanest option when the salon does not already have an active sub-account containing important assets.

1. From **Agency View**, open **Account Snapshots**.
2. Open **My snapshots** or **Imported snapshots**, depending on where the snapshot is stored.
3. Search for **V2 Industry - Beauty & Fashion - Hair Salon**.
4. Click the blue **+** icon labeled **Create new account**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081027751/original/jg18FgVq2UG3cyAmJGvzgj5i66iVvnZmHg.png?1789532634)

5. Enter and verify the salon's business information.
6. Create the sub-account.
7. Wait for the snapshot assets to finish loading.
8. Open the new sub-account and begin the customization checklist below.

### Option B: Load the Snapshot into an Existing Sub-Account

Loading into an existing account preserves the account's live customer data while adding or updating selected snapshot assets. This path requires careful conflict review.

**Conflict warning:** Do not automatically override every conflict. Review the current asset and imported version before choosing **Override** or **Skip**. Loading the same snapshot more than once can create conflicts or duplicate assets.

1. From **Agency View**, open **Sub-Accounts**.
2. Locate the destination sub-account.
3. Open the three-dot menu in the **Actions** column and select **Manage Client**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081027741/original/deZALAP_N8zARsOfYJiZ4gDPqoOOUkGCUg.png?1789532604)

4. From the Manage Client view, click **Actions → Load Snapshot**.
5. Select the Hair Salon Snapshot.
6. Select all assets or only the categories required for the account.
7. Review every detected conflict.
8. Choose whether each conflicting asset should be skipped or overridden.
9. Confirm the load.
10. Wait for the load to finish before editing imported assets.

## What To Customize After Installation

Customization converts the imported template into a functioning account for the specific salon. Complete the highest-impact account settings first so downstream pages, calendars, messages, and workflows use accurate information.

### Priority 1: Business Profile and Custom Values

- Business and legal names
- Logo and brand identity
- Phone number, email address, physical address, time zone, language, and currency
- Website and branded links
- Promotion name
- Website booking-page URL
- Booking thank-you-page URL

### Priority 2: Staff and Calendars

- Create or review user profiles for salon staff.
- Assign staff members to the correct service calendars.
- Update service names, descriptions, duration, pricing, buffers, availability, and booking rules.
- Connect each staff member's supported external calendar.
- Configure linked and conflict calendars to prevent double-booking.
- Test the booking experience on desktop and mobile.

### Priority 3: Form, Funnel, Website, and Link-in-Bio Page

- Update salon name, logo, colors, fonts, images, and contact information.
- Replace placeholder services, descriptions, prices, offers, and FAQs.
- Review the claim-offer form and consent language.
- Update every button, navigation item, calendar link, phone link, and social link.
- Review page titles, descriptions, and SEO metadata.
- Connect the intended custom domain.
- Preview each page before publishing.

### Priority 4: Pipelines, Templates, and Workflows

- Review both pipelines and update stages to match the salon's process.
- Review all five Email Builder Templates.
- Review both Text & Email Templates.
- Review all seven imported workflows.
- Confirm each trigger, filter, sender, action, link, delay, branch, and internal notification.
- Keep workflows in draft while testing.
- Publish only the workflows the salon is ready to use.

### Priority 5: Communications and Integrations

- Purchase or connect the appropriate phone number and configure routing.
- Complete messaging registration where required.
- Set up a dedicated sending domain and branded links.
- Connect Facebook, Instagram, Google Business Profile, and Social Planner as needed.
- Connect Stripe or another supported payment provider before collecting payments.
- Configure review-request destinations and message templates.
- Choose and configure the appropriate chat widget.
- Build and test an optional Voice AI Agent before assigning live phone traffic.

## How To Test the Hair Salon Snapshot Before Launch

End-to-end testing confirms that the imported assets work together and use the correct salon information before real leads and customers enter the account.

1. Create an internal test contact.
2. Submit the imported salon offer form.
3. Confirm the contact record contains the expected custom-field data.
4. Confirm the correct opportunity is created in the intended pipeline and stage.
5. Book a test appointment through each relevant calendar or Service Menu.
6. Review workflow enrollment and execution history.
7. Verify every email, SMS, internal notification, link, and custom value.
8. Test website, funnel, and Link-in-Bio buttons on desktop and mobile.
9. Confirm the connected domain and published pages resolve correctly.
10. Test payment collection only after the payment provider is configured.
11. Test the chat widget and conversation routing.
12. Test any Voice AI Agent before assigning a live business number.

## Troubleshooting the Hair Salon Snapshot

Most snapshot issues can be traced to permissions, an incomplete import, asset conflicts, missing account-specific configuration, or unpublished assets.

| Issue | What To Check |
| --- | --- |
| The share link does not open the import screen | Sign in to the intended agency, reopen the link, and confirm the user has snapshot permissions. |
| The snapshot is greyed out or still importing | Wait for the import status to complete. Review the displayed error and retry if needed. |
| Load Snapshot is missing | Confirm snapshot permissions are enabled for the agency user. |
| Duplicate assets appeared | Check whether the snapshot was loaded more than once or a conflict was imported instead of skipped. |
| Website or funnel is not live | Imported pages are drafts. Connect a domain, review the content, and publish. |
| Calendars show no availability | Confirm assigned staff, schedules, service settings, and conflict calendars. |
| Workflows do not run | Review publication status, triggers, filters, senders, custom values, and execution history. |
| Pages or messages show placeholder information | Update the Business Profile, Custom Values, page content, templates, and workflow actions. |

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How many assets are included?

The current V2 Industry Beauty & Fashion snapshot contains 60 assets across 11 categories, including seven workflows.

Q: Is importing the same as loading the snapshot?

No. Importing adds the shared snapshot to the agency library. Loading applies selected assets to a specific sub-account.

Q: Can I load it into an existing sub-account?

Yes. Select only the required categories and review every conflict before confirming the load.

Q: Does the snapshot include contacts or appointments?

No. Snapshot installation transfers selected configuration assets, not live contacts, conversations, appointments, or historical customer data.

Q: Are the imported pages published automatically?

No. Imported websites and funnels require content review, domain setup, path configuration, testing, and publishing.

Q: Does the snapshot connect phone, email, social, Google, or Stripe accounts?

No. External services and authenticated integrations must be connected separately.

Q: Does the snapshot include a configured ad campaign or Voice AI Agent?

The verified inventory does not list those asset categories. The setup guide provides an advertising example and Voice AI prompt guidance that can be configured separately.

Q: Can I remove the entire snapshot after loading it?

A loaded snapshot cannot be unloaded as one package. Imported assets can be edited, deactivated, or deleted individually.

title_en: Organize and Personalize Tags with Categories and Colors
source_md:
Contacts • Labs

Organize and Personalize Tags with Categories and Colors

Build a cleaner contact-tag system by grouping related tags into categories and assigning colors that make important labels easier to recognize.

What You'll Learn

HighLevel now makes contact tags easier to organize and identify with **tag categories** and **customizable tag colors**. Categories group related tags into a structured system, while colors provide a visual cue when tags appear across supported contact views.

Existing tags continue working without additional setup. They initially appear in gray and are automatically placed in **No category**, allowing you to organize them gradually.

Labs Availability

Tag categories and colors are currently available through **Labs**. Labs features may evolve as they progress toward broader availability.

# **What are Tag Categories and Colors?**

Tag Categories and Colors enhance HighLevel's existing contact-tag system without changing the underlying purpose of tags. Categories provide an organizational layer for grouping related tags, while colors provide a visual layer that makes tags easier to identify.

- **Tag Categories:** Group related contact tags into named categories.
- **Tag Colors:** Apply predefined or custom colors to individual tags.

**Existing tags:** Existing contact tags remain available, initially appear in gray, and are placed automatically in **No category**.

## **Key Benefits of Tag Categories and Colors**

A structured tagging system makes large contact databases easier to maintain and reduces the time users spend searching through long lists of similar tags.

- **Improved Organization:** Group related tags into categories that match your business processes.
- **Faster Identification:** Use color to recognize important tag types at a glance.
- **Flexible Customization:** Choose predefined colors or select a custom color.
- **Safe Existing-Tag Handling:** Existing tags continue working and begin in No category with gray styling.
- **Bulk Management:** Move multiple tags between categories or apply one color to up to 100 selected tags in a single action, reducing repetitive updates across large tag libraries.
- **Cleaner Contact Management:** Category grouping makes tags easier to locate on contact records.
- **Visual Consistency:** Tag colors appear across supported contact and Smart List experiences.

## **Understanding the Tags Management Page**

The Tags management page provides a centralized workspace for reviewing, creating, organizing, and updating contact tags. It combines category, description, color, and tag information so you can manage a growing tag library more consistently.

You can also select up to 100 tags at once and apply the same color to the entire selection. Bulk color updates make it easier to introduce or reorganize a consistent color system without editing each tag individually.

The Tags tab includes information such as:

- Tag name
- Description
- Category
- Created date
- Updated date
- Edit and delete actions

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080662249/original/hkqhWLdcPiFFHLXVRH0ZnJZby80W4zYiAA.png?1789103635)

## **Organizing Tags with Categories**

Categories act as containers for related contact tags. Instead of maintaining one large, flat tag list, you can group tags based on how your team uses them, such as lifecycle stage, product interest, region, source, or customer status.

### **Creating a Category**

A clear category structure makes individual tags easier to locate and creates a repeatable organizational model for teams that use a large number of tags.

1. Open the **Tags** management page.
2. Click **Create category**.
3. Enter a descriptive **Category name**.
4. Add an optional description.
5. Click **Create category**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080662317/original/MxP37jZ-Dv2aLS9MEBrA08m6OhgFvKsIcw.png?1789103661)

### **Understanding No Category**

No category provides a default location for tags that have not been assigned to a custom category, ensuring every tag always has an organizational home.

HighLevel places a tag in **No category** when:

- The tag existed before tag categories were introduced.
- No custom category has been assigned.
- The category containing the tag is deleted.

**Important:** Deleting a category does not delete its tags. Those tags automatically move to **No category**.

## **Creating Tags with Categories and Colors**

Assigning organization and visual styling when a tag is created reduces future cleanup and helps other users understand what the tag represents.

When creating a tag, you can configure:

- Tag name
- Category
- Description
- Tag color

1. Click **New tag**.
2. Enter the **Tag name**.
3. Select the appropriate **Category**. If the category you need does not exist, you can create a new category directly from the category selector and continue creating the tag without leaving the current flow.
4. Add an optional description.
5. Choose a tag color.
6. Review the **Preview**.
7. Click **Create tag**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080662393/original/4s_6EFeVfqPXRmAOV6-0HQuNQQHfKBnpXw.png?1789103682)

## **Personalizing Tags with Colors**

Tag colors provide a visual cue that helps users distinguish tag types faster. A consistent color system is especially helpful when individual contacts have several tags applied at the same time.

### **Using Predefined Colors**

Predefined colors offer a quick way to create visual consistency without manually selecting a specific color value. If no color is selected, the tag uses gray by default.

### **Using a Custom Color**

The custom color picker gives you greater control when the predefined options do not match the visual convention or brand palette you want to use.

1. Open the tag's edit action.
2. Locate **Tag color**.
3. Select the custom color option.
4. Choose the desired color from the picker.
5. Review the **Preview**.
6. Save the update.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080662403/original/luFUzqEqFfdJO2rxjuIz8RG513aWbLvOxg.png?1789103707)

**Best practice:** Use a repeatable color convention instead of assigning colors randomly. For example, use one color family for lifecycle tags, another for lead-source tags, and another for operational tags.

## **Moving Tags Between Categories**

Moving tags lets you reorganize an existing tag library without recreating the tags themselves. This is especially helpful when existing tags begin in No category and need to be organized into a new structure.

### **Bulk Moving Tags**

Bulk movement is the fastest way to organize an established tag library when several tags belong to the same category.

1. Open the **Tags** tab.
2. Select the tags you want to reorganize.
3. Click **Move to category**.
4. Select the destination category.
5. Confirm the move.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080662408/original/RaVUSWOjphfQVPCSd44OXVAtMeiWHl_hXA.png?1789103732)

## **Using Categories and Colors on Contact Records**

Categories make the tag selector easier to navigate on individual contact records, while colors make selected tags easier to distinguish once they have been applied.

### **Selecting Categorized Tags**

The tag selector supports searching by tags or categories and groups available tags according to their category, helping users locate the correct label more quickly.

1. Open the contact record.
2. Locate **Tags**.
3. Click the add/edit tags control.
4. Search for a tag or category.
5. Expand the appropriate category.
6. Select or deselect the required tags.
7. Click **Apply**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080662421/original/znYnrH1ygper2nW8UmWqivBBaQf3Yc7msQ.png?1789103758)

### **Viewing Colored Tags on a Contact**

Once tags are applied, their assigned colors appear on the contact record, making different classifications easier to recognize without opening the tag selector.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080662429/original/L10cbrA0MdXK0brSuqgPxep8f_NVE1wCyg.png?1789103777)

Tag colors also appear in supported **Smart List columns**, helping users scan tagged contacts more quickly.

## **How Existing Tags and Automations Are Affected**
