| **Contact** |  |  |  |  |  |
| vCard (.vcf) | 100MB | 100MB | 100MB | 50MB | 50MB |

---

## **Supported Formats & Browser Compatibility**

The formats below have verified validation, upload, listing, and Preview behavior across **Chrome**, **Firefox**, and **Safari**.

| Category | Formats | Browsers Verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Images** | **JPEG/JPG, PNG, SVG, WEBP, GIF, TIFF, HEIC** | Chrome, Firefox, Safari |
| **Audio** | **MP3, WAV, OGG/OGA** | Chrome, Firefox, Safari |
| **Video** | **MP4, MOV, WEBM, WMV, AVI, M4V** | Chrome, Firefox, Safari |
| **Documents** | **PDF, PPT, TXT, DOC, DOCX, CSV, XLS, XLSX** | Chrome, Firefox, Safari |
| **Archives** | **ZIP** | Chrome, Firefox, Safari |
| **Code/Other** | **JSON, CSS** | Chrome, Firefox, Safari |

```
Verified support includes JSON, CSS, OGG/OGA, M4V, HEIC, and consistent ZIP handling across supported browsers.
```

**Editable Text File Types**

Media Storage supports in-place editing for the following text file types:

- `.txt`

- `.css`

- `.json`

- `.sql`

- `.rtf`

Open a supported file in Preview and click Edit to modify it. Saving updates the existing file while preserving its file name and public URL.

For the complete editing workflow, see [Complete Guide to Media Storage!](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002707)

### **Preview Limit for Edited Text Files**

Supported text files larger than 5 MB can still be saved after editing.

After saving a file larger than 5 MB, the file is no longer available for Preview. Media Storage displays a warning before saving when this limit applies.

---

## **Private Files in Media Storage**

Media Storage supports **private files** for Digital Products. Private files help protect product files that should only be accessible through the appropriate product purchase or delivery flow.

```
Important: You cannot manually mark a file as private or select an Upload as Private option directly from Media Storage.

A file is automatically uploaded as a private file when you upload it as a Digital Product file while creating or configuring a product.
```

### **How Private Files Are Created**

Private status is determined by the HighLevel feature through which the file is uploaded.

For Digital Products, files uploaded through the Digital Product setup are automatically stored as private files.

### **How to Identify Private Files**

A **lock icon** appears on the thumbnail of a private file, indicating that the file has restricted access.

If you uploaded a file for a Digital Product and later locate it in Media Storage, look for the lock icon to confirm that the file is stored as private.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078933615/original/hDfWGPrl9H1rZU7kjlDB1LJLizNhrqdyNA.png?1787241191)

### **Manage Private Files**

Available actions for a private file include:

- **Download** — Download the private file.
- **Copy Private Link** — Generate a temporary link that can be used to access the private file.
- **Delete** — Delete the private file when it is no longer required.

```
Private links expire after 10 minutes. If access is required after the link expires, generate a new private link from Media Storage.
```

Because private links are temporary, do not use them as permanent URLs on websites, funnels, emails, or other locations that require ongoing file access.

### **Public vs. Private Files**

| Public File | Private Digital Product File |
| --- | --- |
| Uploaded normally through Media Storage | Uploaded through the Digital Product setup |
| Standard Media Storage file | Automatically stored as private |
| Does not display the private-file lock indicator | Displays a **lock icon** in Media Storage |
| Uses normal file access behavior | Supports temporary private links |
| Cannot be manually changed to private | Cannot currently be manually changed to public |

---

## **View Storage Usage**

Use the Media Usage modal to review how much storage your account is using and where that usage comes from.

The modal shows total storage with a color-coded bar and provides a per-module breakdown, including Media Library, Conversations, Memberships, Contacts, and Calendar.

Expand a module to review storage usage by file type, such as Images, Videos, Documents, and Audio.

To view storage usage:

1. Click the **three-dot (⋮)** menu and select **Storage**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155062681430/original/XI8ljBWL91zXbe_ZyMzRJOdu8ruXKBmIyQ.png?1768422309)
2. Click a module to view usage by file type.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155062681354/original/DE-M111JGPTTIIrXoiEw0z3VKURzojMwvA.png?1768422129)

---

## **Google Drive Integration**

**Connect Drive** enables you to import files you own from Google Drive.

```
Important: Shared files and shortcuts to shared files do not display because of Google Drive access, visibility, and ownership restrictions. Media Storage currently shows files owned by you.

Workaround: Create a copy of the shared file instead of creating a shortcut. The copied file can then appear as an owned file.
```

**When using Login As:**

- The **Connect Drive** button is disabled and grayed out.
- Google Drive data belonging to the original user does not display.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155045264698/original/HP5NHp025nopa0g-0c_PzcnKLh-1RnUeGA.png?1744887963)

---

## **Media Storage Across HighLevel Products**

Media Storage is integrated with other HighLevel products. When you access Media Storage from products such as funnels or websites, it opens in a modal so you can select or upload media without leaving the current workflow.

```
Note: Drag-and-drop uploads also work when Media Storage opens inside a Funnel modal. Drop files anywhere in the available modal drop zone before inserting them.
```

---

## **Agent-Generated Media**

Images, audio files, and videos created by Managed Agents are automatically saved to Media Storage as reusable files.

Agent-generated media:

- Is stored in Media Storage instead of relying on a temporary generated-media location.
- Appears at the root of the Media Library like a standard uploaded file.
- Uses recognizable generated-file names. For example, generated audio files use names beginning with `generated-audio-` and use the `.mp3` format.
- Can be found later using Media Storage search.
- Can be reused elsewhere in HighLevel, including emails, funnels, and social posts.
- Uses the standard video-processing pipeline for generated videos, including video thumbnails.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079586842/original/TplFwrt54BS9Ix9Pc6Jd1gSpxrghVKYV3A.png?1787946926)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What file types can I upload?**  
Media Storage supports images, videos, audio files, documents, fonts, contact files, and other supported application formats listed in this article.

**Q: Are upload limits the same across all HighLevel products?**  
No. Upload limits vary by file type and product. Use the Per-Product File Limits table above to compare the supported limits.

**Q: Why does a file download instead of opening in Preview?**  
Inline Preview depends on whether the browser and operating system support the file format. Files that cannot render inline remain available for download.

**Q: Can I make an existing Media Storage file private?**  
No. You cannot currently select an existing public file in Media Storage and change it to private. There is also no general **Make Private** option when uploading files directly to Media Storage.

For Digital Products, files uploaded through the Digital Product setup are automatically stored as private files and display a lock icon in Media Storage.

**Q: Can I integrate Media Storage with Google Drive?**  
Yes. Media Storage can display files you own in Google Drive. Shared files and shortcuts to shared files do not display.

**Q: How does Login As affect Google Drive access?**  
When Login As is active, the **Connect Drive** button is disabled and the original user's Google Drive content is hidden.

title_en: How to Use AI Employee Suggestive Mode in the Mobile App
source_md:
AI Employee Suggestive Mode gives your team a ready-to-send AI reply for eligible incoming messages directly in the HighLevel mobile app. Instead of choosing from multiple short suggestions, agents can review one suggested response, send it immediately, or edit it before replying. This creates a faster mobile workflow while keeping a human in control of every message.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is AI Employee Suggestive Mode in the Mobile App?](#What-is-AI-Employee-Suggestive-Mode-in-the-Mobile-App?)
- [Key Benefits of AI Employee Suggestive Mode](#Key-Benefits-of-AI-Employee-Suggestive-Mode)
- [AI Suggested Reply Actions](#AI-Suggested-Reply-Actions)
- [Send an AI Suggested Reply](#Send-an-AI-Suggested-Reply)
- [Edit an AI Suggested Reply](#Edit-an-AI-Suggested-Reply)
- [Dismiss and Restore an AI Suggestion](#Dismiss-and-Restore-an-AI-Suggestion)
- [AI Suggestion Updates and Draft Preservation](#AI-Suggestion-Updates-and-Draft-Preservation)
- [Eligibility and Availability for Mobile AI Suggested Replies](#Eligibility-and-Availability-for-Mobile-AI-Suggested-Replies)
- [Managing Conversation AI Settings on Web and Mobile](#Managing-Conversation-AI-Settings-on-Web-and-Mobile)
- [Suggestion ID and Troubleshooting](#Suggestion-ID-and-Troubleshooting)
- [How To Setup AI Employee Suggestive Mode for Mobile](#How-To-Setup-AI-Employee-Suggestive-Mode-for-Mobile)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is AI Employee Suggestive Mode in the Mobile App?**

AI Employee Suggestive Mode uses Conversation AI to draft a response to an eligible incoming message without sending that response automatically. Your team reviews the AI Suggested Reply and decides whether to send it as written, edit it first, or dismiss it. Core Conversation AI configuration and mode selection are managed from the web, while the mobile app provides the tools needed to work with suggestions during conversations.

When Suggestive Mode is active, the mobile experience displays one clear AI Suggested Reply above the message composer. This brings the mobile workflow in line with the Suggestive Mode experience on the web while reducing the number of decisions required to reply to a contact.

---

## **Key Benefits of AI Employee Suggestive Mode**

Suggestive Mode combines AI-generated responses with human review, helping teams respond efficiently without giving up control over what is ultimately sent to a contact.

- **Faster responses:** Review one ready-to-send suggestion instead of choosing between multiple short reply options.
- **Human oversight:** AI drafts the response, while an agent decides whether to edit or send it.
- **Simpler mobile workflow:** Send, edit, dismiss, and restore suggestions directly from the conversation.
- **Draft protection:** Continue working on an existing draft even when a new inbound message generates an updated suggestion.
- **Consistent web and mobile experience:** Use the same Suggestive Mode approach while working away from your desktop.
- **Easier troubleshooting:** Use the Suggestion ID when additional information is needed for support.

---

## **AI Suggested Reply Actions**

AI Suggested Reply actions let agents decide how much of the AI-generated response they want to use. A suggestion can be sent immediately, customized before sending, temporarily hidden, or restored without leaving the conversation.

### 

### **Send an AI Suggested Reply**

Sending a suggestion as written is useful when the generated response already matches what you want to communicate.

1. Open **Conversations** in the HighLevel mobile app.
2. Select a conversation with an eligible new inbound message.
3. Review the AI Suggested Reply displayed above the composer.
4. Tap **Send** to deliver the response as written.

### **Edit an AI Suggested Reply**

Editing gives agents the speed of an AI-generated draft while allowing them to personalize wording, add context, or make other changes before the message reaches the contact.

1. Review the AI Suggested Reply.
2. Tap **Edit**.
3. The suggested response loads into the message composer.
4. Make the required changes.
5. Send the edited message when ready.

While editing, you can restore the original AI suggestion if you want to undo your changes and return to the response initially generated by AI.

### **Dismiss and Restore an AI Suggestion**

Dismissing a suggestion temporarily clears it from view without preventing you from accessing it again. This is helpful when you want more room to compose your own response but may still want to reference the AI-generated reply.

After dismissing the suggestion, tap **Show AI suggestion** to display it again.

---

## **AI Suggestion Updates and Draft Preservation**

Incoming conversations can change while an agent is already preparing a response. Suggestive Mode keeps the newest AI-generated suggestion available while protecting text the agent has already entered into the composer.

When a new eligible inbound message results in a new AI reply, the suggestion updates to reflect the latest conversation. If you already have an unsent draft in the composer, HighLevel keeps that draft safe rather than replacing it with the new AI suggestion.

This allows you to choose whether to continue with your existing response or review the latest AI suggestion based on the newest contact message.

---

## **Eligibility and Availability for Mobile AI Suggested Replies**

Suggestion eligibility depends on both the mobile conversation and the underlying Conversation AI configuration. Confirming these requirements helps explain why an AI Suggested Reply may appear in one conversation but not another.

To use AI Suggested Replies on mobile:

- AI Employee must be using **Suggestive Mode**.
- Conversation AI must be configured and active.
- The relevant messaging channel or provider must be enabled for the bot.
- The conversation must be eligible for Conversation AI.
- The bot must not be in sleep or paused mode for the conversation.
- The mobile app must be updated to a supported version.

Conversation AI bots can be deployed to supported channels and connected destinations through their deployment settings. Current Conversation AI channel management supports channels including SMS, Email, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Live Chat, and Chat Widget, although individual feature availability can vary by channel.

For this mobile Suggested Reply release specifically:

- **Email suggestions are not available.**
- **Group chats are not supported.**
- **Internal chats are not supported.**
- Conversation AI must be enabled for the active channel or provider.
- Suggestions do not appear while the bot is sleeping.

> **Important:** General Conversation AI support for a channel does not necessarily mean that AI Suggested Replies are available for that channel in the mobile app.

---

## **Managing Conversation AI Settings on Web and Mobile**

Conversation AI configuration is divided between the web application and mobile conversations. Understanding where settings are managed helps teams avoid searching for configuration controls that are not available from mobile.

Core configuration—including creating a bot, selecting its response mode, training it, and configuring advanced behavior—is managed from the web application. HighLevel's current Conversation AI setup flow is available under **AI Agents > Conversation AI**.

The mobile app is designed primarily for working with Conversation AI inside active conversations. Existing HighLevel mobile controls also allow users to manage bot activity for individual conversations, while core setup remains on the web.

For more detailed bot configuration, see [How to Set Up a Conversation AI Bot](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004401?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

---

## **Suggestion ID and Troubleshooting**

A Suggestion ID helps identify a specific AI-generated response when troubleshooting unexpected behavior. Providing the identifier to support can make it easier to investigate the exact suggestion involved rather than relying only on screenshots or message text.

The Suggestion ID is available from the suggestion's information sheet in the mobile app.

When reporting an issue involving an AI Suggested Reply, capture the Suggestion ID along with relevant details about the conversation and the behavior you observed.

If suggestions are not appearing, verify that:

- The bot is configured in Suggestive Mode.
- Conversation AI is active.
- The relevant channel or provider is assigned to the bot.
- The bot is not sleeping or paused for that conversation.
- The conversation is not a group chat or internal chat.
- You are not attempting to use an Email suggestion in this release.
- Your mobile application is updated to a supported version.

Channel assignments determine where a Conversation AI bot can respond, and contact-level bot status can control whether the bot is active for an individual conversation.

---

## **How To Setup AI Employee Suggestive Mode for Mobile**

Proper setup ensures AI Employee can generate suggestions for the conversations and channels your team handles. Configure the bot and its deployment settings on the web first, then use the mobile app to review and send Suggested Replies.

1. On the HighLevel web application, go to **AI Agents > Conversation AI**.
2. Create a Conversation AI bot or open an existing bot.
3. Configure the bot for your business needs.
4. Set the bot's response mode to **Suggestive Mode**. HighLevel's Conversation AI setup supports Suggestive Mode as a response option for bots.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081643276/original/v35GhTwvW1XN9Xwrcf7J7s3Ls-aGySZavw.png?1790159717)
5. Configure the bot's deployment so the appropriate supported channels and destinations are assigned.
6. Save your Conversation AI configuration.
7. Open the mobile app and go to **Conversations**.
8. Open a conversation when an eligible inbound message arrives.
9. Review the AI Suggested Reply displayed above the composer.
10. Choose the appropriate action:

- Tap **Send** to send the response as written.
- Tap **Edit** to modify the suggestion before sending.
- Dismiss the suggestion if you do not want to use it immediately.
- Tap **Show AI suggestion** to restore a dismissed suggestion.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why don't I see an AI Suggested Reply in a mobile conversation?**

A: Confirm that the Conversation AI bot is using Suggestive Mode, the relevant channel or provider is enabled, the bot is active for the conversation, and the message is eligible. Suggestions also will not appear for Email, group chats, or internal chats in this release.

**Q: Can I recover an AI suggestion after dismissing it?**

A: Yes. Tap **Show AI suggestion** to display the dismissed suggestion again.

**Q: What happens if a new message arrives while I am writing my own reply?**

A: Your existing draft remains safe in the composer. If a new AI suggestion is generated from the latest inbound message, you can review it without losing the draft you were already writing.

**Q: Can I restore the original AI response after editing it?**

A: Yes. While editing an AI suggestion, you can restore the original suggestion with the available restore action.

**Q: Are AI Suggested Replies available for Email on mobile?**

A: No. Email suggestions are not available in this mobile release, even though Email can be supported by Conversation AI in other contexts.

**Q: Can I configure Suggestive Mode completely from the mobile app?**

A: No. Core Conversation AI setup, mode selection, bot training, and advanced configuration are managed from the web application. Mobile is used primarily to interact with Conversation AI inside conversations and manage supported conversation-level controls.

**Q: What should I provide to support if an AI suggestion behaves unexpectedly?**

A: Open the suggestion information sheet and locate the **Suggestion ID**. Provide that identifier along with details about the conversation and the behavior you experienced.

**Q: Does pausing or putting the bot to sleep affect AI Suggested Replies?**

A: Yes. Suggestions do not appear while the bot is inactive for the conversation. HighLevel supports managing Conversation AI status for individual contacts when the bot is operating in Suggestive or Auto-Pilot mode.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Use Conversation AI in the Mobile App (HighLevel & LeadConnector)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002669?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Conversation AI Bot Explained](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001335?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to Set Up a Conversation AI Bot](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004401?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to Manage Conversation AI Bot Channels and Routing](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008266-how-to-manage-conversation-ai-bot-channels-and-routing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Bot Status for Individual Contacts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004096?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Conversation AI - Advanced Settings Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004415?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title_en: Workflow Trigger - Payment received
source_md:
The Payment Received trigger is designed to act as a centralized mechanism for capturing all incoming payments across the CRM. It can be customized with filters to target specific use cases. This trigger helps businesses automate tasks, streamline processes, and efficiently respond to real-time customer transactions.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the Payment Received Workflow Trigger?](#What-is-the-Payment-Received-Workflow-Trigger?)
- [Key Benefits Of Payment Received Workflow Trigger](#Key-Benefits-Of-Payment-Received-Workflow-Trigger)
- [How to use the Payment Received Trigger](#How-to-use-the-Payment-Received-Trigger)
  - [Filters](#Filters)
  - [If/Else Conditions](#If/Else-Conditions)
  - [Custom Values](#Custom-Values)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Additional Benefits](#Additional-Benefits)

---

# **What is the Payment Received Workflow Trigger?**

The Payment Received trigger automates processes and actions based on incoming payments when used in a workflow. It can be configured to respond to all payment events across the CRM (ex: one-time purchases, subscription charges, invoices, etc), such as successful or failed transactions or particular products and payment sources.

The trigger starts a workflow instantly whenever a matching payment is received, allowing for automation of actions like sending confirmation emails, generating invoices, or updating customer records. Users can apply various filters to the trigger, such as transaction type, payment source, or product. This enables the creation of targeted workflows for specific scenarios, like subscription renewals, or failed payments.

By using if/else conditions in the Workflow, different actions can be executed in very specific situations depending on the payment characteristics, such as the amount, source, or transaction status. The workflow actions can also capture payment data for analysis and reporting purposes. By monitoring incoming payments and their attributes, businesses can gain insights into sales performance, customer behavior, and potential areas for improvement.

---

## **Key Benefits Of Payment Received Workflow Trigger**

The Payment Received trigger offers numerous usage cases and benefits, helping businesses automate processes, improve customer experience, and gain insights from payment data. Some common usage cases and their benefits include:

- **Automated payment confirmation:**Send customers automated confirmation emails or messages when Payment is processed, which enhances customer satisfaction.
- **Subscription management:**Automatically update subscription status in the system when a subscription payment is successful or failed, which increases business efficiency by streamlining subscription management.
- **Payment failure resolution:**Automatically notify customer support or sales teams to address and assist the Customer when a payment failure occurs; resolve payment issues quickly.

---

# **How to use the Payment Received Trigger**

[동영상](https://www.loom.com/embed/9775a0183c974473a87060eb410d39fb)

**Step 1:** Inside a workflow, add a workflow trigger called **Payment Received.**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155041535027/original/LuaYlXLD0wUPr6GAtd8O9TKuYMunxgXfEA.png?1739444985)

```
Click "add filter" to choose a filter. Then click "add filter" again to add the  Sub-filters.
```

---

## **Filters**

You can make your Workflow trigger more specific using filters. Here is a table of all the available filters and sub-filters.

| Trigger | Filter | Options at Filter Level | Sub-Filter Level 1 | Options at Sub-Filter Level 1 | Operators |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Payment Received | Payment Source | Invoice | Sub-Source | Text2Pay link | is, is not |
| One-time invoice |
| Recurring template |
| Funnel/ Website | Sub-Source | One-step order form |
| Two-step order form |
| Upsell |
| Transaction type | Customer present/first transaction |
| Customer not present/subscription transaction |
| Calendar | Calendar | Calendar names |
| Global Product | Global product Names | Price | Prices Names as per selected Global Product |
| Payment status | Success | --- | |
| Failed |

For example, if you want the workflow to trigger when a two-step order form is submitted, you select (1) Payment Source > (2) is > (3) Funnel and then you select add filter > (4) Sub-Source > (5) is > (6) two-step order form.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155038871990/original/jIbyU9wy4QW1uUfU59g0Oe0Lj9gvorYF8g.png?1735067718)

---

## **If/Else Conditions**

Once you have added your desired set of Filters and Sub-Filters to your workflow trigger, you can add an If/Else Condition for Payment if you need to branch out the Workflow based on certain conditions.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155041545885/original/t7AzOXeC_h2Ny9inaeFgWD2IvemRTkKBPw.gif?1739451375)

This Table explains the possible If/Else Conditions and their branches.

| If/Else Option | Action | Operator | Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Payment | Product | is, is not | Global product Names |
| Funnel/Website | Funnel/Website names |
| Calendar | Calendar names |
| Source | Invoice, Funnel, Website, Calendar |
| Payment status | success/failed |
| Amount | Equal to, is not equal to, Greater than, Greater than or equal to, Less than, Less than or equal to, is not empty, is empty. | Amount paid |

---

## **Custom Values**

After adding and configuring the Payment Received Workflow trigger, the workflow actions have access to a set of Custom Values that you can populate within SMS, Emails, Internal Notifications, etc. This Table explains the custom values in detail.

| Custom Values Category | Custom Values Name  (Custom Value Group Name) | Custom Values within Group | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Payment** | Source |  | {{payment.source}} |
| Currency Symbol | {{payment.currency\_symbol}} |
| Currency Code | {{payment.currency\_code}} |
| **Customer (**Custom Values Group) | ID | {{payment.customer.id}} |
| First Name | {{payment.customer.first\_name}} |
| Last Name | {{payment.customer.last\_name}} |
| Name | {{payment.customer.name}} |
| Email | {{payment.customer.email}} |
| Phone | {{payment.customer.phone}} |
| Full Address | {{payment.customer.address}} |
| City | {{payment.customer.city}} |
| State | {{payment.customer.state}} |
| Country | {{payment.customer.country}} |
| Postal Code | {{payment.customer.postal\_code}} |
| **Invoice**(Custom Values Group) | Name | {{payment.invoice.name}} |
| Number | {{payment.invoice.number}} |
| Issue Date | {{payment.invoice.issue\_date}} |
| Due Date | {{payment.invoice.due\_date}} |
| URL | {{payment.invoice.url}} |
| Recorded By | {{payment.invoice.recorded\_by}} |
| Sub-Total |  | {{payment.sub\_total\_amount}} |
| Discount Amount | {{payment.discount\_amount}} |
| Coupon Code | {{payment.coupon\_code}} |
| Tax Amount | {{payment.tax\_amount}} |
| Created On | {{payment.created\_on}} |
| Total Amount | {{payment.total\_amount}} |
| Transaction ID | {{payment.transaction\_id}} |
| Status | {{payment.payment\_status}} |
| Gateway | {{payment.gateway}} |
| Card Last 4 Digits | {{payment.card.last4}} |
| Card Brand | {{payment.card.brand}} |
| Method | {{payment.method}} |

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**What is the sub-source filter?**

When you select a source like funnels/websites/invoices, they can have sub-sources, like a payment from the funnel can be coming either via a one-step order form, a two-step order form, or an upsell. You can use these sub-source filters to define the Payment's origin.

**Will this trigger include the initial subscription payment and subsequent subscription payments as well?**

Yes, the trigger will fire whenever a payment is received from the end customer directly on an order form submission and when the subscription is charged in the background.

**What does the Customer present/first transaction mean and the Customer not present/subscription transaction?**

We are categorizing the transaction type into two categories

- **Customer present /first transaction** - This includes the transactions where the end customer is on-session and making the Payment. This consists of all one-time purchases and the first order placement for a subscription product.
- **Customer not present / subscription transaction** - This includes the transaction types which run in the background after a subscription has already been created. For example, if a customer purchases a recurring product with a 14-day trial period. The transaction is done while purchasing the recurring product ($0 transaction in this case) would fall into the Customer present/first transaction. After 14 days, when the trial period is over, and you charge $100 for the recurring product, the $100 transaction would fall into the Customer not present/subscription transaction category.

**How can I configure the trigger for successful subsequent subscription transactions?**

Since the subscriptions can be created in a funnel or website, we can create a trigger for Payment Received and apply the following filters for achieving the use case. The source type is Funnel/Website. The transaction type is "Customer not present/subscription transaction." The payment status filter can filter successful or failed payments per the use case.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155041546117/original/7l-LgbEmh0f0FKJXnSMQQaI9SLxv8aWYFw.png?1739451471)

**Will failed payments also be captured in this trigger?**

Yes, by default, without any filters, the trigger runs upon successful and failed payment attempts. For specific use cases around success/failed payments only, we can apply the "Transaction status" filter and set it to either success/failed as per the use case.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155041546210/original/xyXYNTCf_UL6-vTxallLYkcJpPrgJmeFpg.png?1739451511)

**I have configured the trigger and selected a specific product in the filters. Does this mean that the trigger will fire off when that product is sold anywhere?**

If you have configured the trigger and set the filter for a specific product, it will fire off only when that product is sold in funnels/website/invoices. Using the transaction status filter, we can define whether the trigger should work when the purchase is successful or the purchase is a failure.

---

## Additional Benefits

- **Dunning management:**Automatically trigger dunning email sequences for customers with failed subscription payments. Improves revenue recovery by addressing payment failures promptly, reduces churn, and enhances customer retention.
- **Customer segmentation:**Use payment data to create customer segments based on purchasing behavior, such as high-value customers or frequent buyers. Enables targeted marketing campaigns, helps identify upsell or cross-sell opportunities, and facilitates personalized customer experiences.
- **Sales performance tracking:**Monitor payment data to track sales performance and identify trends, such as best-selling products, seasonal fluctuations, or customer preferences. Provides valuable insights for strategic decision-making, helps optimize sales strategies, and drives revenue growth.
- **Integration with accounting systems:**Automatically update accounting records with payment information using outbound webhooks, such as invoicing, revenue recognition, or tax calculations. Ensures accurate financial reporting, streamlines accounting processes, and reduces manual data entry.
- **Handling trial period transactions:**The Payment Received trigger effectively manages transactions involving trial periods for subscription products, such as a 14-day trial. In this example, when a customer signs up for the trial and pays $0 upfront, the trigger categorizes this as a customer present transaction since they are on-session and entering their payment information. After the 14-day trial ends, the customer is charged $100 automatically without entering their payment details again. This subsequent transaction is considered a customer not present transaction, as it occurs in the background. The Payment Received trigger allows businesses to track and automate workflows around trial period transactions accurately. By efficiently handling trial period transactions, businesses can enhance customer experience, improve subscription management, and reduce manual intervention, increasing customer satisfaction and retention.
- **Integrating Text2Pay links:**The Payment Received trigger supports Text2Pay links as a payment source, enabling businesses to automate workflows for payments received through text message-based methods. By incorporating Text2Pay links in the trigger's configuration, businesses can effectively manage and respond to these transactions, improving the overall customer experience and streamlining payment processing. Utilizing Text2Pay links with the Payment Received trigger allows businesses to reach a wider audience, expedite payment processing, and simplify customer communication, ultimately leading to increased revenue and customer loyalty.

title_en: Assets Protected Snapshots ( Called "IP Protected" Earlier )
source_md:
Snapshots • Assets Protection • Internal Reuse

Assets Protected Snapshots (Called "IP Protected" Earlier)

Protect snapshot assets from external redistribution while allowing those assets to be reused across sub-accounts and snapshots within the same agency.

What You'll Learn

Assets Protected Snapshots allow protected assets to be reused within the same HighLevel agency while continuing to restrict external redistribution. This guide explains how protected assets behave when they are loaded into sub-accounts, used to create or refresh snapshots, included in mixed snapshots, and reviewed before external sharing.

Important

The protection boundary is the agency. **Inside the agency, protected assets can be reused.** When protected assets would leave the agency through external sharing or resale, they remain restricted.

# **What Are Assets Protected Snapshots?**

Assets Protected Snapshots help snapshot creators protect assets from unauthorized external redistribution while still allowing the receiving agency to use those assets in its normal internal snapshot workflows. Understanding where protection applies is important because protected assets are no longer blocked from reuse simply because they originated from another protected snapshot.

When Assets Protection is applied to a snapshot, the protected status stays attached to the applicable assets. A receiving agency can load and reuse those assets across its own sub-accounts and can include them when creating or refreshing snapshots for internal use.

The restriction is enforced when protected assets would leave that agency. Protected assets cannot be redistributed or resold to another agency, while eligible non-protected assets can still be shared.

If you are importing an asset-protected snapshot, see [How to Import Snapshots in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007995-how-to-import-snapshots-in-highlevel) for the complete import workflow.

## **Key Benefits of Assets Protected Snapshots**

Assets Protection gives agencies more flexibility to build with legitimately received assets without removing the safeguards established by the original snapshot creator. Internal snapshot workflows can continue normally while external redistribution controls remain in place.

- **Internal Reuse:** Reuse protected assets across sub-accounts and snapshots within the same agency.
- **Flexible Snapshot Building:** Include protected assets when creating or refreshing snapshots for internal use.
- **Creator Protection:** Keep protected assets restricted from being shared or resold to another agency.
- **Mixed Snapshot Sharing:** Share eligible non-protected assets even when the same snapshot also contains protected assets.
- **Pre-Share Visibility:** Review which assets can be shared and which will be excluded before completing an external share.
- **Persistent Protection:** Keep the protected status attached to assets as they move through internal snapshot workflows.

## **How Assets Protection Works**

Assets Protection separates internal reuse from external redistribution. The key boundary is the agency: protected assets can move through snapshot workflows inside the agency, but their protected status prevents them from being redistributed outside that agency.

| Scenario | Protected Asset Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Load into another sub-account in the same agency | **Allowed** |
| Reuse in another internal snapshot | **Allowed** |
| Create or refresh a snapshot using protected assets | **Allowed within the agency** |
| Share a snapshot to another agency | **Protected assets are excluded** |
| Resell a snapshot outside the agency | **Protected assets remain restricted** |
| Share a mixed snapshot | **Non-protected assets can be shared; protected assets are excluded** |

**Important:** Reusing a protected asset within your agency does not remove or change its protected status. The protection continues to follow the asset.

## **Reuse Protected Assets Within Your Agency**

Protected assets can participate in normal snapshot workflows throughout the same agency. This removes the previous internal-use restriction while preserving the protection that applies when the asset would be redistributed externally.

You can use protected assets to:

- Load a protected snapshot into your agency's sub-accounts.
- Reuse protected assets across multiple sub-accounts in the same agency.
- Create another snapshot from a sub-account containing protected assets.
- Include protected assets when refreshing an existing snapshot.
- Build internal snapshots that contain both protected and non-protected assets.

The protected status remains attached as the assets move through these internal workflows. Creating another snapshot from a sub-account does not make a protected asset externally redistributable.

![Snapshot list showing an indicator for a snapshot that contains protected assets](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079639457/original/SayeIS7KD2v9iLiKcpL_pBNxONlmmWLmhA.png?1788099028=)

## **Protected Assets in Mixed Snapshots**

A mixed snapshot contains both protected and non-protected assets. HighLevel evaluates each asset according to its protection status, which means protected content does not prevent eligible content from being shared.

- **Inside the agency:** Protected and non-protected assets can remain available for internal snapshot workflows.
- **Outside the agency:** Protected assets are excluded from the external share while eligible non-protected assets continue normally.

**Result:** A snapshot does not become completely unshareable simply because it contains one or more protected assets.

## **Review Protected Assets Before Sharing**

Reviewing a snapshot before it leaves your agency helps you understand which assets will be included in the external share. HighLevel identifies protected content before you continue so you can see what will be excluded.

If protected assets are present, the sharing experience provides a breakdown of the protected assets that cannot be shared and the eligible assets that can continue. You can expand asset groups to review individual items before proceeding.

![Pre-share review showing protected assets that will be excluded from an external snapshot share](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079639423/original/E7foOi4Auy87TrfEgsQWdNFHXG4a6NkMrA.png?1788098960=)
![Expanded pre-share asset list showing shareable and restricted asset statuses](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079639427/original/ynk1V7vKC42k6ZVMz8XJE7wwx_KblmGv4Q.png?1788098976=)

## **How To Set Up Assets Protected Snapshots**

Properly enabling Assets Protection ensures that recipients can use protected content inside their agency without being able to redistribute that protected content externally. The same protection remains attached when the assets are later used in internal Create or Refresh workflows.

### **Enable Assets Protection When Sharing a Snapshot**

Assets Protection is applied when you generate a protected share from the snapshot sharing workflow. Enabling it before distributing the snapshot establishes the protection that follows the assets after they are imported by the receiving agency.

1. From **Agency View**, go to **Account Snapshots > My Snapshots**.
2. Locate the snapshot you want to share.
3. Open the snapshot's action menu and select **Share Snapshot**.
4. Select the appropriate sharing option for the recipient.
5. Turn on **Assets Protected**.
6. Generate the share link.
7. Send the link to the intended recipient.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080790014/original/J98dDhBlRFMrf3IRwqjvrl0I4uXCbmdd9Q.png?1789242364)**

For additional information about snapshot share links and sharing options, see [How to Share Snapshots](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982513-how-to-share-snapshots).

### **Create or Refresh a Snapshot Using Protected Assets**

Protected assets no longer need to be removed when you create or refresh a snapshot for use inside your agency. The asset selector identifies protected content while still allowing it to be selected for the internal snapshot.

1. From **Agency View**, go to **Account Snapshots**.
2. Create a new snapshot or choose an existing snapshot to refresh.
3. Select the source sub-account or continue into the asset-selection step.
4. Review the available assets. Protected assets are identified with a shield indicator.
5. Select the protected and non-protected assets you want included for internal use.
6. Complete the **Create** or **Refresh** action.

The protected assets remain protected after they are included in the newly created or refreshed snapshot.

![Create Snapshot asset selector showing protected assets available for internal reuse](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079639340/original/jMp8PxMz9PzXRkG8mdI878WGVK59b5stOw.png?1788098876=)
![Refresh Snapshot asset selector showing protected assets available for internal reuse](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079639377/original/Ya9bCehwbJKeozSoXune6xDecnPI_ZKwtw.png?1788098897=)

For complete snapshot creation and refresh instructions, see [Creating New Snapshots in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982512-creating-new-snapshots-in-highlevel) and [Refresh or Update Snapshots](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982583-refresh-or-update-snapshots).

### **Share a Snapshot That Contains Protected Assets**

A snapshot does not become completely unshareable because protected content is present. When a mixed snapshot is shared outside your agency, HighLevel separates the protected assets from the eligible assets before the share is completed.

1. Open the snapshot sharing workflow.
2. Select the external sharing option you want to use.
3. Review the protected and shareable assets shown before continuing.
4. Confirm which assets will be excluded from the external share.
5. Continue with the share.

Protected assets remain behind and are not redistributed to the other agency. Eligible non-protected assets are included in the external share.

**No manual cleanup required:** You do not need to remove every protected asset from a mixed snapshot before sharing it externally.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

Q: Does a protected asset lose its protection after I copy it into another sub-account?

No. Protection continues to follow the asset as it moves between sub-accounts and snapshots within your agency.

Q: Can I create a new snapshot from a sub-account that contains assets from an imported protected snapshot?

Yes. Protected assets can be included when creating a new snapshot for use within your agency. Their protected status remains attached.

Q: Can I refresh an existing snapshot with protected assets?

Yes. Protected assets can be selected during a snapshot refresh for internal use, and refreshing the snapshot does not remove their protection.

Q: What happens if I share a snapshot that contains both protected and non-protected assets?

The snapshot can still be shared externally. Protected assets are excluded, while eligible non-protected assets are included in the share.

Q: Do I need to manually remove protected assets before externally sharing a mixed snapshot?

No. HighLevel identifies protected assets during the sharing process and excludes them from the external share.

Q: Can an agency that receives protected assets use them in more than one of its own sub-accounts?

Yes. After the protected snapshot is legitimately imported, the protected assets can be reused across sub-accounts and snapshots within that receiving agency.

Q: Can the receiving agency resell or share the protected assets with another agency?

No. The restriction is enforced when the protected assets would leave the receiving agency. Protected assets cannot be redistributed or resold to another agency.

Q: How can I tell which assets will be excluded before sharing a snapshot?

When protected assets are detected during external sharing, the review experience identifies the restricted assets and the assets that can be included. Review this list before continuing with the share.

### **Related Articles**

[Snapshots - Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982511) [Creating New Snapshots in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982512-creating-new-snapshots-in-highlevel) [How to Share Snapshots](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982513-how-to-share-snapshots) [How to Import Snapshots in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007995-how-to-import-snapshots-in-highlevel) [Load Snapshots Into Existing Sub-Account](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982582-load-snapshots-into-existing-sub-account) [Refresh or Update Snapshots](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982583-refresh-or-update-snapshots)

title_en: WhatsApp Template Builder Update and Dynamic Media URLs
source_md:
A rebuilt template builder with live phone preview, and media headers that resolve per contact at send time — so one approved template serves every contact's unique asset.

Send every customer their own invoice, ticket, or personalized image from a single template. No more cloning a template for every asset and waiting on Meta to approve each copy.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What's New](#whats-new)
- [Rebuilt Create and Edit Experience](#builder)
- [Live Phone Preview](#preview)
- [Dynamic Media URLs](#dynamic-media)
- [Personalized Images in Bulk](#bulk-images)
- [Where to Find It](#where-to-find)
- [How to Use Dynamic Media](#how-to-use)
- [Why This Matters](#why-it-matters)
- [Related Articles](#related-articles)

---

## **What's New**

The updated builder changes how templates are created and previewed, while dynamic media makes it possible to personalize the file sent to each contact.

- **Rebuilt builder** — Create templates using a guided two-step process, with a live phone preview while editing template details.
- **Live phone preview** — see exactly how the message lands on WhatsApp as you type, before Meta ever sees it.
- **Dynamic media URLs** — media header fields now accept custom fields and dynamic values that resolve per contact at send time.
- **Clear failure behavior** — invalid or empty resolved values fail clearly. No silent wrong media sent.

---

## **Rebuilt Create and Edit Experience**

The updated WhatsApp builder guides you through two steps: **Set up template**, followed by **Template details**. Configure the message content and review the live phone preview before submitting the template for approval.

### **Two-Step Template Creation**

First, choose the template category and type, then click **Next**. On the **Template details** screen, configure the name, language, header, body, variables, and optional buttons.

### **How to Create a WhatsApp Template**

Create a template from your HighLevel sub-account and review its content and sample values before submitting it to Meta.

1. Open the applicable HighLevel **Sub-Account** and select **Settings**.
2. Open **WhatsApp**, then **Templates**.
3. Click **Create Template**, then select **Blank Template**.
4. Under **Set up template**, choose the category and template type.
5. Click **Next**.

![Set up a WhatsApp template by choosing its category and type before selecting Next.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084666557/original/R6JJCW7idQGsC_dhUir_NCV_N478TIAYUA.png?1793476627)

6. Enter the **Template name** and select the **Language**.
7. Configure the header, message body, variables, and optional buttons.
8. Enter sample values for variables where required.
9. Review the **Live preview** and correct any validation errors.
10. Click **Submit for approval**.

### **How to Edit a WhatsApp Template**

Existing templates can be edited when their current status permits changes. Review the fields available in the editor before updating.

1. From the sub-account, select **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**.
2. Find the template and open its three-dot menu.
3. Select **Edit template**, if available.
4. Update the available fields and review the **Live preview**.
5. Click **Update**.

![WhatsApp template editor showing content fields, live preview, and Update action.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084666677/original/ZgFTmLQU0S-SIfeGA8mMMgbfZuxbDfOVvQ.png?1793477061)

### **Consistent Across Authoring Surfaces**

AI template generation now runs through the same builder end to end. The WhatsApp template builder opened from Reputation uses it too. One interface to learn, not three.

### **Create a WhatsApp Template With AI**

AI template creation uses the updated builder and live preview to help you prepare and refine a message before submission.

1. From the sub-account, open **Settings → WhatsApp** and select **Create AI Template**.
2. Complete the initial template setup and continue to **Generate template**.
3. Enter the **Business name**, select a **Language**, and **Describe your use case**.
4. Choose a **Tone** and optionally enable **Add Emoji**.
5. Review the generated content and live preview. Select **Generate again** if needed.
6. Make any necessary edits and click **Submit for approval**.

![Create a WhatsApp template with AI using the business name, use case, tone, and live preview.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084666687/original/Z0_m6osH_a682HriqGuzqxn4Dq2dbx79LA.png?1793477097)

**Note:** This update covers the Create / Edit builder. Template list and folder management shipped separately under a previous update.

---

## **Live Phone Preview**

The initial **Set up template** screen displays an **Example preview**. On the **Template details** screen, the **Live preview** updates as you edit the header, body, media, and buttons. Dynamic values may look different for each contact when the message is sent.

Catching a layout problem in the builder costs you seconds. Catching it after Meta approval costs you another approval cycle.

If the preview appears blank or is not updating, confirm you are in the updated builder via **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates → Create / Edit**.

---

## **Dynamic Media URLs**

Media header fields now accept custom fields and dynamic values — not just one static public URL. At send time the value resolves for that specific contact and Meta receives a concrete URL for that message.

### **One Template Instead of Many**

Previously, a different image or document meant a different template — and every new template goes to Meta for approval. Now a single approved template serves every contact's unique asset. The approved template stays the same; only the resolved URL varies.

### **Supported Sending Surfaces**

Dynamic media URLs are supported in WhatsApp template sending flows that accept media header values or overrides, including the surfaces below. Available mapping controls may differ by workflow.

- Workflows
- Conversations
- Bulk Actions
- Calendar Appointments
- Reputation Review Requests
- Missed Call Text Back

### **Clear Failure Behavior**

A dynamic value that resolves to a supported, publicly accessible media URL meets the media-access requirement, but other template and sending restrictions still apply. An invalid or empty resolved value can cause the message to fail instead of sending the intended media.

### **What Resolves Successfully vs. What Fails**

A valid media URL must be accessible to Meta without authentication. Use these examples to identify what needs to be corrected before retrying a send.

- A publicly reachable HTTPS URL containing a supported media file can be used when sending the template.
- Private Drive links or URLs that require a login — Meta cannot access them and the message will fail.
- An empty field — fails clearly with no silent wrong media sent.

If sending fails with a message such as **"please provide a valid public url"**, check the selected field mapping and the resolved value for that contact.

Confirm the value is not empty, points to supported media, and uses a publicly accessible URL that Meta can download without signing in.

---

## **Personalized Images in Bulk**

Pair dynamic media with an image personalization service like NiftyImages and a single bulk action renders a unique image for every recipient. Build the design once with a name placeholder, map the URL to a custom field, and let it resolve per contact at send time.

### **What Your Contacts Actually See**

Each recipient receives a version of the media generated from their own contact details, even though the approved WhatsApp template stays the same.

- **Shaun** opens WhatsApp to an image reading "Here's a special offer for you, Shaun."
- **Sana** gets the same design reading "Here's a special offer for you, Sana."
- **Alex** gets his. One template, one bulk send, thousands of individually rendered images.

The same approach works beyond names:

- Personalized discount codes
- Event tickets with the attendee's seat
- Course certificates with the recipient's name
- Renewal dates matched to each contact's subscription
- A product image matched to what that contact last bought

---

## **Where to Find It**

Use the appropriate entry point for standard template creation, AI generation, Reputation review requests, or missed-call responses.

| Surface | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Template Builder | Settings → WhatsApp → Templates → Create or Edit |
| AI Template Builder | Sub-Account → Settings → WhatsApp → Create AI Template |
| Reputation | Reputation → Settings → WhatsApp Requests → Open WhatsApp Template Builder |
| Missed Call Text Back | Settings → Phone System → Voice → Voicemail & Missed Call TextBack → Missed Call Text Back → Customize |

---

## **How to Use Dynamic Media**

Dynamic media works best when each contact's resolved URL is valid, publicly accessible, and matches the template's media type.

### **For per-contact documents (invoices, contracts, IDs)**

Use a contact-specific URL to provide each customer with the document that belongs to their record.

1. Store a publicly reachable HTTPS URL on a contact custom field.
2. In your template's media or header field, map to that custom field instead of pasting a fixed URL.
3. Send from a workflow, bulk action, or conversation. Each contact receives their own file.

### **Example: Use a Dynamic Media URL in the Builder**

The updated builder supports dynamic values inside media URLs. For example, a numbered placeholder in a personalized image URL can be mapped to a contact field.

1. Open the HighLevel **Sub-Account** and select **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**.
2. Create a template and continue to **Template details**.
3. Under **Header**, select **Image**, **Video**, or **Document**, as applicable.
4. Select **Media URL**.
5. Enter a publicly reachable HTTPS media URL with a supported numbered placeholder where needed.
6. Map the placeholder to the appropriate contact field using the variable mapping control.
7. Enter a sample value and review the **Live preview**.
8. Complete the template and click **Submit for approval**.

![Configure a dynamic media URL with a numbered placeholder, contact field mapping, and live preview.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084666752/original/X82gC5uvgd2V1cHstkPWPLyCvz6QA5htjg.png?1793477354)

In the illustrated example, the URL contains `{{1}}`, which is mapped to `{{contact.first_name}}` with a sample value for the preview.

A contact custom field can also store an entire public media URL. That is a separate use case from a numbered placeholder inside the URL; available mapping or override controls depend on the sending flow.

### **For personalized images at scale**

Create a single image design, then supply a dynamic URL so the image can be customized for each recipient.

1. Create your image design in a service like NiftyImages, with a placeholder for the contact's name or any other detail.
2. Use the personalized image URL as your media header value, with the contact's detail supplied dynamically via a custom field.
3. Run a bulk action. Every contact receives an image rendered just for them.

**Requirement:** The resolved value must be a publicly reachable URL that Meta can download. Private Drive links, URLs behind a login, and empty fields will fail.

---

## **Why This Matters**

Personalized media used to carry a hidden tax. Every variation meant another template, and every template meant another round of Meta approval before you could send anything. That made per-customer invoices, tickets, certificates, and personalized campaign images impractical for most businesses — so they either skipped them or built fragile workarounds.

- Run personalized image campaigns at bulk scale instead of sending the same flat creative to everyone.
- Send genuinely personalized documents without multiplying your template library.
- Skip the approval queue for asset changes — the approved template stays the same and only the resolved URL varies.
- Keep automations stable — workflows reference a dynamic value rather than a URL you hand-edit after every clone.
- Catch layout mistakes before Meta sees them, with a preview that matches the real message.

**Ready to try it?**

Open **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**, build one, and try a personalized image on your next bulk send.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [How to Create a WhatsApp Template](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000861)
- [WhatsApp Media Templates](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002330)
- [How to Use Custom Fields](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008031)
- [WhatsApp Template Statuses and Best Practice](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001623)
- [WhatsApp Template-Level Analytics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003714)

title_en: How to Setup 301 URL Redirects
source_md:
A 301 redirect permanently sends visitors and search engines from an old URL to a new destination. In HighLevel, you can create redirects for an entire domain or a specific URL path and send visitors to a custom URL, funnel step, or website page. 

This guide explains how to create and manage 301 redirects, when to use them, and how to troubleshoot common redirect issues.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is a 301 URL Redirect?](#What-is-a-301-URL-Redirect?)
- [Key Benefits of 301 URL Redirects](#Key-Benefits-of-301-URL-Redirects)
- [When Should You Use a 301 Redirect?](#When-Should-You-Use-a-301-Redirect?)
- [How to Set Up 301 Redirects in HighLevel](#How-to-Set-Up-301-Redirects-in-HighLevel)
  - [Step 1: Navigate to URL Redirects](#Step-1%3A%C2%A0Navigate-to-URL-Redirects)
  - [Step 2: Add a New Redirect](#Step-2%3A-Add-a-New-Redirect)
  - [Step 3: Select the Source Domain](#Step-3%3A%C2%A0Select-the-Source-Domain)
  - [Step 4: Choose What You Want to Redirect](#Step-4%3A%C2%A0Choose-What-You-Want-to-Redirect)
  - [Step 5: Select the Redirect Target](#Step-5%3A%C2%A0Select-the-Redirect-Target)
- [301 Redirect vs Canonical URL](#301-Redirect-vs-Canonical-URL)
- [Best Practices for 301 Redirects](#Best-Practices-for-301-Redirects)
- [Common Issues & Troubleshooting](#Common-Issues-&-Troubleshooting)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What is a 301 URL Redirect?**

A 301 URL redirect is a permanent redirect from one URL to another. It tells browsers and search engines that the original URL has moved permanently, helping visitors reach the correct page even if they click an old link. In HighLevel, 301 redirects can send traffic from a selected domain or path to a custom URL, funnel step, or website page.

A 301 redirect is commonly used when you rename a page, change a funnel or website path, move content to a different destination, or want an old URL to continue working after updates are made.

---

## **Key Benefits of 301 URL Redirects**

- **Improved visitor experience:** Sends visitors from old URLs to the correct destination automatically.
- **Reduced broken links:** Helps prevent 404 errors when pages are renamed, deleted, or moved.
- **SEO continuity:**Signals to search engines that a URL has permanently moved and helps preserve continuity when URLs are changed.
- **Domain consolidation:** Redirects traffic from one domain version to another, such as a `www` version to a root domain.
- **Flexible destination options:** Allows redirects to custom URLs, funnel steps, or website pages in HighLevel.

---

## **When Should You Use a 301 Redirect?**

Use a 301 redirect when a URL has permanently changed and visitors should automatically be sent to a new destination.

Common scenarios include:

- Renaming a funnel step or website page path
- Moving content to a different URL
- Replacing or deleting a page while preserving traffic from existing links
- Migrating content to another domain
- Redirecting an old campaign or landing-page URL to a current page
- Consolidating domain versions when one URL should permanently point to another

> **Note:** If multiple URLs should remain accessible but you only want search engines to recognize one as the preferred version, consider using a canonical URL instead of a 301 redirect.

---

## **How to Set Up 301 Redirects in HighLevel**

Follow these steps to configure 301 redirects for your domains:

### **Step 1:**Navigate to URL Redirects

1. Go to **Settings** > **Domains & URL Redirects**.
2. At the top of the page, select the **URL Redirects** tab. This opens the redirect management view where you can create, search, edit, or delete redirects.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/fjz9BYWVCmnfkIqeeTxq+/GIF+Recording+2026-06-18+at+17.19.48.gif)

### **Step 2:** Add a New Redirect

1. Click **+ Add Redirect** in the top-right corner.

   If there are no existing redirects, you may also see an option to add your first redirect from the main redirect screen.
2. The **Add Redirect** setup window will open.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/BypLYCyFq3lrw5qXbNhi+/GIF+Recording+2026-06-18+at+18.10.26.gif)

### **Step 3:** Select the Source Domain

```
Note: Source domain must already be added to your HighLevel sub-account.
```

1. Under the **Source** section, click the **Redirect From** dropdown.
2. Select the domain you want to redirect from.

   The dropdown will show the domains currently available in your account.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/O1tsuhiz8XnXJQShOVwP+/Screenshot+2026-06-18+at+18.11.54.png)

### **Step 4:** Choose What You Want to Redirect

After selecting the source domain, choose whether you want to redirect the entire domain or only a specific path.

You can choose one of the following options:

**Option 1:** Redirect a Specific Path

Select this option if you only want to redirect one page or path from the domain.

For example, if you want to redirect: `yourdomain.com/contact`you would enter the specific path, such as:

`/contact`

Use this option for pages like a home page, contact page, thank-you page, or any other individual page.

```
Important: Avoid Special Characters in Redirect Paths

When creating a redirect for a specific path, do not include special characters such as ?, %, &, =, or # in the redirect path. These characters can prevent the redirect from working as expected.

For the most reliable redirect paths, use clean URL slugs containing lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens (-), and forward slashes (/) for supported nested paths.

Nested paths: HighLevel supports nested URL paths. When creating redirects for nested pages, enter the complete supported path, such as /resources/guides/getting-started.

Recommended: /special-offer

Avoid: /special?offer=summer&utm_source=email

If your original URL contains query parameters, enter the clean URL path rather than including the query string when configuring the redirect.
```

**Option 2:** Redirect the Entire Domain

Select this option if you want the whole domain to redirect to another destination.

For example, all traffic from: `yourdomain.com`would be redirected to the target you select.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/Ua1jVlxEuUOqaZ5if6BL+/Screen+Shot+2026-06-18+at+18.19.01.png)

### **Step 5:** Select the Redirect Target

Under the **Target** section, choose where you want visitors to be redirected.

You can redirect users to one of the following destination types:

**Option 1:** Custom URL

Use this option if you want to redirect visitors to any external or custom URL.

1. Select **Custom URL**.
2. Enter the full destination URL.
3. Click **Add Redirect**.

For example, you can redirect users to a thank-you page, external website, or any other URL.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/DWSZTFL7e5eXxvd35cJR+/GIF+Recording+2026-06-18+at+18.29.10.gif)

**Option 2:** Funnel

Use this option if you want to redirect visitors to a funnel connected to the selected domain.

1. Select **Funnel**.
2. Choose the funnel from the dropdown.

   Only funnels linked to the selected domain will appear.
3. Select the funnel step where you want visitors to land.

   You can select only one funnel step at a time.
4. Click **Add Redirect**.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/3tD1Jh3Xe2dEVvJPDuIP+/GIF+Recording+2026-06-18+at+18.31.06.gif)

**Option 3:** Website

Use this option if you want to redirect visitors to a website page connected to the selected domain.

1. Select **Website**.
2. Choose the website from the dropdown.

   Only websites linked to the selected domain will appear.
3. Select the website page where you want visitors to land.
4. Click **Add Redirect**.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/ZoRHwjsNLXcQXTCpWTJd+/GIF+Recording+2026-06-18+at+18.33.36.gif)

---

## **301 Redirect vs Canonical URL**

Use a 301 redirect when the old URL should no longer be used and visitors should automatically reach the new destination. Use a canonical URL when multiple URLs remain accessible but search engines should treat one as the preferred version.

| Use | 301 Redirect | Canonical URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visitors should automatically go somewhere else | **Yes** | No |
| Old URL should permanently move to a new URL | **Yes** | No |
| Multiple URLs should remain accessible | No | **Yes** |
| Tell search engines which accessible URL is preferred | Indirectly through the move | **Yes** |
| Browser URL changes | **Yes** | No |

---

## **Best Practices for 301 Redirects**

- **Use absolute URLs** (e.g., https://newsite.com/page) to prevent errors.
- ****Avoid redirect chains:****Redirect the original URL directly to the final destination whenever possible. For example, avoid `Page A → Page B → Page C`. Instead, configure `Page A → Page C`.
- Check for broken redirects regularly to ensure they work properly.

---

## **Common Issues & Troubleshooting**

| Issue | What to Check |
| --- | --- |
| **Redirect isn't working** | Confirm the source domain is connected and the source path exactly matches the URL being accessed. |
| **Redirect loop** | Make sure the destination does not redirect back to the source URL. |
| **404 after changing a page path** | Confirm a redirect exists from the old path to the new page and that the destination page is published. |
| **Funnel isn't available as a target** | Confirm the funnel is linked to the selected source domain. |
| **Website isn't available as a target** | Confirm the website is linked to the selected source domain. |
| **Specific path redirect fails** | Remove query parameters or unsupported special characters and use the clean URL path. |
| **Unexpected redirect behavior** | Check for other redirects that may affect the same source or destination. |
| **Google still shows the old URL** | Search engines may need time to recrawl the page. Use Google Search Console to inspect/request indexing where appropriate. |

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What is a 301 redirect?**

A 301 redirect is a permanent redirect from one URL to another. It helps send visitors and search engines to the correct webpage when a URL has changed.

**Q: Can I edit or delete a redirect after creating it?**Yes. Return to **Settings** > **Domains & URL Redirects** > **URL Redirects** to manage existing redirects.

**Q: Why should I use 301 redirects?**

301 redirects help preserve SEO rankings, prevent broken links, improve the visitor experience, consolidate domain versions, and ensure outdated links still lead to relevant pages.

**Q: Does the source domain need to be added to HighLevel first?**

Yes. The domain you are redirecting from must already be added to your HighLevel sub-account before you can create a redirect for it.

**Q: Can I redirect an entire domain?**

Yes. When creating a redirect, you can choose to redirect the entire domain so all traffic from that domain is sent to the selected target destination.

**Q: Can I redirect only one specific page or path?**

Yes. You can choose to redirect a specific path if you only want one page or URL path to redirect. For example, you can redirect yourdomain.com/test-one by entering the specific path, such as test-one.

**Q: What target options are available for redirects?**

You can redirect visitors to a Custom URL, a Funnel step, or a Website page. Funnel and website options only show items linked to the selected domain.

**Q. Should I use a 301 redirect or canonical URL?**

Use a 301 redirect when visitors should permanently move from an old URL to a new destination. Use a canonical URL when multiple URLs remain accessible but one should be treated as the preferred version by search engines.

**Q. Should I create a redirect after changing a funnel or website page path?**

Yes, if the previous URL was already being used. A redirect helps visitors using old links reach the new page and avoids sending them to an unavailable URL. HighLevel's nested-path documentation specifically recommends adding a 301 redirect after changing a live URL.

**Q: Why is my funnel or website not showing in the redirect target dropdown?**

Funnels and Websites that are linked with a domain are only listed.

**Q: What can cause redirect issues?**

Common issues include redirect loops, 404 errors, and slow load times. To avoid these, make sure you are not redirecting a URL to itself, confirm the target page exists, and avoid using too many redirects.

**Q: What are some best practices for setting up 301 redirects?**

Use absolute URLs, avoid redirect chains, check for broken redirects regularly, and use REGEX redirects carefully to prevent incorrect redirects.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Troubleshooting URL Indexing Issues in Funnels](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004789)
- [Nested URL Paths Support for Websites, Funnels, Ecomm & Webinars](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005779)
- [How to Add a Domain and Verify DNS Record](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002220)
