title_en: Automate Community Group Access with Workflows
source_md:
Communities • Workflows • Access Automation

Automate Community Group Access with Workflows

HighLevel Workflows can automate how Community group access is monitored, granted, and revoked. Group-access triggers start automation after a member gains or loses access, while group-access actions let a workflow make the access change. This makes it easier to automate onboarding, follow-up communication, access removal, and other Community processes. This guide explains when to use each trigger and action and how to configure both workflow patterns.

What You'll Learn

Learn the difference between Community group-access triggers and actions, create workflows that respond to access changes, automate granting or revoking access, distinguish group access from join requests and private channels, and test workflows before publishing them.

Important

**Group Access Granted** and **Group Access Revoked** respond after a member's access changes. They are different from **Requested to Join Group**, which is designed for pending membership requests before access is approved. Private channel access also uses separate Community workflow triggers and actions.

# What Is Community Group Access Automation?

Community group access automation connects HighLevel Communities with the Workflow Builder. A workflow can either respond when a member's group access changes or change the member's group access as part of a larger automated journey.

The key distinction is whether the access event should **start** the workflow or whether the workflow should **perform** the access change.

| Type | Name | What It Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Trigger** | **Group Access Granted** | Starts a workflow after a member is granted access to a Community group. |
| **Trigger** | **Group Access Revoked** | Starts a workflow after a member's access to a Community group is revoked. |
| **Action** | **Grant Group Access** | Grants a contact access to a specified Community group during workflow execution. |
| **Action** | **Revoke Group Access** | Removes a contact's access to a specified Community group during workflow execution. |

**Quick rule:** Use a trigger when the access change should start automation. Use an action when the workflow should make the access change.

## Key Benefits of Community Group Access Automation

Automating Community access reduces repetitive administrative work and lets group membership become part of a larger customer journey managed through HighLevel Workflows.

- **Automated Onboarding:** Grant Community group access after another qualifying event in the customer journey.
- **Automated Access Removal:** Revoke group access when workflow conditions require it.
- **Access-Based Follow-Up:** Start communication or internal actions after group access is granted or removed.
- **Consistent Access Management:** Apply the same access logic across qualifying contacts.
- **Connected Automation:** Combine Community access with other supported HighLevel workflow triggers, conditions, and actions.

## Prerequisites and Limitations

Identifying whether your automation should respond to an access change or make the access change helps you select the correct Community workflow component before building the rest of the workflow.

Before you begin:

- Create or identify the Community group you want the workflow to monitor or manage.
- Decide whether the workflow should **respond to** an access change or **perform** the access change.
- Identify the event or condition that should cause the contact to enter the workflow.
- Use a representative test contact before publishing the workflow for broader use.

Keep these access types separate:

- **Granted/Revoked Access:** Group Access Granted and Group Access Revoked respond after an access change occurs.
- **Access Actions:** Grant Group Access and Revoke Group Access change the contact's group access during the workflow.
- **Pending Join Requests:** Use Requested to Join Group when automation should begin from a membership request before access is approved.
- **Private Channels:** Private channel access has its own separate grant/revoke triggers and actions.

## Community Group Access Triggers and Actions

Each Community access trigger or action represents a different point in the member journey. Choosing the correct one determines whether the workflow listens for a group-access event or actively changes group access.

### Group Access Granted

**Group Access Granted** is a Community workflow trigger. It starts the workflow after a member receives access to the selected group. Use it when receiving access should begin another process, such as a welcome message, internal notification, tagging sequence, or another supported workflow action.

### Group Access Revoked

**Group Access Revoked** is a Community workflow trigger. It starts the workflow after a member's access to the selected group is removed. Use it when losing access should begin follow-up automation.

### Grant Group Access

**Grant Group Access** is a Community workflow action. It grants the workflow contact access to a selected Community group. Use it when another qualifying workflow event should result in Community group access.

### Revoke Group Access

**Revoke Group Access** is a Community workflow action. It removes the workflow contact's access to the selected Community group. Use it when another workflow event or condition should result in that access being removed.

## How To Create a Group Access Trigger Workflow

A group-access trigger workflow responds after access has already been granted or revoked. Use this setup when an access change should automatically start follow-up communication, internal processing, or another workflow action.

### Step 1: Create the Workflow

Start with a new workflow so the Community access event can serve as the enrollment trigger.

1. From the **Sub-Account View**, click **Automation**.
2. Select **Workflows**.
3. Click **+ Create workflow**.
4. Select **Start from Scratch**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081371537/original/HyT5J-vz4MuLa_D-hMjWYNDW3BtsByxDbA.png?1789849627)

### Step 2: Add the Community Access Trigger

Choose the access event that should enroll the member into the workflow and select the Community group the automation should monitor.

1. Click **+ Add**.
2. Select **Add trigger**.
3. Search for and select **Group Access Granted** or **Group Access Revoked**.
4. Configure the trigger for the Community group you want to monitor.
5. Save the trigger configuration.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081371465/original/pYr-GsCn44eaP0-rbvCkNKrCG9hTHZ0nJQ.png?1789849485)

### Step 3: Add Follow-Up Actions

Follow-up actions determine what should happen after HighLevel detects the group-access event.

1. Click the **+** icon after the trigger.
2. Select and configure the next workflow action.
3. Add any additional conditions, communications, or actions required for the process.

### Step 4: Test and Publish

Testing with a representative contact helps confirm that the workflow follows the expected path before it is made active for qualifying contacts.

1. Review the trigger and all workflow actions.
2. Click **Test workflow**.
3. Select an appropriate test contact.
4. Click **Run test** and confirm the expected workflow behavior.
5. When the workflow is ready, switch it from **Draft** to **Publish**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081371469/original/bsG86aZlmBn3gbV1ePYdLFzfSvPhWKTCoA.png?1789849500)

**Draft vs. Publish:** Saving workflow changes does not make the automation live. A workflow in Draft does not run for qualifying contacts until it is published.

## How To Grant or Revoke Group Access with a Workflow

Grant and revoke actions let another qualifying event in HighLevel determine whether a contact receives or loses Community group access. The trigger starts the customer journey, and the Community action changes the access.

### Step 1: Choose the Workflow Trigger

The workflow can begin from any supported trigger appropriate for your use case. Choose the event that should determine when HighLevel evaluates the contact for the group-access change.

1. Go to **Automation → Workflows**.
2. Create a new workflow or open an existing one.
3. Add and configure the trigger that should enroll the contact.
4. Save the trigger configuration.

### Step 2: Add the Group Access Action

Add the Community action that matches the access change you want the workflow to perform.

1. Click **+ Add** below the trigger or previous workflow step.
2. Select **Add action**.
3. Search for **Grant Group Access** or **Revoke Group Access**.
4. Select the appropriate Community action.
5. Select the Community group whose access should be granted or revoked.
6. Save the action configuration.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081371598/original/NBMlyU-4_ZpNkWqomKFxMBAdgo0KoAHHUg.png?1789849851)

### Step 3: Complete, Test, and Publish the Workflow

Complete the rest of the customer journey, then verify the group-access result before publishing the workflow.

1. Add any additional workflow steps required for the process.
2. Review the selected Community group and access action.
3. Use **Test workflow** with an appropriate contact where applicable.
4. Confirm the expected group-access change occurs.
5. Switch the workflow from **Draft** to **Publish** when it is ready to run.

## Best Practices for Group Access Workflows

Clear trigger logic, descriptive naming, and controlled testing make Community access workflows easier to understand and reduce unintended membership changes.

- **Separate Triggers from Actions:** Use Group Access Granted or Revoked when an access event should start automation. Use Grant or Revoke Group Access when the workflow should make the change.
- **Confirm the Correct Group:** Review the selected Community group in every trigger and action before publishing.
- **Use Descriptive Workflow Names:** Include the access event and Community group in the workflow name so its purpose is easy to identify.
- **Test with Representative Events:** Test both the workflow enrollment and the resulting access state before broad rollout.
- **Avoid Unintended Automation Loops:** If one workflow changes group access and another workflow starts from that same access change, review the combined journey so contacts are not repeatedly routed through conflicting access actions.
- **Use the Correct Join-Request Trigger:** Use Requested to Join Group when the automation should begin before a pending member is approved.
- **Keep Private Channel Logic Separate:** Use the dedicated private-channel triggers and actions when the workflow manages access to a private channel rather than the entire group.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is the difference between Group Access Granted and Grant Group Access?

**Group Access Granted** is a workflow trigger that starts automation after access is granted. **Grant Group Access** is a workflow action that grants access while the contact is moving through a workflow.

Q: What is the difference between Group Access Revoked and Revoke Group Access?

**Group Access Revoked** starts a workflow after group access is removed. **Revoke Group Access** is an action that removes the contact's access during workflow execution.

Q: Can I automate requests to join a Community group?

Yes. Use the separate **Requested to Join Group** trigger when automation should start from a pending membership request. This workflow pattern can use the selected group and configured membership-question responses before access is granted.

Q: Can I send a notification after someone receives or loses group access?

Yes. Use **Group Access Granted** or **Group Access Revoked** as the trigger, then add the supported notification or communication action required by your workflow.

Q: Can another workflow event automatically grant or revoke Community group access?

Yes. Configure the supported event that should start the workflow, then add **Grant Group Access** or **Revoke Group Access** as the Community action.

Q: Do these triggers and actions manage private Community channels?

No. Private channel access uses separate **Private Channel Access Granted**, **Private Channel Access Revoked**, **Grant Private Channel Access**, and **Revoke Private Channel Access** workflow options.

title_en: Voice intelligence
source_md:
Voice Intelligence

Automatic call summaries, QA scores, field suggestions and dispositions after every recorded call.

Overview

Every call ends with work to do. You write notes, update the contact and log how the call went. Voice Intelligence does this for you after each recorded call, so your team can move on to the next one.

Labs Feature

Voice Intelligence is a Labs feature. We are still improving it, and your feedback helps.

## What you get after each call

| Result | What it gives you |
| --- | --- |
| Call summary | Why the contact called, the key points and the next steps. No more typing notes. |
| QA scorecard | A score out of 10, a score for each area you care about, and tips on what to do better. |
| Field suggestions | Contact details mentioned on the call, like a name or email, ready to save. |
| Call disposition suggestion | The call outcome, picked from your own disposition list. |
| Transcript | Every word of the call, split by speaker, next to the recording. |

You Stay in Control

Nothing changes on a contact until someone on your team approves it.

## Before you start

**Turned on in Labs** — Voice Intelligence must be turned on for your account in Labs.

**Call recording is on** — Voice Intelligence only works on recorded calls.

**LeadConnector numbers** — it works on calls made and received with LeadConnector phone numbers.

**Real conversations only** — it skips unanswered calls and very short calls. See [Which calls get Voice Intelligence](#section-3).

**No extra charge** — there is no charge beyond your usual call transcription. Hover on **"Charges apply"** on the settings page for details.

## Which calls get Voice Intelligence

Voice Intelligence works on any recorded call that uses one of your LeadConnector phone numbers. It doesn't matter where the call is answered or made.

| Call type | Supported? |
| --- | --- |
| Web app and dialer | Yes |
| Mobile app | Yes |
| Desk phones (SIP) | Yes |
| Calls forwarded to another phone (e.g. a cell phone) | Yes. The call still goes through your LeadConnector number, so it is recorded. |
| Voice AI calls | Yes, when call recording is on for that number. The summary, scorecard and suggestions cover the call your Voice AI agent handled. |
| IVR calls and calls placed by a workflow | Yes, when they are recorded. |
| Voicemails left for you | Yes. You get a summary of who called, why, and whether they asked for a call back. |
| Your calls that reach a voicemail greeting | Yes. The summary says the call went to voicemail, and the suggested disposition is your voicemail option if your list has one. |

Not Covered

These calls don't get Voice Intelligence:

- Calls made from a personal phone outside the app, because they don't use your LeadConnector number.
- Calls on phone numbers connected from another phone provider.
- Calls on numbers where call recording is off.
- Calls that weren't answered, and calls too short to have real content, like a hang-up after a few words.

Where You See the Results

It depends on where the call happened

Every result is saved on the call in the contact's conversation.

- **Calls in the web app dialer:** the results open in the dialer as soon as the call ends. Confirm the disposition and save field suggestions right away.
- **Desk phone, forwarded, Voice AI, IVR and workflow calls:** there is no screen to review during the call. Open the contact's conversation, then select **View full details** on the call. You can check and save field suggestions there at any time.

Good to Know

On calls outside the web app dialer, the suggested disposition shows as a tag on the call, marked with a sparkle icon. You can see it in Conversations, but you can't change or save it there.

Setup Guide

Turn it on and tailor it to your team

Enable Voice Intelligence, then shape the summary, scorecard, fields, dispositions and language.

## Turn on Voice Intelligence

1. Go to **Settings → Phone System**.
2. Select the **Voice** tab, then **Call Recording & Transcription**.
3. Select **Voice Intelligence** on the left.
4. Turn on the **Voice intelligence** switch.

The transcript and the call summary are always included. Under **Additional features**, check the boxes for the QA scorecard, field suggestions and call disposition suggestions you want.

On by Default

All three additional features are on by default.

![Voice Intelligence settings with the main switch and Additional features checkboxes](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253509/original/QziPHPwucvDhSluueKhPM5mPhDHP8TXihA.png?1793049521)

## Make it fit your business

Admins set Voice Intelligence up once, and every call follows it.

Note

Changes apply to new calls only. Past calls keep their results.

Customize 1

Choose what goes in the call summary

1. Next to the summary line, select **Configure**.
2. You see the summary sections. By default these are Summary, Next steps, Key points, and Concerns and objections.
3. To change a section, select the edit icon. You can change its name, its description and its format: a single sentence, a bullet list or a short paragraph.
4. To add a section, select **Add section**. To remove one, select the **X**. Drag sections to change their order.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Tip

The description tells Voice Intelligence what to write. Keep it short and specific, for example *"Each objection the contact raised and how the agent answered it."*

![Call summary configuration showing the default sections](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253513/original/1wYvKALo8vy2y7MSJOoAqc2vS0doZuQSoA.png?1793049524)
![Editing a summary section's name, description and format](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253514/original/wqVtig59as_MnffnoNYT0cqvyxWfDnWabw.png?1793049524)

Customize 2

Score calls on what matters to you

1. Next to **QA scorecard**, select **Configure**.
2. You see the scoring categories. By default these are Greeting and introduction, Understanding the need, Clear answers, Handling concerns, and Closing and next step.
3. Edit a category to change its name or description. The description says what a good call looks like, so match it to your call script.
4. Select **Add category** to add one, or select the **X** to remove one. Drag to change the order.
5. Select **Save changes**.

How Scoring Works

Each category gets a score from 0 to 10, and the overall score is the average. If a category doesn't come up on a call, it is skipped, not counted as 0.

![QA scorecard configuration showing the default categories](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253519/original/gpfooaBEICQkbjA0Kvtm1kbjUzEh7cqe8w.png?1793049525)

Customize 3

Pick which contact fields to fill in

1. Next to **Field suggestions**, select **Configure**.
2. You see each contact field and its instruction. By default these are First Name, Last Name and Email.
3. Select **Add field** and choose any contact field, including your own custom fields. Then write a short instruction, for example *"The contact's budget in US dollars. Leave empty if not mentioned."*
4. Turn on **Only suggest values for empty fields** if you never want to replace data a contact already has.
5. Select **Save changes**.

![Field suggestions configuration with field instructions](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253520/original/5_KIAL8QaO47R7w2s1JvyyIqMg3M_Wp7BA.png?1793049527)

Customize 4

Use your own call outcomes

Voice Intelligence picks the call disposition only from your own list. To change the list, select **Manage list** next to **Call disposition suggestions**. This opens the **Custom Dispositions** tab.

![Call disposition suggestions with the Manage list link](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253511/original/v0hsG-Y_TJ6hjW9T4VEfzKk9Ob3OOz7cIg.png?1793049522)

Customize 5

Choose the language of your results

Under **Settings**, pick an **Output language**. Summaries, notes and other results are written in this language.

![Output language setting](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253512/original/4GG5fVUHep7sswE5pOSWSGNK5__kEfmC0w.png?1793049523)

## See the results in Conversations

1. Open the contact's conversation. After a call, the call card shows the start of the summary.
2. Select **View full details**.
3. Use the tabs to see the **Summary**, **Field suggestion**, **QA scorecard**, and **Recording & transcript**. The top of the window shows the call disposition and the overall score.

Timing

Results are usually ready a few seconds after the call recording is saved.

![Call card in Conversations showing the start of the summary](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253521/original/IctsbV0eGoW57XTJhi4aaH4eJJPVQHfH4g.png?1793049528)
![Full call details with the Summary tab](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253522/original/GnPfcUSxDEUEl91Krx0QwK5TGOEyxIXUdQ.png?1793049529)
![QA scorecard tab with category scores](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253525/original/j-7R8vpkjvRVcmos4C0-w4TgWOPRFeQI3g.png?1793049530)
![Recording and transcript tab](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253528/original/DpD7MOPuvLQviJOxzGfH6caT72_jMOUDyg.png?1793049531)

Then

Save field suggestions to the contact

1. Open the **Field suggestion** tab.
2. Check each value you want to keep. You can edit a value before you save it.
3. Select **Save Updates**. Only the checked values are saved to the contact.

![Field suggestion tab with values ready to save](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253531/original/AVvqd3QETU2wu3UOPYl8hKo8w-6pf2iTMw.png?1793049532)

## See the results in the dialer

When a call ends in the dialer, the results open next to the call summary. The **Review & update** tab shows the suggested call disposition and the suggested contact fields.

1. Check the disposition. Pick a different one from the list if needed.
2. Check the field values you want to keep, and edit them if needed.
3. Select **Save Updates**.

The **QA scorecard**, **Summary** and **Recording & transcript** tabs show the same results as in Conversations.

![Review and update tab in the dialer after a call](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084253535/original/zbZJJ9iL1sWQ_l_oQUKEruI_Zy3KLqqlVQ.png?1793049533)

You're All Set

Review, tweak if needed, save, and move straight on to your next call.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Why didn't a call get any results?

Check that:

- Call recording was on for that phone number.
- The call used a LeadConnector phone number.
- Voice Intelligence was on when the call happened. It does not run on older calls.
- The call was answered and long enough to have real content. Very short calls are skipped.

Results can also take a few seconds after the call. Refresh the page and try again.

Q: Does Voice Intelligence change my contacts on its own?

No. Field suggestions and the call disposition wait for someone on your team to check and save them.

Q: If I change my settings, do older calls change?

No. New settings apply to new calls only.

Q: Can I turn off a feature I don't need?

Yes. Uncheck the QA scorecard, field suggestions or call disposition suggestions in settings. The transcript and summary are always included while Voice Intelligence is on.

Q: Can I use my own custom fields?

Yes. When you add a field under **Field suggestions**, you can choose any contact field, including custom fields.

Q: Can I edit the suggested disposition from Conversations?

Not for calls outside the web app dialer. There it shows as a tag with a sparkle icon that you can see but not change or save. For calls in the web app dialer, confirm or change it in the **Review & update** tab.

Q: Does Voice Intelligence cost extra?

No. There is no charge beyond your usual call transcription. Hover on **"Charges apply"** on the settings page for details.

Tell Us How We Did

Each tab asks if the result is accurate. Select the thumbs up or thumbs down. Your feedback helps us make Voice Intelligence better.

title_en: How to Share Snapshots
source_md:
Snapshots • Sharing • Assets Protection

How to Share Snapshots

Share reusable Snapshot configurations with the right recipients, choose the appropriate link type, and control how protected assets behave when a Snapshot crosses agency boundaries.

What You'll Learn

Snapshot sharing lets agencies distribute reusable configurations through controlled share links without rebuilding assets manually. This guide explains the available link types, Assets Protection, mixed Snapshots, protected-asset review, and how Snapshot sharing differs from SaaS provisioning.

You'll also learn how sharing, importing, and loading work together and what to do when you need to distribute an updated Snapshot.

Important

Sharing, importing, and loading are different Snapshot actions. **Sharing** generates access to a Snapshot, **importing** adds a shared Snapshot to the recipient's agency-level Snapshot library, and **loading** applies selected Snapshot assets to a sub-account.

# What is Snapshot Sharing?

Snapshot Sharing is the process of generating a share link or invitation that gives another recipient access to a reusable Snapshot. A Snapshot can contain selected configuration assets such as workflows, funnels, forms, templates, calendars, and other supported account settings.

When another agency receives a share link, it imports the Snapshot into its agency-level Snapshot library. The imported Snapshot can then be loaded into the appropriate sub-account according to the access and restrictions associated with the share.

Share-link options let you control who can access a Snapshot, whether the link can be reused, and whether Assets Protection should restrict protected content from being redistributed outside the receiving agency.

## Key Benefits of Snapshot Sharing

Snapshot sharing makes repeatable configurations easier to distribute while giving agencies control over recipient access and protected content. Choosing the right sharing method helps balance speed, consistency, and protection.

**Faster Deployment:** Distribute proven workflows, funnels, templates, and other configurations without rebuilding them manually.

**Consistency:** Give recipients access to standardized configurations that can be imported and reused.

**Controlled Access:** Choose reusable, single-use, agency-restricted, or sub-account-restricted sharing methods.

**Assets Protection:** Allow protected assets to be used within the receiving agency while restricting their redistribution outside that agency.

**Mixed Snapshot Sharing:** Continue sharing eligible non-protected assets even when the Snapshot also contains protected assets.

**Pre-Share Visibility:** Review protected assets that will be excluded before completing an external share.

## Link Types & When to Use Them

Each Snapshot sharing option controls who can access the Snapshot and how the link can be used. Selecting the appropriate link type reduces accidental reuse and helps match access to the intended recipient.

| Link Type | Who Can Import | Behavior / Best Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Permanent Link** | Anyone with the active URL | Reusable for repeated imports. Best when the same Snapshot needs to be distributed more than once. |
| **One-Time Link** | Anyone with the URL until the permitted import is completed | Designed for a single successful import. Generate another link for another recipient. |
| **Email Link** | The intended email recipient | A single-use sharing experience delivered by email instead of manually copying the URL. |
| **Agency-Restricted Link** | Only agencies whose relationship numbers are specified | Restricts access to approved agencies. Multiple agency relationship numbers can be specified when supported by the sharing workflow. |
| **Sub-Account Restricted Link** | Only the designated sub-account | Best when the Snapshot must be limited to a specific destination rather than broadly reusable. |
| **Marketplace Share Link** | Eligible buyers through the HighLevel App Marketplace listing | Used as part of Marketplace Snapshot distribution. Assets Protection is automatically applied to help prevent protected assets from being repackaged or resold. |

**Selling on the Marketplace:** From **Agency View > Account Snapshots**, use the Snapshot action menu and select **Sell on Marketplace** to begin the guided Marketplace listing workflow.

![Sell on Marketplace Snapshot workflow](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064696055/original/FFdPVRdO1QCb0YJu2yo0CaeVfGr8Ss_JUw.gif?1770819813)

## Sharing Snapshots That Contain Protected Assets

Assets Protection controls what happens when protected Snapshot content would leave an agency. Protected assets can be reused across sub-accounts and Snapshots inside the receiving agency, but the protected status remains attached and restricts external redistribution.

Applying Assets Protection to a Snapshot You Share

Turn on **Assets Protected** when generating the share if you want applicable Snapshot assets to remain protected after the recipient imports them. Recipients can use those protected assets within their agency, but protected content remains restricted from external redistribution or resale.

Sharing a Snapshot That Already Contains Protected Assets

If the Snapshot contains protected assets inherited from an earlier protected Snapshot, those assets can continue to be used internally. When the Snapshot is shared outside the agency, protected assets are excluded while eligible non-protected assets continue through the share.

**Important:** The presence of protected content does not make the entire Snapshot unshareable. Mixed Snapshots can still be shared externally; only the protected assets are held back.

### **Review Protected Assets Before Sharing**

When protected content is detected during external sharing, HighLevel provides a review of the assets that cannot leave the agency and the eligible assets that can continue. Expand asset groups when you need to inspect individual items before completing the share.

![Pre-share review showing protected assets that will be excluded from an external Snapshot share](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079639423/original/E7foOi4Auy87TrfEgsQWdNFHXG4a6NkMrA.png?1788098960=)
![Expanded protected-asset review showing individual Snapshot asset sharing status](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079639427/original/ynk1V7vKC42k6ZVMz8XJE7wwx_KblmGv4Q.png?1788098976=)

For the complete protection model, see [Assets Protected Snapshots (Called "IP Protected" Earlier)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002852-assets-protected-snapshots-called-ip-protected-earlier-).

## Snapshot Sharing vs. SaaS Provisioning

Manual Snapshot sharing and SaaS provisioning can both distribute Snapshot configurations, but they solve different onboarding needs. Understanding the distinction prevents share links from being confused with automated SaaS account creation.

| Workflow | How It Works | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Snapshot Sharing** | You generate a share link or invite. The recipient imports the Snapshot and then uses it in the appropriate account workflow. | Manual distribution to agencies, clients, partners, or specific destinations. |
| **SaaS Provisioning** | A Snapshot is attached to a SaaS plan and can be automatically applied when checkout provisions a new sub-account. | Automated SaaS onboarding and repeatable account creation. |

For automated SaaS provisioning, see [Getting Started with the SaaS Configurator](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008015-getting-started-with-the-saas-configurator).

## How To Set Up Snapshot Sharing

Proper setup ensures the Snapshot reaches the intended recipient with the correct access and protection settings. Confirm permissions and refresh the Snapshot when needed before generating the share.

Required Access

The user must have the appropriate Snapshot permissions. If the sharing action is unavailable, verify that **Share/Import Snapshots** access is enabled for that user.

Before Sharing Updated Content

If the source sub-account changed after the Snapshot was created, [refresh the Snapshot](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982583-refresh-or-update-snapshots) first so the share contains the intended current assets.

Step 1

Open My Snapshots

From **Agency View**, go to **Account Snapshots > My Snapshots**.

![Account Snapshots page showing My Snapshots](https://jumpshare.com/share/QmzbOAYgy2d10wuvVx9A+/Screen+Shot+2025-12-10+at+8.01.02+PM.png)

Step 2

Open the Share Snapshot Workflow

Locate the Snapshot you want to distribute, open the **⋯ three-dot** action menu, and select **Share Snapshot**.

![Snapshot action menu showing Share Snapshot](https://jumpshare.com/share/ogUl0SQhW4w2Fy8vph9O+/Screen+Shot+2025-12-10+at+8.06.36+PM.png)

Step 3

Choose a Share Option

Select the sharing method that matches the intended recipient and reuse requirements:

- **Permanent Link** for reusable sharing.
- **One-Time Link** for a single-use share.
- **Email Link** for single-use delivery by email.
- **Agency-Restricted** to limit access to specified agencies.
- **Sub-Account Restricted** to limit the Snapshot to the selected destination.

Step 4

Configure Assets Protection (Optional)

Turn on **Assets Protected** when you want the applicable Snapshot assets to remain protected after the recipient imports them. Protected assets can be reused within the receiving agency but remain restricted from external redistribution or resale.

![Share Snapshot modal with Assets Protection enabled](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080790014/original/J98dDhBlRFMrf3IRwqjvrl0I4uXCbmdd9Q.png?1789242364)

Enable Assets Protection before generating the protected share.

Step 5

Review Protected Assets When Applicable

If the Snapshot already contains protected assets and the share would send content outside the agency, review the protected content shown before continuing. Protected assets will be excluded while eligible non-protected assets can continue through the share.

Step 6

Generate and Share the Link

1. Click **Get Link**.
2. Copy the generated link and send it to the intended recipient.

![Generated Snapshot share link ready to copy](https://jumpshare.com/share/KAsxVvxJwfGqQHYm728A+/Screen+Shot+2025-12-10+at+9.35.56+PM.png)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I share a Snapshot that contains protected assets?

Yes. If the Snapshot contains both protected and non-protected assets, the eligible non-protected assets can still be shared externally. Protected assets are excluded when they would leave the agency.

Q: Do I need to remove protected assets manually before sharing a mixed Snapshot?

No. HighLevel identifies protected assets during external sharing and excludes them while allowing eligible assets to continue.

Q: Can the receiving agency reuse protected assets internally?

Yes. Protected assets can be reused across sub-accounts and Snapshots inside the receiving agency. Their protected status continues to follow them.

Q: Can the receiving agency re-share or resell protected assets to another agency?

No. Protected assets remain restricted when they would leave the receiving agency.

Q: If I update a Snapshot after sharing it with another agency, does the recipient receive the changes automatically?

No. External agencies do not receive Snapshot updates automatically. Refresh the Snapshot, generate the appropriate updated share, and have the external agency import the updated Snapshot.

Q: How do I update sub-accounts inside my own agency?

Refresh the Snapshot first. You can then use **Push Updates** for eligible linked sub-accounts inside your agency and choose which refreshed assets to send.

Q: I shared a Snapshot but the recipient did not see my newest assets. What happened?

The Snapshot may not have been refreshed after the source sub-account changed. Refresh the Snapshot so the new or modified assets are captured, then share the updated Snapshot again.

Q: Why don't I see the option to share a Snapshot?

Check the user's Snapshot permissions. The appropriate **Share/Import Snapshots** permission must be enabled for the user to perform Snapshot sharing actions.

title_en: AI Prompting 101
source_md:
You can achieve a lot with simple prompts, but the quality of results depends on how much information you provide it and how well-crafted the prompt is. A simple prompt can make your bot act as a bot, but a bot with a good prompt can vastly increase your human agency, build relationships and drive up business. 

**IN THIS ARTICLE**

- [Prompt Elements](#Prompt-Elements)
- [Best Prompting Practices](#Best-Prompting-Practices)
- [Elements in action](#Elements-in-action)
  - [Role; specifying Interaction and Flow](#Role;-specifying-Interaction-and-Flow)
  - [Task; specifying Instructions and Objectives](#Task;-specifying-Instructions-and-Objectives)
  - [Guidelines; Guardrails for the bot to abide by](#Guidelines;-Guardrails-for-the-bot-to-abide-by%C2%A0)
- [Best Practices in action](#Best-Practices-in-action)
  - [Repetition](#Repetition)
  - [Examples/Illustrations](#Examples/Illustrations%C2%A0)
- [Advanced Prompting:](#Advanced-Prompting%3A%C2%A0)
  - [Delimiters](#Delimiters%C2%A0)
  - [Conversation Context](#Conversation-Context%C2%A0)
  - [Writing styles](#Writing-styles%C2%A0)
  - [Tone](#Tone)

## Prompt Elements

As we cover more and more examples and applications with prompt engineering, you will notice that certain elements make up a prompt. You can use these elements to instruct the model more effectively to improve the quality of results.

- Role; specifying Interaction and Flow - persona, directions and context that can steer the AI model to better responses. Defining the role plays a pivotal part in the coherence and relevance of AI responses.
- Task; specifying Instructions and Objectives - a specific task or instruction you want the model to perform, At the core of any successful prompt lies a well-defined task. Vague or ambiguous prompts might lead to your GPT bot hallucinating, or simply producing an outcome that’s not what you were expecting or which doesn’t meet your expectations.
- Guidelines; guardrails for bot to abide by - guidelines are more like guardrails, steering the ChatBot toward desired outcomes. Clearly articulate rules to create a roadmap for more precise and tailored responses.

## Best Prompting Practices

- Repetition - Incorporating repetition is key when you want to emphasize specific instructions, guiding the AI to respond more consistently in the desired direction. By reiterating critical parts of the prompt, you ensure the model's outputs align more predictably with your expectations. This approach is particularly effective in reinforcing the bot's adherence to essential guidelines or tasks.
- Examples/Illustrations - Examples help AI ChatBots understand exactly what and how to do the required task, usually when describing the task is harder than just providing examples. Utilizing examples can significantly enhance an AI ChatBot's comprehension of the task at hand. While offering overarching instructions that span across all scenarios and permutations can be helpful, sometimes it's simpler to provide specific examples. This is particularly useful when aiming for the model to replicate a certain response style, tone or manner to user inquiries that are not easily described in words.
- Iterative Improvement - While there are valuable tips and strategies for crafting prompts, developing effective ones for a GPT chatbot is fundamentally an iterative process. So before you set it out in the wild, you should test, tweak and fine-tune it as needed. Experimentation with various phrasings and methods is key to identifying what resonates best with your bot's objectives. Identifying the impact of modifications, such as new instructions or designs, can sometimes be challenging. Initial observations may provide some insights, yet small sample sizes might blur the distinction between genuine improvement and mere chance. To navigate this, use Bot Trial under ConversationAI to test, iterate and enhance your prompts and make the bot behave exactly as you want. The more you repeat this process, the better outcome your chatbot will achieve, and the better you will become at writing effective prompts

## Elements in action

### Role; specifying Interaction and Flow

- Worse:  
  “You are a salesperson for {{ai.business\_name}}, assist customers and help them book appointments. Act like a human. You are talking to {{contact.name}}."
- Better:  
  “- You work for {{ai.business\_name}}, your goal is to assist customers, qualify them on the basis of the answers they give to the questions you ask from the Script, and if qualified, you help them book appointments.  
  - Always maintain the persona of a human assistant. Do not disclose, suggest, or hint at being an AI assistant unless asked. Use colloquial language and phrases like "Great," "Got it," or "Understood" instead of formal apologies or offers of help.  
  - Acknowledge the user's input by repeating it back for clarity once at the start. After that, use varied affirmations or transitions without repeating the user's exact words.  
  - Maintain a professional, yet casual demeanor. Use periods instead of exclamation points to moderate the tone.  
  - You are talking to {{contact.name}}. Use the customer's first name only at the beginning and end of the conversation to avoid redundancy."

### Task; specifying Instructions and Objectives

- Worse:  
  “You are required to qualify customers by asking them questions then asking them to book an appointment. If they are not interested, just collect their details.”
- Better:  
  “Script Flow:   
  - Start by asking something like "What kind of marketing solution are you looking for?". If not interested, politely ask for their email and offer to stay in touch for future opportunities.  
  - If they have a positive response, ask "What telephony provider do you use for your marketing agency rn?".  
  - Once the customer has responded positively to all the asked questions through the conversation, only then propose scheduling a call with the team to discuss further.   
  - Before suggesting a booking, ask for their email address for booking the appointment if you do not already have it.  
  - Then help them book a call. Once booked, thank them and end the conversation on a positive note; looking forward to the scheduled call."

### Guidelines; Guardrails for the bot to abide by

(You can specify these under Role and Instructions as well)

- Worse:  
  "Reply in a concise manner. Ask all the questions in script and then have them book an appointment.”
- Better:  
  “- Keep answers short, direct, and within a 20-word limit.  
  - Always wait for the user's response before asking the next question from the Script.  
  - Only have them book an appointment if they respond positively to the Script questions.”

## Best Practices in action

- ### Repetition

                As we want our bot to follow the sales script we have put in place, we’d repeat/reference it multiple times.

- In Role we have:   
  “- You work for {{ai.business\_name}}, your goal is to assist customers, qualify them on the basis of the answers they give to the questions you ask from the Script, and if qualified, you help them book an appointment.”
- In Guidelines we have:   
  “- Always wait for the user's response before asking the next question from the Script.  
  - Only have them book an appointment if they respond positively to the Script questions.”
- ### Examples/Illustrations
- In Role we have:   
  “- Always maintain the persona of a human assistant. Do not disclose, suggest, or hint at being an AI assistant unless asked. Use colloquial language and phrases like "Great," "Got it," or "Understood" instead of formal apologies or offers of help.”
- It can also be written as:  
  “EXAMPLES OF WHAT TO SAY AND WHAT NOT TO SAY:

- Avoid: I didn't understand your response.

- Use: Wait, what did you say? Sorry, could you repeat that?

- Avoid: I apologize for the confusion.

- Use: Sorry if that didn't make sense.

- Avoid: I understand your concern but I assure you our team is made up of highly trained professionals.

- Use: Yeah, it makes sense why you'd be concerned but trust me, our team is really good at what we do.”

## Advanced Prompting:

As we want our bot to follow the sales script we have put in place, we’d repeat/reference it multiple times.

- Static Information

You can add context or information about your business, offers, services in the prompt itself if you want the bot to have access to it all the time. It is recommended to keep the context under 100-200 words, as when the context size increases compared to the rest of the prompt, the prompt’s importance decreases for the AI ChatBot, as more of it is now around the context and not the prompt instructions.

- ### Delimiters

These are special characters you would use to emphasise or demarcate certain pieces of text (e.g. Context) in the prompt from other instructions in the prompt. 

- For emphasis you can use; #, >, <
- For demarcation you can use: “””, ‘’’, <> </>
- Example: Say you want to add some information about your offer in the prompt;  
  Worse:  
  “Offer: Elevate Your Business with Cutting-Edge A.I. Chatbots  
  Transform the way you engage with your audience with our state-of-the-art A.I. chatbots, trusted by leading industry giants. Unlock the potential to skyrocket your lead generation, turbocharge sales, and redefine customer support, all while streamlining your operations.  
  Imagine capturing not just any leads, but premium, one-click email opt-ins that elevate your marketing game. Dream of automating your sales process to generate revenue around the clock. Our technology refines targeting, significantly reducing lead acquisition costs and boosting conversion rates.  
  But why stop there? Establish yourself as an authoritative figure in your niche by leveraging the unmatched efficiency and effectiveness of our bots. Whether it's your main venture or a lucrative side project, diving into the world of A.I. Chatbots opens up a realm of possibilities. Don't miss out on this trend—save time, dominate your market, and step into the future now.”  
  Better:  
  “# Offer:  
  <offer>  
  Elevate Your Business with Cutting-Edge A.I. Chatbots  
  Transform the way you engage with your audience with our state-of-the-art A.I. chatbots, trusted by leading industry giants. Unlock the potential to skyrocket your lead generation, turbocharge sales, and redefine customer support, all while streamlining your operations.  
  Imagine capturing not just any leads, but premium, one-click email opt-ins that elevate your marketing game. Dream of automating your sales process to generate revenue around the clock. Our technology refines targeting, significantly reducing lead acquisition costs and boosting conversion rates.  
  But why stop there? Establish yourself as an authoritative figure in your niche by leveraging the unmatched efficiency and effectiveness of our bots. Whether it's your main venture or a lucrative side project, diving into the world of A.I. Chatbots opens up a realm of possibilities. Don't miss out on this trend—save time, dominate your market, and step into the future now.  
  </offer>  
  “
- ### Conversation Context

For specific use cases you can also add conversation context in the prompt, describing why and under what situation is the bot talking to a customer. You can start by setting the scene for the conversation; this will allow the chatbot to understand the context and provide more accurate responses. Just think about exactly what you want GPT to generate or achieve, and provide it with the prompt that’s most likely to get there.  

- Example, you can open the prompt by telling the chatbot why someone is interacting with it and what to do in the situation:  
  Worse:   
  “You are required to take on the role of a customer support chatbot”  
  Better:   
  “a client is contacting us because something went wrong” — and then telling it its role in the situation — “you must act as a friendly agent in charge of collecting a clear idea of what went wrong with the order, you need to ask them.”
- ### Writing styles

Analytical, Conversational, Creative, Descriptive, Informative, Instructive, Persuasive, Satirical, Technical etc.

- ### Tone

Authoritative, Clinical, Confident, Empathetic, Formal, Friendly, Humorous Informal, Optimistic, Playful, Sarcastic, Serious, Sympathetic, Warm etc.

title_en: How to Use the Ask AI Home Screen Widget in HighLevel
source_md:
The Ask AI Home Screen Widget gives you instant access to HighLevel's Ask AI assistant directly from your phone's home screen. With dedicated Chat, Voice, and Camera shortcuts, you can start a new conversation, ask questions hands-free, or capture photos without navigating through the mobile app. Available on supported iOS and Android devices, the widget makes it easier to get answers and complete tasks while on the go.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the Ask AI Home Screen Widget?](#What-is-the-Ask-AI-Home-Screen-Widget?)
- [Key Benefits of the Ask AI Home Screen Widget](#Key-Benefits-of-the-Ask-AI-Home-Screen-Widget)
- [Chat Bar: Start a New Ask AI Conversation](#Chat-Bar%3A-Start-a-New-Ask-AI-Conversation)
- [Voice Button: Start a Hands-Free Conversation](#Voice-Button%3A-Start-a-Hands-Free-Conversation)
- [Camera Button: Capture a Photo and Ask AI](#Camera-Button%3A-Capture-a-Photo-and-Ask-AI)
- [How to Set Up the Ask AI Home Screen Widget](#How-to-Set-Up-the-Ask-AI-Home-Screen-Widget)
- [Add the Ask AI Widget on iOS](#Before-You-BeginMake-sure-the-following-requirements-are-met:1.-Your-device-has-a-supported-version-of-iOS-or-Android.2.-Your-HighLevel,-LeadConnector,-or-eligible-White-Label-app-is-updated-to-version-4.27.0-or-later.3.-Ask-AI-is-enabled-for-your-account.4.-You-can-sign-in-to-the-mobile-app.5.-If-you-use-a-White-Label-app,-the-Ask-AI-Home-Widget-has-been-enabled-for-your-company.Add-the-Ask-AI-Widget-on-iOS)
- [Add the Ask AI Widget on Android](#Add-the-Ask-AI-Widget-on-Android)
- [Start a Conversation from the Widget](#Start-a-Conversation-from-the-Widget)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is the Ask AI Home Screen Widget?**

The Ask AI Home Screen Widget is a mobile shortcut that lets you launch Ask AI directly from your device's home screen. Instead of opening the HighLevel app and navigating to Ask AI, you can start a fresh conversation with a single tap. The widget supports text, voice, and camera interactions, making it useful when you need quick assistance while managing your business.

The widget includes three interactive components:

- **Chat Bar:** Opens a new Ask AI conversation with the keyboard ready for typing.
- **Voice Button:** Opens a new Ask AI conversation in hands-free Voice Mode.
- **Camera Button:** Opens your device's camera, attaches the captured photo to a new Ask AI conversation, and waits for your question.

The widget automatically uses your app's language and brand colors and supports both light and dark modes. It is available in supported HighLevel, LeadConnector, and White Label mobile apps.

---

## **Key Benefits of the Ask AI Home Screen Widget**

The Ask AI Home Screen Widget reduces the steps required to access AI assistance from your mobile device. Whether you're managing clients, reviewing documents, or working away from your desk, these shortcuts help you interact with Ask AI using the input method that best fits your situation.

- **Faster Access to Ask AI:** Start a new Ask AI conversation directly from your phone's home screen without navigating through the app.
- **Hands-Free Assistance:** Launch Voice Mode to ask questions and interact with Ask AI while multitasking.
- **Instant Photo-Based Questions:** Capture a document, product, receipt, or job site photo and ask Ask AI about it without manually attaching the image.
- **Flexible Communication:** Choose between typing, speaking, or capturing a photo based on your immediate needs.
- **Consistent Branding:** Display the widget using your app's brand colors and language, including support for White Label apps.
- **Seamless Sign-In Experience:** Continue the widget action you selected after signing in if your session has expired or you are signed out.

---

## **Chat Bar: Start a New Ask AI Conversation**

The Chat bar provides a quick way to ask questions or submit instructions without navigating through multiple app screens. It is especially useful when you need to create content, retrieve information, or request assistance with a business task.

For example, you can use the Chat bar to ask Ask AI to draft an email, summarize information, or retrieve supported business data.

For additional information about supported tasks, see [Overview of Ask AI Assistant & Its Capabilities in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005327-introduction-to-ask-ai-assistant).

---

## **Voice Button: Start a Hands-Free Conversation**

The Voice button provides direct access to Ask AI Voice Mode, allowing you to communicate through speech instead of typing. Voice conversations are useful when you're moving between appointments, working on-site, or using your phone while performing other tasks.

**Note:** Voice Mode requires microphone access. If your device requests microphone permission, allow access to use spoken interactions.

For more information about voice interactions, see [How to Use Ask AI Voice Mode](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008022-how-to-use-ask-ai-voice-mode).

---

## **Camera Button: Capture a Photo and Ask AI**

The Camera button allows you to start an Ask AI conversation using a photo captured with your mobile device. This eliminates the extra steps of taking a picture separately, opening Ask AI, and manually attaching the image.

For example, you might capture a printed document and ask Ask AI to summarize its contents, or photograph a product and request help creating a description.

The Camera shortcut is especially useful when your question involves something physically in front of you.

**Note:** Camera access may be required. If your device requests camera permission, allow access to capture photos.

---

## **How to Set Up the Ask AI Home Screen Widget**

Adding the Ask AI Home Screen Widget places Chat, Voice, and Camera shortcuts directly on your device's home screen. Proper setup ensures that your app meets the version requirements and that the widget is available when you need to start an Ask AI conversation.

### ``` Before You Begin Make sure the following requirements are met: 1. Your device has a supported version of iOS or Android. 2. Your HighLevel, LeadConnector, or eligible White Label app is updated to version 4.27.0 or later. 3. Ask AI is enabled for your account. 4. You can sign in to the mobile app. 5. If you use a White Label app, the Ask AI Home Widget has been enabled for your company. ``` **Add the Ask AI Widget on iOS**

iOS users can add the Ask AI widget through the device's home screen customization options.

1. **Open your Home Screen:** Unlock your iPhone and navigate to the home screen where you want to place the widget.
2. **Enter Edit Mode:** Touch and hold an empty area of the home screen until the app icons enter edit mode.
3. **Open the Widget Gallery:** Tap **+** or use the available widget-adding option, depending on your iOS interface.
4. **Find Your App:** Search for HighLevel, LeadConnector, or your White Label app.
5. **Select Ask AI:** Choose the **Ask AI** widget from the available widget options.
6. **Add the Widget:** Tap **Add Widget** and place it on your home screen.
7. **Finish Editing:** Exit home screen editing mode to save the placement.
8. **Test the Widget:** Tap the Chat bar, Voice button, or Camera button to launch a new Ask AI conversation.
9. [동영상](https://jumpshare.com/embed/AtqTalP8XajDwznIOWEu)

### 

### **Add the Ask AI Widget on Android**

Android users can add the Ask AI widget using the device's widget selection menu. The appearance of this menu may vary depending on the phone manufacturer and Android launcher.

1. **Open your Home Screen:** Unlock your Android device and navigate to the home screen.
2. **Open Home Screen Options:** Touch and hold an empty area of the home screen.
3. **Select Widgets:** Tap **Widgets** from the available options.
4. **Find Your App:** Locate HighLevel, LeadConnector, or your White Label app in the widget list.
5. **Select Ask AI:** Find and select the **Ask AI** widget.
6. **Add the Widget:** Drag or place the widget onto your home screen using your device's available controls.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084821748/original/dYWMkda8QMqVuDdMr75slQ-MWhTPp5nS8w.png?1793701746)
7. **Confirm Placement:** Finish the placement process.
8. **Test the Widget:** Tap the Chat bar, Voice button, or Camera button to start a new Ask AI conversation.

### **Start a Conversation from the Widget**

Once the widget has been added, you can select the shortcut that best matches how you want to interact with Ask AI.

1. Tap the **Chat bar** to open a new conversation and begin typing.
2. Tap **Voice** to start a new hands-free conversation.
3. Tap **Camera** to capture a photo and attach it to a new conversation before entering your question.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084821838/original/zKdHUaKyVt7_miVQtZFM4ElsojuyyvC8NA.png?1793701797)

Each shortcut starts a fresh Ask AI conversation. If you are signed out when you select a widget shortcut, the app will ask you to sign in. After successful authentication, it resumes the action you originally selected.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why can't I find the Ask AI widget in my phone's widget list?**

A: Confirm that your mobile app is updated to version 4.27.0 or later, your device meets the supported operating system requirements, and Ask AI is enabled for your account. If you're using a White Label app, confirm that the Ask AI Home Widget switch has been enabled for your company.

**Q: Do I need to sign in every time I use the widget?**

A: Not necessarily. If you're already signed in, the widget opens the selected Ask AI experience. If you're signed out, the app prompts you to sign in and resumes your selected action afterward.

**Q: Can I use the widget with a White Label mobile app?**

A: Yes. White Label mobile apps support the widget when the company-level Ask AI Home Widget feature is enabled and the app and account meet the requirements.

**Q: What if the Camera button cannot open my camera?**

A: Check whether the mobile app has permission to use your device's camera. If camera access is blocked, review the app's permissions in your device settings before trying again.

**Q: Can I return to conversations I started through the widget?**

A: Ask AI supports conversation history and multiple conversation threads. You can use Ask AI's Chat History to find previous conversations. For more information, see [Ask AI Multi-Threading: Run Multiple Tasks at Once](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008420-ask-ai-multi-threading-run-multiple-tasks-at-once).

**Q: Does the widget provide access to additional Ask AI features?**

A: The widget provides shortcuts to existing Ask AI functionality rather than introducing a separate AI assistant. Available capabilities continue to depend on your Ask AI access and supported features.

**Q: Can I change the widget's colors independently of my app's branding?**

A: The widget automatically follows the app's language and brand colors. The release does not identify separate widget-specific color customization settings.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Overview of Ask AI Assistant & Its Capabilities in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005327-introduction-to-ask-ai-assistant)
- [How to Use Ask AI Voice Mode](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008022-how-to-use-ask-ai-voice-mode)
- [HighLevel Mobile App Experience](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008398-highlevel-mobile-app-experience)
- [How to Customize Your White Label HighLevel Mobile App](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005009-how-to-customize-your-white-label-highlevel-mobile-app)
- [Ask AI Multi-Threading: Run Multiple Tasks at Once](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008420-ask-ai-multi-threading-run-multiple-tasks-at-once)
