title_en: Email AI Access for Agency Users Across Locations
source_md:
Agency users can now access Email AI across locations, even when Email AI is disabled for location users in a specific location. This makes it easier for agencies to create and manage Email AI templates directly where they are needed instead of relying on enabled locations as a workaround. Location users continue to receive Email AI access according to their location's Labs configuration. The **“Visible to Agency Users Only”** indicator helps agency users understand when Email AI is not available to location users.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Email AI Access for Agency Users Across Locations?](#What-is-Email-AI-Access-for-Agency-Users-Across-Locations?)
- [Key Benefits of Email AI Access for Agency Users](#Key-Benefits-of-Email-AI-Access-for-Agency-Users)
- [How Email AI Access Works for Agency and Location Users](#How-Email-AI-Access-Works-for-Agency-and-Location-Users)
- [Email AI Templates and Template Sharing](#Email-AI-Templates-and-Template-Sharing)
- [Set Up Email AI for Agency Users](#Set-Up-Email-AI-for-Agency-Users)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What is Email AI Access for Agency Users Across Locations?**

Email AI helps users create and refine emails in HighLevel using guided prompts, brand-aware styling, and conversational editing. Expanded agency-user access allows agencies to work with Email AI inside locations even when the location has not enabled Email AI for its own users, reducing unnecessary template duplication while preserving location-level controls.

---

## **Key Benefits of Email AI Access for Agency Users**

Giving agency users consistent Email AI access reduces the administrative work required to create client email assets while maintaining separate controls for location users. Agencies can work more efficiently without enabling a Labs feature for client users who are not ready to use it.

- **Create templates where they are needed:** Agency users can build and manage Email AI templates directly inside the applicable location.
- **Reduce duplicate work:** Agencies no longer need to use an Email AI-enabled location as a workaround and then manually distribute templates solely because Email AI is disabled elsewhere.
- **Maintain location-level controls:** Location users continue to receive Email AI access according to their location's Labs configuration.
- **Improve access clarity:** The **“Visible to Agency Users Only”** tag helps agency users understand why they can see Email AI when a location user cannot.

---

## **How Email AI Access Works for Agency and Location Users**

Email AI availability now considers both the user's context and the location's Labs configuration. Understanding that distinction helps agencies prepare templates for clients without unintentionally changing which features are available to the client's own users.

| User context | Email AI disabled for the location | Email AI enabled for the location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agency user | Email AI remains accessible | Email AI is accessible |
| Location user | Email AI is unavailable | Email AI is available, subject to applicable permissions |

For location users, Email AI continues to follow the location's Labs configuration.

For additional information about Labs controls, see [Labs Features - Complete Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003588-labs-features-complete-overview).

```
Important: Expanded Email AI availability does not give someone access to a location or module they otherwise cannot access. HighLevel user type, role, sub-account assignment, and module permissions continue to determine a user's broader account access.
```

---

## **Email AI Templates and Template Sharing**

Direct Email AI access gives agencies more flexibility to create templates inside the location where the template will be used. Template sharing remains useful when an agency intentionally wants to copy an existing email template to other locations, but it is no longer required solely as a workaround for an agency user being unable to access Email AI in a location.

Use direct Email AI creation when you want to build or manage a template specifically for the current location. Use template sharing when you intentionally want to reuse or distribute an existing template across locations.

For instructions on copying an existing template, see [Share Email Template across Agencies](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002945-share-email-template-across-agencies).

---

## **Set Up Email AI for Agency Users**

Agency users can access Email AI in locations they already have access to, even when Email AI is disabled for location users.

1. Log in to HighLevel as an agency user.
2. Open the location where you want to create or manage an Email AI template.
3. Go to **Marketing → Emails → Templates**and Type in to **Build with AI**. The **“Visible to Agency Users Only”** tag is also visible here.

   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079394545/original/jDK9MvCPOXmgRQhvOEF0aHhuN6pFkF3xfg.png?1787794368)
4. If Email AI is disabled for location users, look for the **“Visible to Agency Users Only”** tag.

   The **“Visible to Agency Users Only”** tag helps prevent confusion when an agency user can access Email AI but the feature is disabled for the location's users. The indicator communicates that the agency user is seeing functionality that is not currently available to location users under that location's Email AI configuration.

   Seeing this tag does not require the agency user to enable Email AI for the location before continuing their work. If location users also need Email AI access, the appropriate Email AI Labs configuration must be enabled for that location.

   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079394523/original/U9G_6qZxS6YvWIoQRP3OgccR251PAvCUKA.jpeg?1787794279)
5. Create or update the template, then save your changes.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does expanded Email AI access give an agency user access to locations they were not otherwise permitted to access?**

No. Email AI access does not replace HighLevel's existing user type, role, account scope, or permission controls. Those settings continue to determine the accounts and modules a user can access.

**Q: Does an Admin role inside a location automatically receive agency-user Email AI access?**

Not simply because the user is a location Admin. HighLevel distinguishes between user scope and role, and sub-account users have permissions within their applicable location. The agency-user access described here applies to the agency-user context identified by this feature release.

**Q: Does creating an Email AI template in one location automatically copy it to every other location?**

No. Expanded access lets agency users create templates directly where they are needed; it does not automatically synchronize a template across locations. HighLevel's template-sharing workflow can still be used when you intentionally want to share or clone a template.

**Q: Can agency users still use the existing email-template sharing feature?**

Yes. Template sharing remains available as a separate workflow for reusing an existing email template across supported locations.

**Q: Does this access enhancement remove other Email AI prerequisites?**

No. It changes how Email AI availability works for agency users when the feature is disabled at the location level. Existing Email AI requirements and recommendations still apply.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Email AI (Beta 2.0) — Create On-Brand Emails Faster](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007382-email-ai-beta-2-0-create-on-brand-emails-faster)
- [How to Use the Email Builder and its In-line Editor](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000087-how-to-use-the-email-builder-and-its-in-line-editor)
- [Labs Features - Complete Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003588-labs-features-complete-overview)
- [Share Email Template across Agencies](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002945-share-email-template-across-agencies)
- [How to Manage Agency User Roles and Permissions in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002543)
- [Manage Sub-Account User Roles & Permissions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002544-sub-account-managing-user-roles-permissions)

title_en: Connect External MCP Servers to AI Agents in Workflows
source_md:
AI Agents in HighLevel Workflows can now connect to external services using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This allows your AI Agent to access real-time information from compatible tools such as web search providers, browser automation platforms, databases, and custom APIs. By extending your AI Agent beyond CRM data, you can automate research, enrich records, and perform more intelligent workflow actions.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are MCP Connections for AI Agents?](#What-are-MCP-Connections-for-AI-Agents?)
- [Key Benefits of MCP Connections](#Key-Benefits-of-MCP-Connections)
- [Supported MCP Servers](#Supported-MCP-Servers)
- [Authentication Options](#Authentication-Options)
- [Supported Transport Types](#Supported-Transport-Types)
- [How Tool Discovery Works](#How-Tool-Discovery-Works)
- [Configure an MCP Connection](#Configure-an-MCP-Connection)
- [Managing Tool Permissions](#Managing-Tool-Permissions)
- [Best Practices](#Best-Practices)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What are MCP Connections for AI Agents?**

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables AI applications to securely communicate with external tools and services. With MCP Connections in HighLevel Workflows, AI Agents can connect to compatible MCP servers and use their available tools while executing workflow actions.

Unlike standard AI Agent capabilities that rely primarily on information available within HighLevel, MCP Connections allow agents to retrieve live information, automate browser tasks, perform searches, and interact with external systems in real time.

---

## **Key Benefits of MCP Connections**

Connecting external MCP servers expands what your AI Agent can accomplish during workflow execution.

- **Real-Time Data Access:** Retrieve current information from external services while the workflow is running.
- **Extensible AI Capabilities:** Connect to any compatible MCP server instead of being limited to built-in tools.
- **Automatic Tool Discovery:** Detect available tools automatically after testing a connection.
- **Granular Tool Permissions:** Choose exactly which tools each AI Agent is allowed to use.
- **Workflow Automation:** Eliminate manual research and repetitive tasks by allowing AI Agents to interact with external services.
- **Flexible Authentication:**Support multiple authentication methods depending on the MCP provider.

---

## **Supported MCP Servers**

HighLevel supports connections to any MCP-compatible server.

Common examples include:

- **Exa** – AI-powered web search across companies, people, and news.
- **Tavily** – Real-time web search and webpage extraction.
- **Browserbase** – Browser automation for navigation, clicks, screenshots, and data extraction.
- **Custom MCP Servers** – Self-hosted or internally developed MCP servers that follow the MCP specification.

```
Note: HighLevel does not host or manage third-party MCP servers. Availability, pricing, authentication requirements, and supported tools are determined by the provider.
```

---

## **Authentication Options**

Different MCP providers require different authentication methods. HighLevel supports multiple authentication types to accommodate a variety of services.

Supported authentication methods include:

- None
- API Key
- Bearer Token
- OAuth2
- Custom Header

Some providers allow API keys to be passed through HTTP headers, while others require them as query parameters. Refer to your MCP provider's documentation for the correct configuration.

---

## **Supported Transport Types**

Transport types determine how HighLevel communicates with the MCP server.

Supported transport options include:

- HTTP Streamable (default)
- Server-Sent Events (SSE)

Unless your provider specifies otherwise, use HTTP Streamable, which is the recommended default option.

---

## **How Tool Discovery Works**

After entering your connection information, HighLevel can validate the connection and retrieve the tools made available by the MCP server.

Selecting Test Connection will:

- Verify communication with the server.
- Validate authentication credentials.
- Discover available tools automatically.
- Display every tool returned by the MCP server.

After discovery, choose which tools your AI Agent can access.

---

## **Configure an MCP Connection**

Proper configuration ensures your AI Agent can securely communicate with external services during workflow execution.

1. Open the desired Workflow.
2. Add or edit an AI Agent action.
3. Select Add Tools.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075528017/original/tAnm6_KhDvo0fiNH5zIJD8U63K63H8X54w.png?1783518106)
4. Open the MCP tab.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075528140/original/4yKAL_sQBGQZIafmA-Z9vBRyVQagnu9nlw.png?1783518152)
5. Click Add Connection.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075528294/original/xtoMJjTQ1Tbh03IciVOAf3BMnylMa427cA.png?1783518193)
6. Enter a descriptive Connection Name. Enter the Server URL supplied by your MCP provider. Select the appropriate Transport Type. Choose the required Authentication Type. Enter any required credentials.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075528721/original/CUKOQ4tJfUyQE_pu5RgatQ_pbKTpTMRhAg.png?1783518316)
7. Click Test Connection.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075529008/original/MNO4-rmrRsQBsYdOWsxZtMAgvK7FgKNXgg.png?1783518387)
8. Review the discovered tools.
9. Enable only the tools the AI Agent should be allowed to use.
10. Save the connection.

---

## **Managing Tool Permissions**

Each MCP server may expose multiple tools. Not every workflow requires access to every available capability.

Limiting tool access helps improve security, simplifies AI decision-making, and ensures the agent only performs approved actions.

After testing the connection:

- Review the discovered tools.
- Enable only the required tools.
- Disable tools that are unnecessary for the workflow.
- Save your selections.

These permissions apply at the AI Agent level, allowing different agents to use different tool sets even when connecting to the same server.

---

## **Best Practices**

Following these recommendations helps improve reliability and security when using external MCP services.

- Connect only trusted MCP providers.
- Use descriptive names for each connection.
- Enable only the tools required by the workflow.
- Test every connection before activating production workflows.
- Rotate API credentials according to your organization's security policies.
- Monitor third-party service availability.
- Review tool permissions periodically as workflows evolve.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What is an MCP server?**  
A: An MCP server exposes tools that AI applications can use through the Model Context Protocol.

**Q: Can I connect more than one MCP server to an AI Agent?**  
A: If supported by the AI Agent configuration, multiple MCP connections can be added, allowing the agent to use tools from different providers.

**Q: Does HighLevel provide MCP servers?**  
A: No. HighLevel provides the ability to connect to compatible MCP servers. Third-party providers or your organization are responsible for hosting and managing those servers.

**Q: What happens if the Test Connection fails?**  
A: Verify the server URL, authentication settings, API credentials, transport type, and that the MCP server is online and reachable.

**Q: Can I restrict which tools an AI Agent uses?**  
A: Yes. After tool discovery, you can enable or disable individual tools before saving the connection.

**Q: Are third-party MCP services included with my HighLevel subscription?**  
A: No. Third-party providers may require their own accounts, subscriptions, or API usage fees.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [HighLevel MCP Server: Connect AI Agents to HighLevel Tools](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007981)
- [How to Use the HighLevel MCP Server](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005741)
- [AI Studio in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007587)
- [How to Build Smarter AI Agents Using AI Agent Node in Agent Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007648)

title_en: Add Funds to Your Agency Wallet Using ACH Direct Debit
source_md:
Billing & Payments

# Add Funds to Your Wallet Using ACH Direct Debit

Save on processing fees by topping up your agency wallet with ACH bank transfers for payments over $1,000

What You'll Learn

HighLevel agencies can now fund their wallet using ACH direct debit (US bank transfer) in addition to credit or debit cards. This payment method is specifically designed for high-value top-ups and offers significant cost savings compared to card payments.

This article explains ACH eligibility requirements, cost differences, processing times, and step-by-step instructions for adding funds to your wallet using ACH direct debit.

## What is ACH Direct Debit for Wallet Top-Ups?

ACH (Automated Clearing House) direct debit is a bank-to-bank electronic payment method that allows HighLevel agencies to transfer funds from their US bank account directly into their agency wallet. This method is specifically optimized for high-value deposits and provides a cost-effective alternative to credit or debit card payments.

When you select ACH as your payment method in the "Add balance" modal, funds are withdrawn from your bank account and deposited into your HighLevel wallet after a settlement period of 3–10 business days. This longer processing time is offset by significantly lower transaction fees compared to instant card payments.

ACH direct debit is available exclusively to agency-level accounts and is not accessible in location (sub-account) wallets.

## Key Benefits

ACH direct debit offers several advantages for agencies making large wallet deposits:

**Significant Cost Savings** — ACH processing costs only 0.8% per transaction (capped at $5), compared to approximately 3% for card payments. On a $10,000 deposit, you save approximately $295 in processing fees.

**Optimized for High-Value Transactions** — With a $1,000 minimum deposit requirement, ACH is designed specifically for agencies making substantial wallet top-ups.

**Direct Bank Integration** — Funds transfer securely from your US bank account without requiring credit card limits or approval.

**Maximum Fee Cap** — The $5 maximum fee means even extremely large deposits (e.g., $50,000+) never exceed $5 in processing costs.

## Eligibility Requirements

To use ACH direct debit for wallet top-ups, your account must meet the following criteria:

Requirement 1

US-Based Agency

Your agency must be based in the United States. ACH direct debit is not available to agencies located outside the US or to international bank accounts.

Requirement 2

Minimum Deposit Amount

ACH top-ups require a minimum deposit of $1,000. This threshold ensures the payment method is used for its intended purpose: high-value transactions where cost savings are most meaningful.

Requirement 3

Agency-Level Access Only

ACH direct debit is available exclusively in the agency wallet. Location (sub-account) users will not see this payment option when attempting to add funds to their location wallet.

## Cost Comparison: ACH vs. Card Payments

Understanding the cost difference between ACH and card payments helps you make informed decisions about which payment method to use for wallet top-ups. The table below illustrates processing fees for common deposit amounts:

| Deposit Amount | Card Fee (≈3%) | ACH Fee (0.8%, max $5) | Savings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1,000 | $30.00 | $5.00 (capped) | $25.00 |
| $5,000 | $150.00 | $5.00 (capped) | $145.00 |
| $10,000 | $300.00 | $5.00 (capped) | $295.00 |
| $50,000 | $1,500.00 | $5.00 (capped) | $1,495.00 |

Cost Savings Tip

The $5 maximum fee cap means ACH becomes exponentially more cost-effective as deposit amounts increase. For deposits of $625 or more (where 0.8% equals $5), you pay only $5 regardless of the total amount.

## How to Add Funds Using ACH Direct Debit

Follow these steps to top up your agency wallet using ACH direct debit:

Step 1

Navigate to Wallet & Transactions

From your agency account, go to Settings → Billing. Click the "Wallet & Transactions" tab to view your current wallet balance.

Step 2

Open the Add Balance Modal

Click the "+ Add" button in the top-right corner of the Wallet & Transactions section. The "Add balance" modal will open, displaying your current balance and the subtitle "Add money to your wallet manually via card or ACH direct debit."

Step 3

Enter Deposit Amount

In the "Amount" field (showing "$ Enter amount" as placeholder text), type the dollar amount you want to add to your wallet. You must enter at least $1,000 to unlock the ACH payment option.

Step 4

Select ACH Direct Debit Payment Method

Under "Payment Method," you'll see two radio button options:

- **Pay with credit/debit card** — Shows "Charged instantly to your default card on file" (selected by default)
- **Pay with ACH direct debit** — Shows "3-10 business days" with a "$1000+" badge (only visible when amount is $1,000 or more)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077357337/original/F07tz3Fc07n32pBzBCrRD1JE0HIkWaPpzQ.png?1785509731)

Select the "Pay with ACH direct debit" option to proceed with bank transfer.

Step 5

Complete the Transaction

Click the "Add" button at the bottom-right of the modal to proceed. You'll be directed to a secure bank connection flow where you can authorize the ACH withdrawal from your US bank account. Follow your bank's authentication process to complete the setup.

Step 6

Wait for Settlement

Once authorized, your ACH transfer will be initiated. Funds typically settle within 3–10 business days. You can monitor the transaction status in your Wallet & Transactions tab. Your wallet balance will update automatically once the transfer completes.

Important

Ensure your bank account has sufficient funds to cover the deposit amount plus the 0.8% processing fee (max $5). Failed ACH transfers due to insufficient funds may result in processing delays or additional bank fees.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why can't I see the ACH payment option in my Add Balance modal?

ACH direct debit is only visible when three conditions are met: (1) Your agency is US-based, (2) you're accessing the agency-level wallet (not a location wallet), and (3) your deposit amount is at least $1,000. If you're in a location account or entering less than $1,000, only the card payment option will appear.

Q: How long does it take for ACH deposits to show in my wallet?

ACH transfers typically take 3–10 business days to settle. The exact timing depends on your bank's processing schedule and the ACH clearing network. You can track the transaction status in your Billing Dashboard under Wallet & Transactions.

Q: What are the actual processing fees for ACH deposits?

ACH deposits are charged 0.8% of the transaction amount, with a maximum fee cap of $5 per transaction. This means deposits of $625 or more will always cost exactly $5, regardless of size. Compare this to card payments, which typically cost approximately 3% with no cap.

Q: Can I use ACH for urgent wallet top-ups?

No. ACH is designed for planned, high-value deposits where cost savings outweigh speed. If you need immediate funds availability, use the "Pay with credit/debit card" option, which processes instantly. Consider maintaining a buffer balance to avoid urgent top-up situations.

Q: Can my sub-accounts (locations) use ACH to fund their wallets?

No. ACH direct debit is available exclusively at the agency level. Location wallet top-ups can only be processed via credit or debit card. This restriction ensures proper financial oversight and reconciliation at the agency level.

Q: What happens if my ACH transfer fails?

Failed ACH transfers are typically caused by insufficient bank funds, closed accounts, or incorrect bank details. You'll receive a notification if your transfer fails. Check your bank account status and balance, then initiate a new transfer. Your bank may also charge a returned payment fee.

Q: Is there a maximum limit for ACH deposits?

HighLevel does not impose a maximum ACH deposit limit at the platform level. However, your bank may have daily or per-transaction ACH limits. Contact your bank to confirm their ACH debit authorization limits before attempting large deposits.

Q: Will my bank information be stored securely?

Yes. HighLevel uses secure, encrypted connections through certified payment processors to connect your bank account. Your bank credentials are never stored on HighLevel servers. Each ACH authorization follows banking industry security standards and requires your bank's multi-factor authentication.

title_en: How to Use Custom Values and Variables in Agent Studio
source_md:
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/OuXLMSHWvYY?&wmode=opaque)

Use Custom Values and built-in variable sources to make your Agent Studio workflows dynamic, reusable, and scalable. Instead of manually typing business details or contact information into every node, you can insert smart placeholders that automatically pull real data when your agent runs.

This guide explains how to use Account details, Contact data, real-time date and time, form submissions, and Custom Values inside your agents without duplication or manual updates.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Custom Values and Variables?](#What-Are-Custom-Values-and-Variables?)
  - [Key Benefits of Using Variables in Agent Studio](#Key-Benefits-of-Using-Variables-in-Agent-Studio)
  - [Custom Values](#Custom-Values)
  - [Account Variables](#Account-Variables)
  - [Right Now Variables](#Right-Now-Variables)
  - [Form Data Variables](#Form-Data-Variables)
  - [Contact Variables](#Contact-Variables)
  - [Contact vs Runtime Variables](#Contact-vs-Runtime-Variables)
  - [How To Set Up Custom Values and Variables](#How-To-Set-Up-Custom-Values-and-Variables)
  - [Frequently Asked Question](#Frequently-Asked-Question)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Custom Values and Variables?**

Custom Values and Variables allow you to insert real information into your agent automatically. A variable is a placeholder written inside double curly braces, like {{contact.first\_name}}, which is replaced with real data when the agent runs.

For example:

**Hi {{contact.first\_name}}**

If the contact’s name is John, the message becomes: **Hi John**.

You can use variables anywhere you type text inside Agent Studio, including AI Agent prompts, Text Generation nodes, tool inputs, message cards, and conditional logic fields. Simply click the dropdown arrow in the text field to insert a variable or type it manually using {{ }}.

Agent Studio includes five built-in variable categories:

- Account
- Custom Values
- Right Now
- Form Data
- Contact

Each category pulls information from a different part of your system.

---

## **Key Benefits of Using Variables in Agent Studio**

Using variables helps you build dynamic and reusable agents.

- **Build once, use everywhere:**One agent template can work across multiple locations automatically.

- **No manual updates:**If a phone number or address changes, it updates everywhere instantly.

- **Automatic personalization:**Pull contact names and CRM data into conversations without extra work.

- **Real-time awareness:**Insert today’s date or current time automatically.

- **Safe execution:**If a variable has no value, it returns blank instead of breaking your agent.

---

## **Custom Values**

Custom Values are reusable key–value pairs you define in:

**Settings → Custom Values**

You create them once and use them anywhere.

**Example:**

**Key:**support\_email

**Value:**support@yourcompany.com

**Then inside your agent:**For help, email {{custom\_values.support\_email}}

If you update the value later, it automatically updates everywhere the variable is used.

---

**Update Custom Values from the AI Agent Action**

Workflows that use the **AI Agent** action can update custom values directly with the **Update Custom Value** tool. This allows the agent to write context-based values during execution instead of relying only on fixed workflow branches.

For full setup steps, refer to the [AI Agent workflow action](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007600) article.

---

## **Account Variables**

Account variables pull business information from your Location settings.

Use these when your agent needs to reference:

- Business name
- Phone number
- Address
- Website
- Logo URL

**Example:**Welcome to {{account.name}}. Call us at {{account.primary\_phone}}.

These values pull directly from your Location settings.

---

## **Right Now Variables**

Right Now variables insert live date and time information.

Examples include:

- Today’s full date
- Current time
- Day of the week
- Month or year

**Example:**Today is {{right\_now.date}}.

The system automatically inserts the correct date based on the location’s timezone.

---

## **Form Data Variables**

Form Data variables are available when your agent is triggered by a **Form Submitted** event.

Each form field becomes available as a variable.

**Example:** If your form has a field called “service\_type”, you can use: You selected {{form.service\_type}}

```
Important: Form variables only populate when the agent is triggered by a form submission.
```

---

## **Contact Variables**

Contact variables pull information directly from the CRM record. They allow standard as well as custom fields for deep personalization.

**Examples:**

- {{contact.first\_name}}
- {{contact.last\_name}}
- {{contact.email}}
- Custom contact fields

If the contact record updates, the next time the agent runs it will use the updated information.

---

## **Contact vs Runtime Variables**

- Contact variables pull saved CRM data.

- Runtime variables store temporary information collected during the current conversation.

- If the information already exists in the contact record before the conversation starts, use Contact variables.

- If the value is collected during the conversation, use Runtime variables.

---

## **How To Set Up Custom Values and Variables**

Follow these steps to start using variables.

#### **Step 1:** Create Custom Values

1. Go to **Settings** → **Custom Values** and select **Add Custom Value**
2. Enter a Name and Value then click **Create**

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155066195846/original/UcquCJLbh_kjtNn829WXLxBUD765leQiTA.gif?1772634838)**

#### **Step 2:**Open Agent Studio

Go to **AI Agents → Agent Studio** and open an existing agent or create a new one

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155074615036/original/0R71MpiOCz7VLaOAuNOBP1jMdWsI_KVKkQ.png?1782488945)

#### **Step 3:** Insert a Variable

### 1. Click inside any prompt or message field 2. Click the dropdown arrow in the field OR type {{ manually 3. Choose a category: - Account - Custom Values - Right Now - Form Data - Contact 4. Click a variable to insert it

```
Note: Some nodes, such as API Call steps, generate runtime variables based on their output. These variables can be reused in later steps by selecting them from the variable picker.
```

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155066197202/original/VQqhp9eIAz5W_LF314FtD0LW78jD23JeBw.png?1772635503)

#### **Step 4:**Save and Test

### 1. Click **Save** 2. Click **Test** 3. Run a sample conversation 4. Confirm variables resolve correctly

If a value appears blank, verify that the corresponding data exists in the CRM or Location settings.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155074615546/original/6A9eTQdsXH4xl_J1PAmcQZwR_Sv6MLnxUA.png?1782489324)

#### **Step 5:** Publish

Once everything works correctly, promote the agent to Production.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155074615652/original/_xaRKs-PSMkGjmOep9rWlMG0G58-dgIQnA.png?1782489421)

---

## **Frequently Asked Question**

**Q: What happens if a Custom Value is deleted?**

It returns an empty value instead of causing an error.

**Q: Can I reference Opportunity or Task fields?**

Currently supported sources are Account, Custom Values, Right Now, Form Data, and Contact.

**Q: What Happens If a Variable Has No Value?**

If a variable is missing or empty, the system returns a blank value. It does not cause an error or stop the agent from running. This ensures safe and reliable execution.

**Q: Do Right Now variables respect timezone?**

Yes. They use the sub-account’s timezone.

**Q: Can Form Data variables be used anywhere?**

They populate only when triggered by a Form Submitted event.

**Q: Are variable placeholders case-sensitive?**

Yes. Use the exact key names shown in the variable picker.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Use the AI Agent Studio in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006058)
- [How to use Custom Values](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001161575)
- [How to Set Up Agent Studio Triggers for Real-Time Starts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007310)

title_en: From 'Just Browsing' to 'Book Me Now': Your Salon Lead Gen Funnel That Fills Your Calendar
source_md:
## **Why This Funnel Works for Salons**

Your dream clients are already online — scrolling through Instagram, Googling “facial near me,” and clicking on promos. But without the right follow-through, most of them never take the next step. They like your posts, maybe tap your story, maybe even click the link in bio... and then disappear.

That’s where your **Lead Generation Funnel** comes in. It’s not just a landing page. It’s a guided experience — one that turns interest into action, and clicks into confirmed appointments.

This guide will walk you through building a high-converting funnel that doesn’t just look good — it works.

We’re not just setting up forms. We’re building your **client magnet machine.**

---

## **Understanding the Structure of a High-Converting Salon Funnel**

Every salon lead funnel should follow this sequence:

1. **Landing Page** — A visually compelling, on-brand page that clearly communicates your offer
2. **Lead Capture Form** — A short form where clients drop their name and number
3. **Thank You Page** — A confirmation page that tells them what to do next
4. **Automated Follow-Up** — Texts or emails that remind and encourage them to book
5. **Tracking + Retargeting (Optional but powerful)** — Useful for ad campaigns later on

Each part plays a specific role — together, they move someone from “I’m curious” to “I’m booking now.”

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Why This Funnel Works for Salons](#Why-This-Funnel-Works-for-Salons)
- [Understanding the Structure of a High-Converting Salon Funnel](#Understanding-the-Structure-of-a-High-Converting-Salon-Funnel)
- [Step 1: Craft an Offer That Feels Like a Steal](#Step-1%3A-Craft-an-Offer-That-Feels-Like-a-Steal)
- [Step 2: Build a Simple, Beautiful Landing Page in GHL](#Step-2%3A-Build-a-Simple,-Beautiful-Landing-Page-in-GHL)
- [Step 3: Add a Short, Effective Lead Capture Form](#Step-3%3A-Add-a-Short,-Effective-Lead-Capture-Form)
- [Step 4: Guide Them with a Thank You Page](#Step-4%3A-Guide-Them-with-a-Thank-You-Page)
- [Step 5: Automate the Follow-Up (So You Never Drop a Lead Again)](#Step-5%3A-Automate-the-Follow-Up-(So-You-Never-Drop-a-Lead-Again))
- [Step 6: Track Every Lead with a Pipeline](#Step-6%3A-Track-Every-Lead-with-a-Pipeline)
- [Step 7: (Optional) Add Facebook Pixel and Run Retargeting Ads](#Step-7%3A-(Optional)-Add-Facebook-Pixel-and-Run-Retargeting-Ads)
- [Final Words: Your Funnel Is Your Front Door](#Final-Words%3A-Your-Funnel-Is-Your-Front-Door%E2%80%8B)

---

## **Step 1: Craft an Offer That Feels Like a Steal**

This is the first and most important piece. If the offer doesn’t feel exciting or exclusive, people won’t fill out the form — no matter how pretty the page looks.

Think about what first-time clients care about: trust, results, and feeling special. Then craft your offer to speak to that.

**Examples of irresistible salon offers:**

- “First-time facial: Just $50 for your full glow-up experience”
- “Free 15-minute consultation + scalp check with any hair service”
- “Bridal trial offer: 10% off your wedding-day package when you book now”
- “Book any full-face cleanup and get brow threading free”

Don’t worry about giving everything away. The point here is to get them in the door. A small intro offer can easily lead to bigger bookings — full facials, treatments, bridal packages, and recurring visits.

[**How to Build a Funnel in GHL**](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005057-getting-started-launch-a-funnel)

---

## **Step 2: Build a Simple, Beautiful Landing Page in GHL**

Now that you’ve got your offer, it’s time to create the page that promotes it. This is your salon’s digital storefront for that offer — it needs to be clear, welcoming, and easy to navigate.

Using GHL’s drag-and-drop builder, you can design your own page without writing a single line of code.

**What your landing page should include:**

- A **strong headline** that states the offer clearly
- 2 to 3 short bullet points explaining the benefits ("Get glowing skin, save time with online booking, experience personalized beauty care")
- One or two testimonials or transformation photos
- A **form** to collect the lead’s information
- A big, bold **call-to-action button** that says “Claim This Offer” or “Book Now”

Keep it short. The goal is not to explain your entire service menu — it’s to get them to sign up.

**[How to have different websites for desktop and phone](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001161151-how-to-have-different-websites-for-desktop-and-phone)**

---

## **Step 3: Add a Short, Effective Lead Capture Form**

This is the form someone fills out on your landing page. It tells you who’s interested — and gives you a way to follow up.

**Form fields to include:**

- First Name (so you can personalize messages)
- Phone Number (for SMS reminders)
- Email (optional but useful for confirmations)
- A dropdown for service of interest (optional)

Keep the form short. Too many fields can scare people off. Your goal is to get the minimum amount of info needed to follow up.

Once your form is ready, embed it into your funnel.

**[Form Builder Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000980307-two-step-order-form-step-1-)**

---

## **Step 4: Guide Them with a Thank You Page**

The thank-you page is more than just a “you’re done” message. It’s your chance to move them toward actually booking.

Here’s what your thank-you page should do:

- Confirm that you received their submission
- Let them know what to expect next (“We’ll text you shortly with your booking link.”)
- Offer an immediate action — like scheduling now
- Optionally, include a short intro video of you or your team welcoming them

Also a great place to include:

- Social media links ("Follow us on Instagram for beauty inspo")
- A referral bonus (“Tag us after your visit and get $10 off next time”)

**[How to add CTA to your webpage](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000980316-click-to-call-click-to-text-and-click-to-email-links-buttons)**

---

## **Step 5: Automate the Follow-Up (So You Never Drop a Lead Again)**

Now that someone has submitted the form, your system needs to do the heavy lifting.

Set up an automated workflow that sends:

- **Immediate SMS**: “Hey [Name], thanks for claiming your offer! Tap here to book your glow-up: [booking link]”
- **Follow-up email**: Share a bit more about your salon, your team, or the experience
- **Reminder text** (after 48 hours): “Still interested in booking your [service]? Slots are filling up — book now.”

All of this can be built in GHL’s **Workflow Builder** — and once it’s set, it runs automatically.

**[Getting started with Workflows](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002288-getting-started-with-workflows)**

---

## **Step 6: Track Every Lead with a Pipeline**

Your funnel is generating leads — now it’s time to track them.

Using GHL’s **Opportunities Pipeline**, you can visually move each lead across stages like:

- New Lead
- Contacted
- Booking Pending
- Appointment Confirmed
- Won Client

You can also add **tags** like:

- “Facial $50”
- “Hair Consult – May”
- “Bridal Trial – Hot Lead”

This helps you stay organized and know exactly who’s ready to book — and who needs a little nudge.  
  
**[Step-by-Step Guide: Creating Opportunities](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001999-step-by-step-guide-creating-opportunities)**

---

## **Step 7: (Optional) Add Facebook Pixel and Run Retargeting Ads**

If you plan to run paid ads — or already are — install your **Meta Pixel** now.

It lets you retarget people who visited your landing page but didn’t fill the form.

Example: someone clicks your Instagram ad, reads your offer, then closes the tab. Two days later, they see a new ad saying: “Still thinking about glowing skin? Claim your $50 facial today.”

---

## **Final Words: Your Funnel Is Your Front Door**

If your salon’s Instagram and website are the showcase windows, this funnel is your **front door**.

You don’t need dozens of ads or offers. Just one powerful, well-executed funnel can bring a steady stream of leads — and your systems can take care of the rest.

Now, you’re not waiting for leads to message you. You’re guiding them to book.

Ready to grow? **[Sign up with HighLevel](https://www.gohighlevel.com/?utm_source=seo&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=beautysalon&utm_term=beautysalon&utm_content=playbook)**

source_md:
Kickstart your content strategy with **Blogs in**HighLevel. This guide walks you through creating your blog, writing posts, adding authors and categories, placing the Blog Post List on a page, and setting essential SEO so your articles can be discovered.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Blogs in HighLevel?](#What-is-Blogs-in-HighLevel?)
- [Key Benefits of Blogs in HighLevel](#Key-Benefits-of-Blogs-in-HighLevel%C2%A0)

---

# **What is Blogs in HighLevel?**

HighLevel Blogs is a built‑in publishing system for writing and organizing articles on your website or funnels. It lets you manage authors, categories, SEO, and design so you can publish consistently and route traffic to the right pages.

---

## **Key Benefits of Blogs in HighLevel**

- **Centralized publishing**: Manage all posts, authors, categories, and SEO in one place.
- **Flexible placement**: Show posts on any website page or funnel step using the Blog Post List element.
- **Built‑in SEO fields**: Set slugs, meta data, and canonical URLs to improve discoverability.
- **Design options**: Choose Standard or Compact layouts for your list and post views.
- **Scalable workflows**: Draft, schedule, publish, or import in bulk as your library grows.

---

## **How to Create a Blog in HighLevel**

If you're new to blogging or want to start your own blog but don't know where to begin, follow the steps to get started:

### **Step 1:**Create your Blog Site(container)

1. Go to **Sites.**
2. Click on**Blogs**
3. Click on **Create Blog**. Create from scratch or choose from template.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064779424/original/OiYF3mABKqw7rZqW5H23dRkDcSvWob6htg.jpeg?1770900245)

### **Step 2:**Add Blog Site Details

1. Add **Blog****Site****Title**. (This is what appears in a browser tab title barand search results)
2. **Select** or **Add**/**Edit****Domain**. (Optional you can connect a domain later in Blog Settings.)
3. **Domain management:** You can connect a domain at creation time or later from Blog Settings. If you need to switch domains, use Remove Domain in Blog Settings and then connect the new domain.
4. Add **Slug**.
5. Add a **Blog Meta Description**. (Optional but recommended)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064779485/original/M-l1QTgtlbe4xtiEOCEf57_wpanMIKzu1A.jpeg?1770900284)

### **Step 3:**Create Blog Post

1. Go to **Sites → Blogs.**
2. **Click on the Blog Site** you created from the **list** or any other existing blog site you want to add the blog post to.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/W1ZseR5HZIB5gqCKFqVA+/GIF+Recording+2026-02-12+at+6.22.19+PM.gif)
3. Click on **New Post**.
4. Click **+ New Post**to create a**blog post from scratch**. You can also [**Import Blog Posts from URL**](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004034) or [**Import Blog Posts from CSV**](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006464).
5. To create a blog post from scratch or edit one, check out our article on [**Creating Blog Posts**](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002450).  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/lauN1KBkpiMjO4w8pQju+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-12+at+6.23.44+PM.png)

### **Step 4:** Add Blog Post Details

1. Once you are done adding and formatting content of the blog post in the editor, click on **Continue**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/ODj6plhHTcGJP049Rix9+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-12+at+6.33.01+PM.png)
2. Add blog post **URL****S****lug**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/2qSl2zO7wamgKp1EYRyN+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-12+at+6.38.18+PM.png)
3. **Select** or **Create****Category** and **Author**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/TRJGa96erSfwYce2526S+/GIF+Recording+2026-02-12+at+6.40.37+PM.gif)
4. Edit **[Canonical Link](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002451)** or keep as it is.
5. Add **Keywords**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/yIPdQ9TzuhrBXv0OwOUn+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-12+at+6.43.37+PM.png)

### **Step 5:** Add SEO Details

1. Add **SEO****Title.**
2. Add **Post****Description**.
3. Add **Cover****Image** and it's **Alt Text**.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/JAMVKS0xLVx9C9PIGEAX+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-12+at+6.47.35+PM.png)

### **Step 6:** Publish Blog Post

1. You can keep the post in **Draft** to make further edits at a later time.
2. You can **Publish** the post immediately or **Schedule** it for a future time.

```
Note: To add a blog to a Funnel or Website, checkout our detailed guide.
```

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/NUDN2nvuLcneDX3T7hnt+/GIF+Recording+2026-02-12+at+6.51.58+PM.gif)

### **Step 7:**Customize Your Blog Layout

After creating and publishing your blog, you can customize how the blog and its posts appear to visitors.

Open the blog you want to edit, then use the available layout and styling options to customize the design.

You can:

- Select a blog layout.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082986124/original/yy_1Ip0DhAGiymLWm-I7WFYTfNLPDUh7Kw.jpeg?1791571049)
- Customize the appearance of blog cards.
- Adjust the styling of images, tags, headings, titles, descriptions, authors, and publish dates.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082986144/original/te_gTy2mSnTJRp2VkpOpf29WDSRPePg5UA.jpeg?1791571091)
- Manage the pages used for the blog home and individual blog posts.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082986151/original/hKVlhSTUcADGIh-vfQGM0kI9tysAT4GA0A.jpeg?1791571106)

Use these settings to keep the blog design consistent with the rest of your website and brand.

---

## **How to Update a Published or Draft Blog Post Details**

1. Go to the Blog Post and click on the **three** **dots** beside the post and click on **Update Post**.
2. Make edits to the blog post content in the editor.
3. To **make changes to blog post details** like **author**, **category**, **slug**, **SEO** etc, click in the **Update Settings** button.
4. Make necessary updates and click on **Publish**.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/WwE17o2QD3KECvtgabk0+/GIF+Recording+2026-02-12+at+6.58.41+PM.gif)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: How does the domain work with the blog?**

The Domain will be added to the Funnel or Website where the blog list element is added.

Blog URL formats:

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Domain | Slug of Blog Post | Final URL |
| abc.com | b/sample-now | abc.com/b/sample-now |
| abc.com/xyz | b/sample-now | abc.com/xyz/b/sample-now |
| blog.abc.com | b/sample-now | blog.abc.com/b/sample-now |

**Q: Can I have separate blog pages for each category?**

That is not currently supported. In the upcoming updates, we will allow users to create a funnel/website page based on a Category filter with the slug and SEO details.

**Q: Is it optional to add an Author, Category, or Keywords?**

URL Slug, Category, Author, Title and Post Description are mandatory.

**Q: Can I use custom values in a blog post?**

No, Custom Values are not supported in blog posts at the moment. You cannot use values like {{contact. name}} or {{custom\_values.xyz}} 

**Q: How to add Forms, Surveys, or Custom Code to my blog post?**

Forms or Surveys cannot be added to blog posts at the moment. The option to add custom code will be out soon.

**Q: What is the recommended image size for a blog post?**

We don't have a recommended size. However, the page width inside the blog post editor is 736 px.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Add Blog Post Element in Funnel(s) step or Website(s) page](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002776)
- [How to Customize Blog Design and Layout](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002449)
- [Blog and Blog Post Statuses](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002454)

title_en: Custom Object Templates: Pre-Built CRM Setup in One Click
source_md:
Custom Object Templates help you create industry-specific CRM structures in HighLevel without building everything from scratch. Each template includes ready-to-use Custom Objects, fields grouped into folders, and associations, making it easier to organize business data around real-world processes. Templates are available from the Template Library and can be previewed before they are applied.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Custom Object Templates?](#What-is-Custom-Object-Templates?)
- [Key Benefits of Custom Object Templates](#Key-Benefits-of-Custom-Object-Templates)
- [Agency Visibility Controls for Custom Object Templates](#Agency-Visibility-Controls-for-Custom-Object-Templates)
- [How To Setup Custom Object Templates](#How-To-Setup-Custom-Object-Templates)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Custom Object Templates?**

Custom Object Templates are pre-built configurations that help you quickly create Custom Objects for common industries and use cases. Instead of manually deciding which objects, fields, folders, and associations to create, you can start with a ready-made structure and adjust it to fit your business needs.

Custom Objects are used to track business data that does not fit neatly into standard CRM records like Contacts, Companies, or Opportunities. Templates make that setup faster by giving you a practical starting point based on common industry workflows.

Custom Object Templates are available in the Template Library alongside other template modules in HighLevel. Users can browse supported industries, preview template details, and apply a template when creating Custom Objects.

---

## **Key Benefits of Custom Object Templates**

Custom Object Templates help teams launch structured CRM setups faster while still allowing flexibility for industry-specific processes.

- **Faster Setup:**Create Custom Objects, fields, folders, and associations in one flow instead of building each part manually.
- **Industry Specific Starting Points:** Choose from templates designed for common industries such as Real Estate, Insurance, Automotive, SaaS, Events, Pets, and Home Services.
- **Easier Data Organization:** Use predefined fields and folders to keep related information grouped clearly.
- **Built In Relationship Mapping:** Templates can include associations so records can be connected across Companies, Opportunities, and Custom Objects.
- **Preview Before Applying**: Review the template’s objects, fields, associations, description, tags, and prerequisites before using it.
- **Agency Visibility Control:**Agency Admins can manage which template modules or categories are visible to sub-accounts through Template Library visibility settings.

---

## **Agency Visibility Controls for Custom Object Templates**

Agency visibility controls help agencies keep the Template Library focused for each sub-account. This is useful when an agency serves a specific niche and only wants clients or team members to see relevant template categories.

Agency Admins can manage Custom Object Template visibility using the existing Template Library visibility controls. 

These controls can be used to show or hide template access for specific sub-accounts or product areas. Hiding Template Library access restricts browsing or importing new templates, while assets already created from templates remain available for editing.

---

## **How To Setup Custom Object Templates**

Applying a Custom Object Template gives your account a ready-made object structure that can be used as a starting point for your CRM setup. Reviewing the template before applying it helps confirm the objects, fields, and associations match your business process.

To use a Custom Object Template:

1. Go to Settings in the sub-account.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070636537/original/sXcWd7eHIOiJoy8_znMI3EwAzEd2T5dmng.png?1777997853)
2. Select Objects in the left pane.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070636820/original/cJV3hneMHx-DSsJ8M7VFbvEIqaTW3l__lw.png?1777997897)
3. Click Add Custom Object to create a new custom object.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070636918/original/kmn_GITsAuxr05FWMymgktdzZXtkblrZvw.png?1777997966)
4. Choose Use a template to create objects using templates.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070636989/original/OXeI7mUsVwJK2eLeMtVuQRkUZLZQLHmu_w.png?1777998028)
5. Browse the available Custom Object Templates.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070637029/original/rU5U8NMIL0UICYNHFto_J7ElAcNokJBwZw.png?1777998092)
6. Select the template that matches your industry or use case.
7. Review the template preview, including objects, fields, associations, description, tags, and prerequisites.
8. Click "Import Objects" to apply or use the template.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070637228/original/jBrh_USg27JMXRjZuuyCyimWP3Wnr6F6jA.gif?1777998206)
9. Review the created Custom Objects and make any needed adjustments.

After the template is applied, review the created objects, fields, and associations to ensure they match your workflow. Custom Objects can be managed from the Objects area in Settings, and associations can be reviewed from the object’s association settings.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do Custom Object Templates create records automatically?**A: Custom Object Templates are designed to create the CRM structure, such as Custom Objects, fields, folders, and associations. They are not described as importing customer records or sample records in the current release note.

**Q: Can I edit a template after applying it?**A: You can manage Custom Objects from the Objects area in Settings. Review the created objects, fields, and associations after applying a template and adjust the setup as needed based on your business process.

**Q: Will applying a Custom Object Template overwrite my existing Custom Objects?**A: The release note does not state that templates overwrite existing Custom Objects. Review the template preview before applying and verify the created setup afterward.

**Q: Can Agency Admins hide Custom Object Templates from sub-accounts?**A: Yes. Custom Object Templates use the existing Template Library visibility controls, allowing Agency Admins to manage access for sub-accounts.

**Q: What happens if a template is hidden after it has already been used?**A: Existing assets created from templates remain available for editing even if browsing or importing new templates is later restricted.

**Q: Do Custom Object Templates include associations?**A: Yes. Templates can include associations, helping connect related records such as Companies, Opportunities, and Custom Objects.

**Q: Are workflows or sample data included with Custom Object Templates?**A: Not in the current release. Workflows and sample data are planned for a future phase based on the release note provided.

**Q: Can users create and save their own Custom Object Templates?**A: Not in the current release. User-contributed templates are planned for a future phase based on the release note provided.

**Q: Which industries are currently supported?**A: Current templates include Real Estate, Insurance, Automotive, SaaS, Events, Pets, and Home Services.
